articles.title: Bulacan residents wade through floods to protest flood-control corruption
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Around 500 residents, farmers and fisherfolk in Bulacan on Monday waded through floodwaters to protest corruption in “flood-control projects.” They are also opposing the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Around 500 residents, farmers and fisherfolk in Bulacan on Monday waded through floodwaters to protest corruption in “flood-control projects.”
They are also opposing the reclamation initiative that reportedly “worsened” the flooding in the province.

The flooding in Bulacan—known as one of the most flood-prone areas in the country—as well as in other provinces, is caused by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” which is being enhanced by Tropical Depression Pilandok.

Led by anti-corruption alliance Kilos Bulacan, members of fishers’ group Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya), farmers’ group Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP), and rural-based group Anakpawis marched along the City of Malolos to hold the protest this Monday.
Their action coincides with National Heroes’ Day.
According to KMP Chairperson Danilo Ramos, also a Malolos resident, the province’s residents “have long endured the repeated flooding caused by these useless, anomalous flood-control projects.”
“While corrupt officials and big corporations plunder the public funds and our environment, ordinary people suffer,” Ramos emphasized in a statement.
“We demand justice in the form of genuine mitigation measures, accountability, and appropriate compensation for this systematic disaster that caused unmeasurable losses,” he noted.

Meanwhile, Pamalakaya Vice Chairperson Ronnel Arambulo noted that the reclamation project New Manila International Airport (NMIA) in Barangay Taliptip, Bulakan, Bulacan, has led to “critical risks of flooding and subsidence, threatening its long-term viability.”
Pamalakaya cited a study by non-government organization Global Witness, which warns that “rising sea levels and storm surges could render the airport unusable within decades.”
The group also pointed out that the 2,500-hectare project displaced almost 1,000 fishing families in Barangay Taliptip and uprooted over 600 mangrove trees.

“The protest launched by residents, farmers and fishermen in Bulacan is timely. We once again call for justice and accountability for all those involved in the anomalous and botched flood control, as well as the widespread plunder of nature that is submerging communities,” Arambulo remarked.
Echoing these sentiments, Anakpawis Coordinator Glo Fernandez urged the Bulacan provincial government to heed their constituents’ call for an “immediate solution” against flooding.
“It has been more than a year since the anomaly in flood control broke out. But until now, many sectors remain vulnerable to flooding,” said Fernandez.
“Both politicians involved in the anomalous flood control and the big corporations that destroyed the environment must be held accountable,” he stressed. /apl

articles.title: Leila de Lima tells DENR to suspend relocation of mangroves
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Mamamayang Liberal partylist Rep. Leila de Lima has called for the suspension of earth-balling and relocation of mangroves until the Department of Environment and Natural…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Mamamayang Liberal partylist Rep. Leila de Lima has called for the suspension of earth-balling and relocation of mangroves until the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) comes up with a more comprehensive study on the matter.

During a recent House hearing tackling the 2027 budget of the DENR, De Lima asked about the status of the department’s memorandum dated Oct. 8, 2025 concerning the interim operational guidance and conditions on the earth-balling and relocation of mangroves in exceptional circumstances.
She questioned why the memorandum was issued despite the lack of scientific studies or even consultations.

“We understand that there is a Technical Working Group that was recently created regarding the earth-balling of mangroves. I am wondering why that Memorandum was issued at all, even before consultations, or even before the creation of TWG, or a scientific study. What exactly is the survival rate?” De Lima asked.
“All of these things should have been confirmed or verified first before allowing the issuance of this Memorandum,” she further pointed out.
According to De Lima, what was supposed to be an “interim operational guidance” has seemed like a “de facto policy” allowing the earth-balling of mangroves for flagship infrastructure.

In response, DENR Sec. Juan Miguel Cuna said the department deemed it appropriate at the time—under sustainable development that they are following—to issue interim guidelines through a memorandum specifying certain methods or guidelines to be followed.

He also claimed that the DENR was in consultation with the Ecosystem Research and Development Bureau, the Biodiversity Management Bureau and the Forest Management Bureau, which are the agencies they requested to come up with a study particularly on the mangroves’ survival rate.
“We’re encouraged by the initial results that have been sent to us already, but for us to be able to really extensively complete the study, we are targeting December of this year,” he said.
With this, De Lima told the DENR that it must be more direct about the study’s findings especially if the mangroves’ survival rate in the process is extremely low.
She then urged the DENR to “first suspend the implementation, if not do away with the memorandum altogether.”
Cuna then committed to evaluate the matter in light of ongoing developments.

De Lima in July 2026 filed House Resolution No. 1206 seeking to conduct an inquiry into the DENR Memorandum as this directly conflicts with the Philippines’ internationally-endorsed commitments and undermines the country’s credibility and standing as a steward of global mangrove conservation.

De Lima also filed House Bill No. 8353 seeking to require the establishment of coastal greenbelt zones, which are mangroves and beach forests stretching to at least 100 meters in width, designed to prevent coastal erosion.
The measure also specifically defines the country’s policy goals and objectives for the management of mangrove resources in the country.

“The lack of a national policy on mangroves poses a great challenge and has caused existing mangrove protection and rehabilitation efforts to remain ineffective and unsuccessful,” said De Lima in filing the bill.
“We must urgently implement a comprehensive mechanism to shield coastal communities, protect habitats, and set the stage for rebuilding our fisheries and achieving food security,” she added. /mr

articles.title: Lacson: P3.7B ‘wasted’ on ‘illegal’ Taguig reclamation projects
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — At least P3.713 billion in public funds may have been wasted on flood control and multipurpose projects in reclamation areas facing Laguna de Bay in Taguig City, Sen. Panfilo…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — At least P3.713 billion in public funds may have been wasted on flood control and multipurpose projects in reclamation areas facing Laguna de Bay in Taguig City, Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said Monday.

“WASTED PUBLIC FUNDS DUE TO MISUSE: Based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH Flood Control and Multi-Purpose Projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore Reclamation Areas in Taguig City has so far reached P3.713 billion,” Lacson said in a post on X.

According to Lacson, “These do not include other anomalous Slope Protection and Flood Mitigation projects along Taguig River involving double appropriations and ‘ghost’ projects using recycled photographs in different ‘completed’ projects, for billing purposes.”
Lacson said five contractors with projects totaling P2.372 billion were:

items: Dahl Construction – P858.22 million covering five solo projects worth P571.5 million and four joint ventures totaling P286.7 million
J.C. Uyecio – P483.1 million for four joint ventures
Toughbuilt – P434.2 million covering three solo projects
Topnotch – P329.9 million covering two joint ventures with Core Check and one with Beam Team
GR Fervidal – P266.6 million covering five solo multi-purpose building projects

blocks.text: All five of GR Fervidal’s multipurpose building projects were suspended over a “revision of plans” involving a soil re-investigation, Lacson said.

The disclosure came as Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon confirmed on Sunday that his agency had issued cease-and-desist orders against reclamation projects in Taguig City, following a directive from the Office of the President coursed through the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA).

Lacson earlier said PRA officials had told him that all unpermitted reclaimed areas in Taguig, whether owned by the city government or private individuals, could be subject to forfeiture in favor of the national government.

He also said on Saturday that at least four parcels of reclaimed land in Taguig had been covered by “fraudulently” issued titles, while four other parcels had no plotted title lots in the Land Registration Authority’s digital records.
Cayetano: Gov’t could benefit
Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano, meanwhile, said that the government stands to gain if the allegations involving the questioned land titles are proven true.

“May isang nasa dyaryo kahapon na [nagsabi na may] 181,000 square meters o 18 hectares daw na ‘illegally titled.’ Sa isang banda po, nagho-hope din kami na totoo iyon. Bakit? Kasi kung totoong illegal iyon, sa gobyerno iyon [mapupunta], eh di may 18 hectares tayo ngayon para sa gobyerno,” Cayetano said while speaking at a church anniversary event on Sunday.

(Yesterday, there was something in the newspaper saying that there is a 181,000-square-meter, or 18-hectare, property that was supposedly ‘illegally titled.’ On one hand, we are also hoping that’s true. Why? Because if it is indeed illegal, it would go to the government. Then we would have 18 hectares now for the government.)
Cayetano was referring to one of the parcels identified by Lacson, a 181,077-square-meter property whose title allegedly originated from a homestead patent.
Cayetano also welcomed the scrutiny of the land titles, saying Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano had long wanted them examined.
Cayetano, however, disputed allegations involving the Lakeshore Tent.

“Iyon ang pinapalabas na illegal reclamation at pinapalabas na kinakamkam ko rin daw po ‘yung iba para sa aking sarili. Pero ang blessing po ay marami kasing gumagamit at alam naman po na hindi amin iyon,” Cayetano added.

(That is being portrayed as illegal reclamation, and it is also being portrayed as though I am taking some of it for myself. But the blessing is that many people are using it, and they know that it does not belong to us)

Lacson’s probe into infrastructure projects in Taguig, the political bailiwick of the Cayetanos, was triggered by a verbal feud between the senators. Cayetano has denied allegations of ghost projects and challenged Lacson to substantiate his claims.
The Inquirer also sought Cayetano’s comment on Lacson’s latest pronouncements but has yet to receive a response as of posting time. /mr

articles.title: Yellow rainfall warning up over 4 Luzon provinces
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The state weather bureau raised a yellow rainfall warning over four Luzon provinces on Monday morning due to the continuous effect of the southwest monsoon, locally known as…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The state weather bureau raised a yellow rainfall warning over four Luzon provinces on Monday morning due to the continuous effect of the southwest monsoon, locally known as “habagat,” which is being enhanced by Tropical Depression Pilandok.

Based on the 11 a.m. advisory of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), the yellow warning level, which covers rainfall of 7.5 to 15 millimeters, was raised over the following areas:

items: Zambales
Tarlac (San Clemente, Camiling, Mayantoc, San Jose, Capas, Bamban, Santa Ignacia)
Pampanga (Porac, Floridablanca)
Bataan (Dinalupihan)

blocks.text: Pagasa warned that flooding is possible in areas under the yellow rainfall, particularly in places prone to flooding.
Meanwhile, Bulacan is forecast to experience light to moderate rains within the next three hours.
Pagasa also said the habagat is expected to bring light to moderate with occasional heavy rains over the following areas, which may persist within the next three hours and may affect nearby areas:

items: Nueva Ecija (Cabiao, San Antonio, San Isidro, Aliaga, Bongabon, Cabanatuan, Gabaldon, General Mamerto Natividad, Guimba, Jaen, Laur, Licab, Llanera, Nampicuan, Palayan, Pantabangan, Penaranda, Quezon, Rizal, San Jose, San Leonardo, Santa Rosa, Santo Domingo, Science City of Muñoz, Talavera, Zaragoza, Carranglan, Cuyapo, Lupao, Talugtug)
Tarlac (Concepcion, Anao, La Paz, Pura, Ramos, Victoria, Tarlac City, Gerona, Paniqui, San Manuel, Moncada)
Pampanga (Arayat, Bacolor, San Fernando, Magalang, Mexico, Santa Ana, Angeles, Mabalacat, Guagua, Santa Rita)
Bataan (Morong, Bagac, Mariveles)

blocks.text: Pagasa said in a separate 11 a.m. weather bulletin that Tropical Depression Pilandok has maintained its strength, carrying a maximum sustained wind speed of 55 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gustiness of up to 70 kph.
Pilandok was last located 1,160 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon and is moving almost stationary.
The tropical depression is expected to exit the Philippine area of responsibility by Wednesday afternoon or evening. /dp

articles.title: Pangasinan’s San Roque Dam nears spilling level
articles.summary: CALASIAO, Pangasinan – The San Roque multi-purpose dam’s elevation has almost reached its mandatory spilling level of 280 meters above sea level as of 8 am of Monday (Aug. 31). The dam’s reservoir…

blocks.text: CALASIAO, Pangasinan – The San Roque multi-purpose dam’s elevation has almost reached its mandatory spilling level of 280 meters above sea level as of 8 am of Monday (Aug. 31).

The dam’s reservoir elevation rose by 4.76 meters in 24 hours, or from 275.09 meters as of 8 am on Sunday (Aug. 30) to 279.85 meters as of 8 am on Monday, records of the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration showed.
No spillway gate is open as of presstime, although the dam’s low-level output continues to release 150-169 cubic meters per second of water.
Tommy Valdez, San Roque Power Corporation’s senior vice president for community affairs, said the company is waiting for instruction from the National Power Corporation if the gates would be opened.
The NPC officials are at the SRPC office at of presstime to study the situation, he said.
Most barangays in Bayambang town in central Pangasinan, where Agno River joins Tarlac River, are already under heavy flooding. /mr

articles.title: 2 CDO cops axed for alleged acts of lasciviousness
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Two police officers have been sacked from their posts for alleged acts of lasciviousness against female criminology student-interns here, an official said Monday. The…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Two police officers have been sacked from their posts for alleged acts of lasciviousness against female criminology student-interns here, an official said Monday.
The information comes from Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., Police Regional Office (PRO)–10 director.

He said that the two officers of the Cagayan de Oro City Police Office’s (COCPO) Station 7 — a police captain and a corporal — have been placed under restrictive custody at the Regional Personnel Holding and Accounting Unit (RPHAU) following the alleged incident.

“Misconduct will not be tolerated. All PNP (Philippine National Police) personnel are expected to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, integrity and respect for the dignity and welfare of every person,” Babagay said in a statement.
He directed the Regional Investigation and Detection Management Division (RIDMD) to conduct a pre-charge evaluation.
On the other hand, COCPO Director Col. Dexter Paje has been instructed to assist the alleged victims through the Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) in filing criminal complaints.
Last Aug. 25, COCPO said that it formed an investigation team from its Criminal Investigation and Detection Management Unit (CIDMU) and WCPD.
The probe came after a local higher education institution formally requested the immediate withdrawal of its student-trainees from their field assignments.
On Monday, PRO-10 confirmed that two COCPO personnel allegedly committed acts of lasciviousness against two female interns inside Police Station 7 on Aug. 8. /apl

articles.title: Iceland votes ‘No’ to resuming EU talks
articles.summary: REYKJAVIK, Iceland — Iceland voted ‘No’ to resuming membership negotiations with the European Union, referendum results showed Sunday, dealing a blow to Brussels which had been keen…

blocks.text: REYKJAVIK, Iceland — Iceland voted ‘No’ to resuming membership negotiations with the European Union, referendum results showed Sunday, dealing a blow to Brussels which had been keen to welcome a new wealthy member.
Almost 53 percent of Icelanders rejected the resumption of EU entry talks suspended 13 years ago, while some 47 percent voted in favour in Saturday’s referendum.
Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir, who favoured a ‘Yes,’ stressed she didn’t “see this as a setback”.
“I see this as a victory for democracy,” she told reporters, pointing to voter turnout of over 80 percent.
“I want to make it absolutely clear, this government is not going forward with the accession talks this term.”

This means any discussions of Icelandic accession are frozen at least until 2028 — an apparent disappointment to Brussels, which had appeared willing to compromise on thorny issues to facilitate Iceland’s accession.
EU chief Antonio Costa nonetheless told Frostadottir the bloc “fully respects the democratic choice” made by voters, a spokesperson said.
“Iceland remains one of the EU’s closest and most trusted partners,” said the spokesperson.
Far-right, eurosceptic leaders in Britain and France hailed the result.

“At a time when some are pushing for greater federalism and the transfer of sovereignty to the European Commission, this vote reminds us that another Europe is possible, a Europe of free, sovereign nations cooperating voluntarily on matters of common interest,” France’s Marine Le Pen wrote on X.
“Congratulations to Iceland on voting to keep their independence,” Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, who was one of the faces of Britain’s Brexit, wrote on the same platform.
Iceland, a country of just under 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of the 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy.
Membership talks were then suspended in 2013 when a eurosceptic government came to power.
The island is, however, already closely linked to the EU as a member of the European Economic Area and the free-movement Schengen zone, ties which will remain unchanged.
The referendum result was non-binding but the government had vowed to respect it.
High turnout

Debates ahead of the vote had mainly revolved around domestic and economic issues, though the war in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump’s ambitions for neighbouring Greenland — which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions — also featured.

The campaign had “lifted discussions about the EU, about Iceland’s place in the world, about our general geopolitical situation and status, to a higher level”, Frostadottir said after casting her ballot Saturday.
Political analysts had said it was unlikely the government would resign in the event of a ‘No’ victory, though it could emerge weakened by the rejection.
According to RUV, voter turnout was 82.5 percent, the highest participation in any Icelandic vote since April 2009 parliamentary elections during its crippling financial crisis.
The campaign divided Icelanders.
“It’s hard to grasp that it’s a ‘No’,” 37-year-old artist Elisabet Anna Kristjansdottir told AFP.
“It’s quite sad that the Icelandic people don’t even want to see the possibilities of joining the EU.”
Anna Maria Bogadottir said meanwhile she was “really happy”, but acknowledged it would now “be a challenge to unite 50 percent on each side.”
Wooing from Brussels

A ‘Yes’ vote would have given the government a mandate to resume negotiations with Brussels, including on the hotly contested issue of fishing — a pillar of Iceland’s economy and part of its national identity, and over which Reykjavik wants to retain exclusive control.
Any accession agreement would then have then been put to another referendum in Iceland.

The fisheries sector has been fiercely opposed to joining the bloc — 90 percent of companies in the industry are against the idea — and the EU had tried to woo it with a conciliatory approach ahead of the vote.
EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos had said Brussels and EU member states would be willing to “find creative solutions” to Iceland’s “unique specificities on fisheries and agriculture”.
An EU source in Brussels told AFP: “I don’t think anyone (in the EU) wants to block an accession over a question of fish.”

Brussels had hoped to be able to present wealthy Iceland as an example of positive enlargement that could also make it more palatable for member states to agree to take in poorer countries like Montenegro.
It would also have enabled it to enlarge its presence in the strategic Arctic region, and perhaps helped change some minds in ultra-wealthy non-EU member Norway. /dl

articles.title: 5 days after Nepal-Tibet flood, missing Filipino doctor's family still waits
articles.summary: Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo remains missing following the catastrophic Nepal floods.

blocks.text: Undated photo showing Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo, who remains missing after the flash flood in Nepal. Meanwhile, people look at photographs of missing persons in the aftermath of flash floods, outside a hospital in Kathmandu on Aug. 30, 2026.
Chiara Manalo via FB; AFP / Manan Vatsyayana

MANILA, Philippines — The family of Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo is appealing for help in finding him after he went missing following the catastrophic flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border last week.
In an August 28 Facebook post, Manalo's sister Chiara said the family last heard from him on August 25 at 1:21 p.m. Philippine time, a day before the Aug. 26 disaster.
"Filipino doctor, Juan Carlos Manalo, has been missing and out of contact since the flash flood at the Nepal border last August 26, 2026," the post read.

Chiara said her brother had been traveling with an Isha Foundation Kailashyatra pilgrimage group. His group's last known location was the immigration office at Gyirong, on the Tibetan side of the China-Nepal border.
Nepali tourism authorities have identified Manalo as the lone Filipino among foreign nationals still unaccounted for after the flood.

The Department of Foreign Affairs said Sunday night that it had yet to receive new information on Manalo's whereabouts. The Nepal Tourism Board first announced on August 27 the nationalities of the missing foreign nationals.
The Nepal Tourism Board said 289 foreign nationals had been rescued as of 6 p.m. Sunday, while 591 remained out of communication.
Anyone with information on Manalo's whereabouts may contact his family through the numbers provided in their public appeal:

items: Jose Rodrigo Manalo: +63 917 302 3077
Dinah Marie Manalo: +63 917 514 3465
Chiara Manalo: +63 917 791 7849

blocks.text: The August 26 flood devastated communities and tourism routes along the Nepal-China border. Nepal's disaster agency reported 781 deaths and nearly 3,000 people still missing as of Sunday evening.

articles.title: Marcos on National Heroes Day: Defending our territory a shared responsibility
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday urged Filipinos to take part in protecting national sovereignty and help shape a nation that stands firm against all forms of pressure.

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 12:17pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday urged Filipinos to take part in protecting national sovereignty and help shape a nation that stands firm against all forms of pressure.

In his speech during the commemoration of National Heroes Day at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City, the President honored the country’s modern-day heroes, including the fisherfolk, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), and Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR).
“Ipaglalaban natin ang ating mga karapatan sa paraang mapayapa, naaayon sa batas, at naaayon sa ating mga prinsipyo,” Marcos said.
(We will fight for our rights through ways that are peaceful, lawful, and consistent with our principles.)

“But defending our territory is a responsibility shared by the entire nation. It calls on each of us to understand our history, to know our rights, and to take part in protecting the national interests,” he added.

The President noted that this year marks a decade since the historic 2016 arbitral award affirmed the Philippines' maritime entitlements under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

He also recalled his recent State of the Nation Address, where he reaffirmed that the duty to the people “extends to protecting the country’s interests, upholding the rule of law, and securing the resources upon which our communities depend.”
Doing so, Marcos emphasized, begins by educating the youth on where the Philippines’ maritime rights come from and why they matter.
He said that disinformation must also be countered and responsible discourse should be encouraged across every platform available.
The President also said that fisherfolk need unconditional support as their continued presence in the country’s waters “strengthens our connection to our maritime territory.”

“Above all, we have a duty to uphold the integrity of our institutions—by demanding transparency, accountability, and a standard of service worthy of the Filipino people. Sapagkat ang tibay ng ating paninindigan bilang bansa ay nagsisimula sa lalim ng ating kaalaman at lakas ng ating pagkakabuklod-buklod bilang isang bayan,” Marcos said.
(Because our resolve as a nation begins with the depth of our knowledge and the strength of our unity.)

“Magkakaiba man ang ating pamamaraan, iisa ang mensahe ng mga ito: Ang Pilipinas ay karapat-dapat na ipaglaban. Ang bawat Pilipino ay karapat-dapat na paglingkuran. Ang ating soberanya ay karapat-dapat na ipagtanggol,” he added.
(Our methods may differ, but the message is the same: The Philippines is worth fighting for. Every Filipino is worth serving. Our sovereignty is worth defending.)

Marcos also called on the Filipinos to help shape a nation where everyone stands firm against all forms of pressures, where institutions serve with integrity, and where sovereignty remains secure for generations to come.
After the President delivered his speech, he paid tribute to his late father, former president Ferdinand Marcos Sr., who is also buried at the Libingan ng mga Bayani. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: PH, Brunei Darussalam sign MOU on strengthened judicial cooperation
articles.summary: The Philippines and Brunei Darussalam have formalized the agreement between the two countries to strengthen judicial cooperation in emerging, cross-border, and transnational legal issues. Areas of…

blocks.text: The Philippines and Brunei Darussalam have formalized the agreement between the two countries to strengthen judicial cooperation in emerging, cross-border, and transnational legal issues.

Areas of cooperation include the study of Shari’ah (religious and moral code of Islam), approaches to trafficking in persons, cybercrime and electronic evidence, and climate justice and environmental adjudication.

Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo and Brunei Darussalam Chief Justice Dato Seri Paduka Steven Chong led the ceremonial signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) at The Empire Brunei last August 30.

With Gesmundo were Philippine Judicial Academy (PHILJA) Chancellor and retired Associate Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos, PHILJA Vice Chancellor Sedfrey M. Candelaria, and PHILJA Academic Affairs Office Chief Emerito I. Enginco.

A briefer issued by the Supreme Court’s (SC) Office of the Spokesperson stated that the MOU designates PHILJA and Brunei’s Judicial Education and Training Unit as the implementing institutions for the partnership.

Under the agreement, the two judiciaries will cooperate in the exchange of expertise, knowledge, and best practices in judicial education, including curriculum design, teaching methods, and evaluation systems.
They will also organize and participate in workshops, seminars, conferences, study visits, and other capacity-building programs for judges, judicial officers, and court personnel.

The partnership also covers the development and sharing of educational resources, such as publications, research, bench books, training modules, and other learning materials; the undertaking of joint initiatives on issues of mutual interest, particularly emerging challenges affecting judicial administration and adjudication; and the facilitation of professional exchanges and networking opportunities to strengthen institutional ties and mutual understanding.
In his message, Chief Justice Gesmundo said the MOU reflects the Philippine SC’s belief that the administration of justice is strengthened when judiciaries learn from one another.
He also said the MOU is “an affirmation of the enduring friendship between our two nations and of our commitment to judicial excellence, rule of law, and effective delivery of justice.”
He pointed out that the rapid pace of change requires judges and court personnel to engage in continuous learning and greater collaboration across jurisdictions.

He also said: “Our courts today operate in an increasingly interconnected world. Legal disputes and criminal activities no longer remain neatly within territorial boundaries. Technological advances have transformed the way evidence is created, preserved, and presented. Environmental and climate concerns increasingly find their way into courtrooms. Artificial intelligence is reshaping institutions and raising profound questions about fairness, accountability, and the ethical exercise of judicial authority.”
Gesmundo pointed out that the MOU’s greatest value lies in the stronger relationships it will foster between the two judiciaries.

He stressed: “I believe the deeper value of this initiative lies in the relationships it will cultivate among our judges, judicial officers, judicial educators, and court personnel. Through candid dialogue and the sharing of experiences, we gain not only new knowledge but also a deeper appreciation of the circumstances and perspectives that shape another judiciary. In this regard, judicial education becomes a bridge, not merely between institutions, but between people and legal traditions, as well.”
For his part, Chief Justice Chong described the MOU as a recognition that judicial education is strengthened through cooperation and the sharing of experiences among courts.

Chong said: “The MOU reflects a shared recognition that judicial education is not simply an internal matter for individual judiciaries. It is an endeavor in which we can learn from one another, benefit from one another’s experience, and work together to strengthen the administration of justice.”
He also acknowledged the Philippines’ contributions as co-chair of the Working Group on Judicial Education and Training under the Council of ASEAN Chief Justices (CACJ).
“That role reflects the Philippines’ commitment to strengthening judicial education not only within its own judiciary, but also as an area of regional cooperation,” he also said.
The signing of the MOU was a result of the discussions held during the recent Advanced Courses on the Role of International Law in Advancing ASEAN Judiciaries, hosted by the Philippines.

The program brought together more than 100 delegates from ASEAN member states, including Brunei Darussalam. During the event held last February, representatives of the Philippine and Brunei judiciaries explored ways to deepen institutional cooperation and create more opportunities for judges, court personnel, and judicial educators to learn from one another.

articles.title: Solon: Tax collection sharing formula unfair to coastal communities
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The budgeting formula on tax sharing between the national government and local units is disproportionately biased towards regions with vast land areas, Agusan del Norte Rep.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The budgeting formula on tax sharing between the national government and local units is disproportionately biased towards regions with vast land areas, Agusan del Norte Rep. Dale Corvera said on Monday.
In a statement, he said the National Tax Allotment (NTA) sharing formula “is not fair” to coastal communities, as 25 percent of the equation considers land mass for allocations.
“There is a big disconnect because the national government only factors in dry land area when computing their financial support to LGUs through the NTA,” Corvera said.

The NTA is based on national tax collections from 2024, or the third fiscal year preceding the current fiscal year, and 50 percent of the allotments for provinces, cities and municipalities is based on population, 25 percent on landmass and another 25 percent for equal sharing.
For barangays, 60 percent of earmarked shares is based on population and 40 percent on equal sharing.
“The current formula favors landlocked LGUs [that have] no municipal waters to take care of,” said Corvera.
The National Government earmarked P1.32-trillion in NTA in the proposed 2027 national budget as part of efforts to pass down governance duties to local units.

“Coastal LGUs do not seek a larger overall slice of the national budget, but rather fairness in computing their NTA shares to bridge the resource gap so that all communities have a fair chance at local economic growth,” Corvera said.

Under the allocation formula provided in Section 285 of Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code of 1991, municipalities will receive 34 percent of the total NTA, or P448.84 billion, while provinces and cities will each receive 23 percent, or P303.56 billion. Barangays will receive the remaining 20 percent, equivalent to P263.97 billion.

The 2027 NTA will come mainly from national tax collections: P990.68 billion from the Bureau of Internal Revenue and P329.09 billion from the Bureau of Customs, with the remainder from other certified collections. /mr

articles.title: Pilandok maintains strength over PH sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok has maintained its strength while moving almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, the state weather bureau reported…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok has maintained its strength while moving almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, the state weather bureau reported on Monday.

Based on the 11 a.m. weather bulletin from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), Pilandok—which was located 1,160 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon—still carries a maximum sustained wind speed of 55 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gustiness of up to 70 kph.
No tropical cyclone wind signal is currently hoisted in any part of the country.
According to Pagasa, Pilandok is forecast to move slowly northwestward or remain almost stationary for the next 36 hours before moving generally north-northwestward for the remaining forecast period.
The tropical depression is expected to exit the Philippine area of responsibility by Wednesday afternoon or evening.

“This tropical cyclone is less likely to make landfall over the country and will remain far from the Philippine landmass,” Pagasa said, but noted the forecast track may still be subject to change in the succeeding bulletins.

As for its strength, Pilandok is expected to intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday. It would then weaken into a tropical depression by Wednesday and “maintain its strength throughout the remainder of the forecast period.” /mr

articles.title: Countries gear up to create lunar standard time amid global race on Moon
articles.summary: Countries are gearing up to establish a unified lunar time standard, with a key international conference in Paris set to take up the issue amid a global race to establish a presence on the Moon.…

blocks.text: Countries are gearing up to establish a unified lunar time standard, with a key international conference in Paris set to take up the issue amid a global race to establish a presence on the Moon.

Member states will try to work it out at the plenary meeting of the General Conference on Weights and Measures, which decides global measurement standards, as operations including the construction of a permanent base and lunar navigation are expected to be in full swing from around 2030.
China and the United States are among the countries pursuing plans to land astronauts on the lunar surface and secure lunar resources.

Under the theory of general relativity, time on the Moon passes slightly faster than on Earth because lunar gravity is only about one-sixth of Earth’s, meaning lunar time runs ahead of time on Earth by around 56 microseconds per day.
The difference between time on the Moon and on Earth is believed to pose problems for future lunar missions.

In building a lunar base, for example, operators must know the exact location where work is being done. Signals from satellites orbiting the Moon are expected to be used to calculate positions, similar to Earth’s Global Positioning System.
Lunar time needs to be accurate, because a timing error of just 1 microsecond can change a calculated position by about 300 meters, potentially affecting robots working at a lunar base.

Mamoru Sekido, a research manager at Japan’s National Institute of Information and Communications Technology, said international cooperation to coordinate and unify time standards for satellites operated by different countries is vital for lunar development.

There are two proposals for setting lunar time. One assumes a hypothetical clock at the Moon’s center of mass and calculates lunar time from it, while the other uses a real clock placed at the Moon’s average surface height as the reference, an approach that would be closer to how time is defined on Earth. /dl

articles.title: Man who murdered Molly Ticehurst will not face life in jail, judge says
articles.summary: Justice Natalie Adams says she is troubled by expert evidence about rape allegations in slain woman’s police statement

blocks.text: Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend will not face a life sentence for her domestic violence murder, a crime which galvanised a national movement against gendered abuse.
Ticehurst, a 28-year-old childcare educator, was found dead in her home at Forbes, in the New South Wales central-west, in the early hours of 22 April 2024.
Her former boyfriend Daniel Billings broke into her bedroom and stabbed her 15 times in a ferocious attack that lasted less than a minute.

Billings had been charged with several counts of raping Ticehurst and a string of domestic violence offences just over two weeks before the killing, but he was freed on bail by a local court registrar the next day.
During a mention in the NSW supreme court on Monday, Justice Natalie Adams told the legal parties she did not expect them to seek a life sentence.
Adams said there would likely be mitigating factors to consider when sentencing Billings, as there were in almost all cases.
“It’s difficult to identify what’s [legally] unique about this case,” she said.
But the judge said she was troubled with how to deal with expert evidence about Ticehurst’s police statement that she was repeatedly raped by Billings.
The sexual assault charges were dropped when Billings pleaded guilty to murder in November 2025 after 18 months of legal negotiations.
Billings always denied raping Ticehurst and developed a dark obsession with clearing his name in the lead-up to the murder.
“If I’m going to do the time, I may as well do the crime,” he said in a conversation with a friend soon before the murder, according to a statement of agreed facts before the court.
Adams said she could not ignore the rape allegations, despite the charges being dropped, when it came to sentencing Billings for murder.
“It was him seeing the police facts that set him to spiral,” the judge said.
Acting out of spite over the allegations could push his crime into another serious category, she said.
“The sense of grievance about a perceived false allegation, there’s no getting around that,” Adams said.
“Whether it’s almost a public-justice type murder or domestic-violence type murder.”
after newsletter promotion
Adams said it was possible all the elements to satisfy the legal definition of sexual assault were in Ticehurst’s account to police.
Changes to consent laws in NSW, which included affirmative language in the legislation, meant it was a crime where both parties “feel they’re telling the truth”.
“The only witness who could have told us is dead,” the judge said.
Billings, who has been in custody in the supermax wing of Goulburn jail since he was charged, will face court in person.
He will hear victim impact statements from the Ticehurst family, along with expert evidence about his mental state at the time of the murder.
A series of videos he made before and after the murder are also expected to be played to court.
Ticehurst’s death became a flashpoint in the nation’s fight against domestic violence and led to legal changes in NSW, including tighter bail laws.
Billings, 31, who has pleaded guilty to murder, is set to face court in Orange for a two-day sentence hearing from Thursday.
Adams has indicated she will sentence Billings later in September.

articles.title: ‘Everything’s smashed to bits’: Ukrainians turn anger on those storing weapons near their villages
articles.summary:
As Russia hits another ammunition warehouse, killing at least 38, locals put blame on poorly placed depots

It is a day and a half since a Russian jet-powered drone
articles.byline: Dan Sabbagh in Myla, Kyiv region. Photography by Julia Kochetova

blocks.text: It is a day and a half since a Russian jet-powered drone smashed into an ammunition dump in Myla, a village 15 miles outside central Kyiv. Volodymyr, 61, a security guard, leads visitors from his family’s badly damaged home, its roof blown off, back windows shattered, through the garden towards the impact site 300 metres away.

The garden, like so many in Ukraine’s villages and suburbs, is a sizeable allotment. But today the greenhouse is shattered, a vegetable patch is blackened and crisp underfoot. Several metres of grapevine have been destroyed. Even so, Volodymyr finds two surviving bunches to hand to the Guardian.

blocks.caption: Inside the damaged house in Myla village, Kyiv region. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: It is a remarkable moment of generosity, though his family now has no electricity and no water after Thursday night’s extended bombing. The death toll rose by one on Sunday, to 38, and four more people are still missing in an episode that has swiftly raised questions about why ammunition was stored so close to people’s homes.

In the yard before the garden, Vira, 65, knows who is at fault. “Those who set up the depot here are to blame. There are people here, this is a village. You can’t keep something like that here,” she says. She and her son Serhii hid for hours in a small bunker by the side of the house waiting out what witnesses said were 30 or 50 explosions that went on for about six hours after the initial strike at 8pm.

Serhii says they had no idea ammunition was stored in their village. “I thought it was humanitarian aid that was stored there.” Now the family is presented with a cleanup that will be costly and difficult while starting with next to nothing. He is charging his phone from a car battery via a converter. It is all the power they have.

A missile shell from a Grad rocket launcher was found on their property once the explosions subsided, Serhii adds, as well as “several mines and cluster munitions”. They have been removed by the cleanup team, although a burnt-out box of bullets, freshly discovered in another part of the semi-collapsed ceiling, has not and sits by the front door awaiting a further collection.

blocks.caption: Volodymyr shows his working place where he was during the attack. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Volodymyr’s tour continues out back. A grass line, effectively a track, has been marked out through the wood beyond the garden, between blackened patches where fires burned. There is smouldering, even flames in places, more bullets and boxes of bullets, then, on the right, unmistakably, a detonated anti-tank mine.

Finally, the woods open out, revealing a warehouse site, large parts of which are bombed out, an open area of destruction. A sulphurous smell endures, and periodically explosions can be heard, though they may be controlled detonations. Clear-up work by the emergency services is in the process of being halted at lunchtime because there is another drone threat above.

blocks.caption: Rescue services are still working on the site. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Volodymyr was on guard duty at a lumber yard close to the ammunition store on the night of the bombing. He survived the initial strike unscathed, and headed back home promptly, but feels a guard’s need to return. “I’ve been coming back and forth for two days to see these ashes,” he says.

Thirty of the dead were from a care home close to the ammunition store, the location of which is now subject of a criminal inquiry by Ukraine’s intelligence service. But it is not the first attack of its kind in recent weeks. There have been other Russian bombings of poorly placed ammunition dumps, as Moscow aggressively targets warehouse sites at a time when Ukraine is doing similar.
after newsletter promotion

The fact this has happened recently in Ukraine is not lost on Liudmyla, whose adult daughter was in the house a couple of doors down when the Shahed drone hit. The home is also heavily damaged, windows facing the warehouse blown in, and Liudmyla recalls that a similar incident happened in early July, on the edge of Kyiv.

blocks.caption: Liudmyla near her damaged house. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: “Look at what’s going on here. Everything’s smashed to bits right here. Vyshneve [the scene of the previous incident, nine miles south-east] wasn’t enough for them, and there was more somewhere else too. No, they’ve dumped all this right by people’s vegetable gardens, right on their doorsteps,” she says, warning that munitions are still strewn around, not yet cleared up.

Nine people were killed after a munitions store was hit at Vyshneve, and 280 homes damaged. Two people have been detained on suspicion of allowing weapons to be stored in an inappropriate place after the episode, but as the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said on Saturday, similar has happened again.

It is a dismal repetition at a time when Kyiv is already coming under increased attack from Moscow, the harm to civilians from attacks on food stores and logistics warehouses increasing. When Liudmyla is pressed to say who is at fault for the deaths and destruction at Myla, she offers a double answer.
“Putin! Who else? And those who set up the depot here.”

articles.title: Properties in UK national parks command 24% premium, study finds
articles.summary:
Nationwide research also shows average 14% premium for housing in national landscapes of England and Wales

Housebuyers are paying a premium of almost a quarter to own a property located…

blocks.text: Housebuyers are paying a premium of almost a quarter to own a property located within a UK national park, with the New Forest the most expensive national park to live in, according to Britain’s biggest building society.

Nationwide found that a property located within a national park cost 24% more on average than a similar property elsewhere, while buyers were also stumping up a 6% premium for homes within three miles of a national park.

The lender said that, as well as the attractions of the beautiful countryside, restricted development in national parks meant construction of new housing was limited, which kept house prices relatively high.
The average property in the New Forest was £563,000, followed by the South Downs park at £485,000, and the Peak District at £450,000.

Nationwide also found a 14% premium for properties located in the national landscapes of England and Wales, formerly known as areas of outstanding natural beauty, such as Surrey Hills and the Chilterns.

Surrey Hills is the most expensive national landscape in which to buy property, with average prices of £710,000, the building society said. Designated in 1958 and covering approximately a quarter of the county of Surrey, the area is home to about 40,000 people who mostly live in small villages and rural hamlets, such as Shere, Mickleham and Westhumble.
after newsletter promotion

The premiums paid on properties in these areas appear to be remaining remarkably consistent, with similar research by Nationwide from 2024 showing that homes in national parks attracted a 25% premium, while national landscape properties were 15% more expensive.

articles.title: 15,800 rescued across Luzon as ‘habagat’ rains trigger floods
articles.summary: More than 15,800 residents across Luzon were rescued and evacuated by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) as intensified rains from the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” caused widespread flooding in…

blocks.text: (PCG PHOTO)

More than 15,800 residents across Luzon were rescued and evacuated by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) as intensified rains from the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” caused widespread flooding in several provinces.
The PCG said its teams conducted simultaneous rescue operations and preemptive evacuations in coordination with local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices.

“Our ongoing efforts are supported by the anticipatory deployment of personnel, floating assets, land vehicles, and rescue equipment to strategic locations,” Commodore Noemie Cayabyab, the spokesperson of PCG, said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31.

blocks.caption: (PCG PHOTO)

blocks.text: According to the PCG, the advance deployment of its resources allowed response teams to reach communities affected by flooding more quickly.
“These capabilities allow us to position response units closer to high-risk communities, shortening the time needed to reach families requiring assistance,” Cayabyab added.
PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan credited the Coast Guard’s continuing modernization and additional equipment and personnel for its improved disaster preparedness.
Also, he cited the provision of a Quick Response Fund, which enables the agency to address operational gaps and sustain its emergency response efforts.

articles.title: PH, Brunei Supreme Courts sign MOU on judicial education, cooperation
articles.summary: The Supreme Courts (SC) of the Philippines and Brunei have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to strengthen judicial education and institutional cooperation, the Philippine SC announced…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 11:56am

The Supreme Courts (SC) of the Philippines and Brunei have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to strengthen judicial education and institutional cooperation, the Philippine SC announced Monday.
According to the High Court, the signing ceremony was held at The Empire Brunei in Brunei Darussalam on Sunday, August 30.

“Our courts today operate in an increasingly interconnected world. Legal disputes and criminal activities no longer remain neatly within territorial boundaries,” Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo said in a statement.
Under the agreement, the Philippine Judicial Academy (PHILJA) and Brunei’s Judicial Education and Training Unit were designated as the implementing institutions.
The two institutions will exchange expertise, knowledge, and best practices in judicial education, including curriculum design, teaching methods, and evaluation systems, the SC said.
They will also organize and participate in workshops, seminars, conferences, study visits, and other capacity-building programs for judges, judicial officers, and court personnel.

Gesmundo also identified several areas for cooperation, including the study of Shari’ah, approaches to trafficking in persons, cybercrime and electronic evidence, and climate justice and environmental adjudication.
The Chief Justice said the MOU is “an affirmation of the enduring friendship between our two nations and of our commitment to judicial excellence, rule of law, and effective delivery of justice.”
“Through candid dialogue and the sharing of experiences, we gain not only new knowledge but also a deeper appreciation of the circumstances and perspectives that shape another judiciary,” he said.
“In this regard, judicial education becomes a bridge, not merely between institutions, but between people and legal traditions as well,” he added.

Meanwhile, Brunei Chief Justice Dato Seri Paduka Steven Chong said the Philippines’ role as co-chair of the Working Group on Judicial Education and Training under the Council of ASEAN Chief Justices reflects the country’s commitment to strengthening judicial education.
He said there is much to gain from looking beyond their own institutional boundaries and learning from their counterparts.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Google Maps changes Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' in US
articles.summary: The name change even made its way to some government websites in Canada which pull map data from Google Maps. Meanwhile, Ontario Premier Doug Ford made his position clear by erecting a billboard on…

image.caption: Trump's desired name change was reflected in the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)Image: Jim Watson/AFP

blocks.text: Google Maps has changed the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for users in the US.
It comes days after President Donald Trump ordered the lake to be renamed, which included changing the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

"Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the US, people using Maps in the US will see 'Lake America,' those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario,' and those outside of the US and Canada will see both names," Google said in a brief statement.
"These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now."

blocks.caption: The lake's new moniker appears for users in the USImage: Google/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Google's decision to follow through with Trump's order echoes its 2025 move to label the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America." Mexico sued Google in response.
Why did Trump order the name change?
Lake Ontario gets its name from the Indigenous Wendat word "Ontari'io," meaning "big, beautiful lake." The province of Ontario to the north later adopted this name after the lake.
Trump's decision to change this centuries-old name comes amid a trade war between the US and Canada.
What will Trump rename next?

The two countries had spent weeks negotiating a deal to resolve the war which was started by Trump, but Canada pulled out after Prime Minister Mark Carney complained of "last-minute changes" that were "unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal."
Among the sticking points, Carney said, were American objections to French product labeling laws as well as French content requirements for streaming services in Quebec.
Canada puts up signs, takes down websites
On Saturday, Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a new sign on the shore of the lake.
It read, "Lake Ontario: Now and always" — in both English and French.
"President Trump can call it whatever he wants, but I can tell you, the rest of the world will always call it Lake Ontario," Ford said.

blocks.caption: Ontario Premier Doug Ford put up a new sign on the shores of the lakeImage: Keito Newman/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: However, the new name "Lake America" did sneak into some applications north of the border.

A number of government-run websites in Canada that use Google Maps saw the name change automatically. This included the Liquor Control Board of Ontario, which had actually pulled American alcohol off the shelves as part of the trade war.
"Some Ontario government agency websites pull map data directly from Google Maps," Ontario's public services minister Stephen Crawford said on Sunday evening.
"Following recent changes by Google, we're actively reviewing our websites to make sure they all identify Lake Ontario by its correct name: Lake Ontario."

articles.title: DSWD spox to public: Check your facts on food pack cost before sharing
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Aug. 31, disputed the ₱1,503.84 price tag being circulated online for its family food packs, saying the figure referred to the…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Aug. 31, disputed the ₱1,503.84 price tag being circulated online for its family food packs, saying the figure referred to the maximum amount allowed for the procurement package, not the actual cost of each food pack.

DSWD Disaster Response Management Group Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao said the actual winning bid for the food packs cited in the post was ₱797.80 per box, submitted by 2 Go Global International Corporation.

“₱797.80 lang ang halaga ng bawat kahon ng food packs na nasa post based on the winning bid. Kaya mali ang pinalalabas sa isang social media post na ₱1,503.84 ang halaga ng bawat family food pack ng DSWD (The food packs in the post cost only ₱797.80 per box based on the winning bid. Therefore, it is wrong to claim in a social media post that each DSWD family food pack costs ₱1,503.84),” Dumlao said.
The DSWD spokesperson urged the public to direct questions or complaints to the agency and to exercise caution when sharing information from social media.

“Hindi po nakatutulong ang mga ganitong misinformation, lalo’t higit sa panahon na ang atensiyon dapat ay nakatuon sa mabilisang pagtugon sa pangangailangan ng mga nasalanta (This kind of misinformation does not help, especially at a time when attention should be focused on responding quickly to the needs of disaster-affected families),” Dumlao said.

“Nag-aappeal din po kami sa mga concerned citizens na siguraduhin ang inyong dokumento ay accurate sa inyong pagshare. Inuulit din po namin na ang DSWD ay bukas sa lahat ng komento at reklamo (We also appeal to concerned citizens to make sure that the documents they share are accurate. We reiterate that the DSWD is open to all comments and complaints),” she added.
Dumlao said the amount indicated in the bidding document was based on market scoping and covered procurement specifications, packaging, logistics, delivery, and other factors related to the project.

“We would like to clarify that the amount of procurement of family food packs differs per bid. The total amount spent for family food packs depends on the winning bid. The bid document which was posted is a public document and is the maximum bid amount of the package of items,” she said.
She said the DSWD uses a simplified approach in procuring food packs to help ensure the availability and quick delivery of food assistance to families affected by disasters.

“Dumadaan sa ‘competitive bidding’ ng DSWD ang lahat ng procurement ng family food packs kung saan ang may pinakamababang price bid offer at compliant sa mga specifications at iba pang requirements ang idinedeklarang bid winner (All DSWD procurement of family food packs goes through competitive bidding, where the bidder offering the lowest price while complying with the specifications and other requirements is declared the winner),” Dumlao said.

Under the process, the DSWD Bids and Awards Committee evaluates suppliers based on their technical, financial, and legal requirements and determines the lowest calculated and responsive bid in accordance with government procurement rules.
Each family food pack contains six kilograms of rice, four cans of tuna flakes, four cans of corned beef, two cans of sardines, five sachets of instant coffee, and five sachets of choco malt drink.

DSWD said the composition of the food packs was endorsed to the National Nutrition Council and follows the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake formulated by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute.
The contents are intended to provide affected families with a combination of staple food, protein sources, energy, and essential nutrients.
However, the food packs are not intended to replace a family’s regular food supply for an extended period.
DSWD said the food assistance is intended to help sustain a family of five for two to three days.

articles.title: PIDS: Stronger institutions key to turning human capital investments into growth
articles.summary: The Philippines needs stronger institutions to turn increased investments and major reforms in education, health, social protection, and skills development into higher productivity and sustained…

blocks.text: The Philippines needs stronger institutions to turn increased investments and major reforms in education, health, social protection, and skills development into higher productivity and sustained economic growth, according to state-run policy think tank Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS).

In a recent discussion paper titled “Reshaping Economic Institutions for Transformational Partnerships in Human Capital Development,” PIDS said the country has strengthened its macroeconomic fundamentals and reached upper-middle-income status, but persistent gaps in learning, health-system integration, skills matching, enterprise participation, and productivity continue to hamper economic transformation.
The paper was authored by PIDS senior research fellows John Paolo R. Rivera, Michael Ralph M. Abrigo, and Valerie Gilbert T. Ulep.
“The Philippine development challenge is not the absence of reform,” PIDS quoted the paper’s authors as saying in an Aug. 30 statement.
The constraint, they argued, lies in how investments are “coordinated, implemented, sustained, and evaluated,” PIDS added.

The paper identified four interrelated institutional constraints: fragmentation and coordination failures; uneven implementation capacity; short policy horizons and weak credible commitment; and learning and incentive failures.
These weaknesses limit the benefits of investments in human capital because education, health, employment, and productivity are closely interconnected.

Educational outcomes, for instance, are influenced by health, nutrition, household conditions, and labor market opportunities, while skills generate greater economic value when businesses can put them to productive use.
Innovation likewise requires not only capable workers but also enterprises willing to invest in technology and improve their operations.
“Human capital is produced and utilized through an interconnected ecosystem and not through isolated sectoral interventions,” the authors said.
As a result, investments in one sector may deliver lower returns when complementary investments in other areas fail to keep pace.
The paper said fragmented investments can also prevent the government, businesses, households, and other stakeholders from realizing the full collective benefits of their individual efforts.
PIDS thus called for a shift from a program-centered to an institution-centered approach to human capital development.

Instead of focusing solely on higher spending or expanding individual programs, policymakers should strengthen institutions that allow investments across education, health, labor markets, innovation, and productive sectors to reinforce one another, according to the paper.
“Government acts only as a financier or service provider but also as an institutional architect,” the authors wrote.
In this role, the government establishes the rules, incentives, information systems, and coordination mechanisms needed to support collective action and encourage long-term investment.

The paper also proposed what it called “transformational partnerships,” or institutional arrangements that enable multiple stakeholders to coordinate long-term investments in human capital and productivity.
PIDS stressed, however, that the goal is not merely to establish more partnerships.

Unlike conventional public-private partnerships (PPPs), which are often focused on infrastructure and service delivery, transformational partnerships emphasize sustained collaboration on complex development challenges that cannot be addressed by a single institution.
“The policy objective is not more partnerships per se, but better institutions that enable productive partnerships,” the authors said.

The paper identified five priorities to improve the effectiveness of human capital investments: better coordination around shared outcomes; credible long-term commitments; stronger institutional learning and information systems; better-aligned incentives for public and private investments; and greater capacity to implement and sustain complex reforms.

“The Philippines needs continued investment in its people, but investment alone is not enough. Institutions must enable these investments to reinforce one another and produce lasting gains in human capital, productivity, and economic transformation,” PIDS said.
“Institutional reform is itself a prerequisite for making human capital investment effective, sustained, and productive,” the authors said.

articles.title: Dutch federation calls for FIFA summit, turns against Infantino
articles.summary: AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Dutch football federation is calling for an international summit to discuss the future of FIFA after becoming the latest nation to call for new leadership at the global soccer…

blocks.text: AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Dutch football federation is calling for an international summit to discuss the future of FIFA after becoming the latest nation to call for new leadership at the global soccer governing body on Sunday, Aug. 30.
In a statement, the federation said it “no longer has confidence” in FIFA President Gianni Infantino, and offered to host an international summit to discuss ideas to reshape the organisation.
The Dutch federation said there is a need for a “new FIFA,” not just a new president.

“The 2027 presidential election should not only be about who leads FIFA,” it said. "First, we need to determine what kind of FIFA we want. Then we can identify the leadership needed to deliver that change.

“For us, this discussion must be about more than Gianni Infantino. The key question is: what kind of FIFA does football need?” the federation said. “Our ambition is clear: a strong and credible FIFA that belongs to football, serves its members and develops the game around the world.”

It said “this should not be a European plan for the rest of the world. We want to develop this new direction together with FIFA’s 211 Member Associations and the confederations from all parts of the world.”
The federation said it shared “this position and our vision for the future of FIFA” in a letter to UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin.
UEFA, the European soccer confederation, is spearheading the backlash against Infantino over his failed World Cup sell-off plan that created a deep rift in the sport.
Many of its other member federations have withdrawn their support for the FIFA leader, who is up for re-election in March 2027. Some have called for his resignation.
Infantino has not given any indication he plans to step down.
“We believe FIFA needs new leadership from 2027 onwards. But a new president alone is not enough. The way FIFA is governed must change as well,” it said.

“We see too much power concentrated around the FIFA president and insufficient separation between the president and the FIFA administration,” the federation said. “The process surrounding the now-withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal was a turning point for us. Withdrawing the proposal was necessary, but it does not restore the trust that has been lost.”
The Dutch federation said it sees three priorities: improved governance with a better balance of power, putting soccer’s social power at the heart of FIFA and investing more in soccer worldwide.

articles.title: Angelica Jones on Sachzna Laparan's cover of 'Miss Flawless': 'Nakaka-offend ‘yun on my part'
articles.summary: Former actress Angelica Jones opens up about her thoughts on the 2019 cover of "Miss Flawless" by Flow G and Bosx1ne featuring Sachzna Laparan. On the "Your Honor" podcast, the comedienne and…

blocks.text: Former actress Angelica Jones opens up about her thoughts on the 2019 cover of "Miss Flawless" by Flow G and Bosx1ne featuring Sachzna Laparan.
On the "Your Honor" podcast, the comedienne and politician said she and Sachzna originally planned to meet to discuss the use of the song.
"Ang sabi nila magsu-shoot daw sa Laguna at makikipag-meet up. Meet up for shooting na, of course, ipapaalam muna (pag-revive sa kanta)... parang meron silang idi-discuss," Angelica shared.
The meeting did not push through.

"To be honest with you nakaka-offend ‘yun on my part kasi elected official ako and then nag-react ‘yung tourism ng Laguna na ang sabi ay hindi raw tuloy ang shooting, hindi raw tuloy ‘yung pagpunta nila doon,” Angelica said.
She continued: ''Nalaman ko na lang na pumunta sila dun sa fourth district (sa Laguna), (doon) nag-shoot at ‘yung kantang ‘Miss Flawless’ (ginamit nila)."
According to Angelica, she was asked by Lito Camo, who composed the song, if the group asked permission to cover the song.
"Tinanong ako ni Kuya Lito Camo, tanong niya sa akin, ‘Bokal, nagpaalam ba sa sila ‘yo sila?’ Kasi sabi ko bago sila mag-shoot at ilabas ‘yung kantang ‘yan, magpaalam muna sa ‘yo,” she shared.
Angelica had never met Sachzna prior, although she had seen her once at an awards ceremony.
Still, Angelica said she would accept Sachzna’s apology if she offered one.
"Wala naman problema sa akin puwede namang sabihin sorry, apologize. I will accept the apology kung meron pero as of now wala, e."

articles.title: Drunk tricycle driver nabbed after nearly hitting cops at checkpoint
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – A 51-year-old tricycle driver was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to evade a police checkpoint and nearly hitting two policemen along the…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – A 51-year-old tricycle driver was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to evade a police checkpoint and nearly hitting two policemen along the national highway in Barangay Tigbao, Tigbao town in Zamboanga del Sur.

Capt. Derf Jay Maquinta, spokesperson of the Zamboanga del Sur Police Provincial Office, said personnel of Tigbao Municipal Police Station were conducting a checkpoint at around 6:10 p.m. when the driver of a red Bajaj RE tricycle, traveling from Lakewood toward Pagadian City, sped through the area.
The tricycle overtook a vehicle under inspection and proceeded without stopping, nearly striking two police personnel who managed to move aside and avoid injury.

Authorities pursued the vehicle, which allegedly accelerated in an attempt to escape. The driver eventually lost control, causing the tricycle to crash and overturn about 300 meters from the checkpoint.
Police said the driver, reportedly under the influence of liquor, sustained minor bruises.

His two passengers, aged 20 and 23, suffered minor injuries and chest pain. All three were brought to the Tigbao Rural Health Unit, with the passengers later referred to Pagadian City for further evaluation.
The driver is now under police custody awaiting the filing of appropriate charges. INQ
