articles.title: Barrier lake near Nepal-China border fully drains, China says
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — A barrier lake formed near the Nepal-China border after last week’s massive ice-rock avalanche has fully drained through natural outflow, China’s Ministry of Water Resources said on…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — A barrier lake formed near the Nepal-China border after last week’s massive ice-rock avalanche has fully drained through natural outflow, China’s Ministry of Water Resources said on Sunday, easing fears of another sudden flood downstream.

The lake had formed near the confluence of Nepal’s Chhochen Khola and China’s Purepu Tsangpo following Wednesday’s glacier collapse on the northern face of Langtang Ri, which triggered a devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi river system.

Citing the ministry, China Daily reported that around 2 million cubic metres of water had accumulated behind the blockage. The ministry’s hydrological emergency monitoring team said water was now flowing normally through natural channels and the impounded water had been almost completely discharged.

Nepali scientist Nitesh Khadka, who works at the Chinese Academy of Sciences in Chengdu, also shared photographs sent by colleagues showing that the lower barrier lake had drained. He said more than half the water in an upper lake had also flowed out.
The development comes as river levels rose again in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems on Sunday, raising fresh concerns in areas already devastated by Wednesday’s disaster.

The swollen Trishuli river has eroded riverbanks in Nuwakot and Dhading districts. Flood-induced erosion and a subsequent landslide at Krishnabhir in Dhading have completely blocked the Muglin-Kathmandu section of the Prithvi Highway.
Floodwaters also swept away a suspension bridge over the Trishuli river linking Ghyachok in Gorkha with Charaudi in Dhading on Sunday.

Chinese authorities had earlier warned that the barrier lake posed a high risk of breaching, with continued rainfall expected to increase the volume of water behind the natural dam. Satellite monitoring later showed that the lake had begun draining gradually, reducing the immediate threat. /dl

articles.title: Zambales agriculture losses reach P37.5 million
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Damage and losses to Zambales agriculture due to heavy rains and floods have reached P37.55 million, based on the latest data from the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Damage and losses to Zambales agriculture due to heavy rains and floods have reached P37.55 million, based on the latest data from the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office on Sunday (Aug. 30)
According to Rolex Estella, head of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office, the tally is the accumulated losses from the habagat and tropical cyclones.

Rice accounted for the biggest share of the losses at P21.58 million with damages in 1,069.42 hectares of farmland affecting 1,267 farmers, based on the assessment of the Office of the Provincial Agriculturist (OPA).
The municipality of Sta. Cruz recorded the highest rice losses at P11.38 million, followed by the towns of San Antonio with P2.8 million and Subic with P2.05 million.
High-value crops sustained P10.7 million in losses, affecting 358 farmers and 73.64 hectares.
Sta. Cruz also recorded the highest losses in high-value crops at P4.03 million, followed by the town of Botolan at P3.54 million and Subic at P1.69 million.
The assessment also included damage to agricultural facilities, irrigation systems and farm equipment.
Agricultural infrastructure sustained P1.21 million in damage, including a pig pen in Barangay Sta. Fe, San Marcelino, which was washed out and covered by mud.
Damage to agricultural machinery and equipment reached P1.55 million, including farm machinery in Sta. Fe, San Marcelino that was either washed away by floodwaters or buried under soil deposits.
A hand-held agricultural tractor in Barangay Bayto, Sta. Cruz, was also partially damaged.
The assessment also placed damage to a small water impounding project in Barangay Amungan, Iba, at P700,000 after its embankment slope and foundation were undermined.
Fisheries were also affected, with losses of P906,220 in capture fisheries and P796,065 in aquaculture.
Separately, the Provincial Veterinary Office reported the loss of 193 animals valued at P1.18 million.
The figures, said Estella, remain a progress report as assessment and validation of losses continue in affected areas.
The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Zambales earlier declared the province under a state of calamity following the widespread flooding and damage caused by the successive episodes of heavy rains.
As of Sunday, 710 families or 14,052 individuals have been evacuated in the province, some of which were forced to evacuate due to widespread flooding. INQ

articles.title: Nepal buries dead as rescuers seek thousands missing after floods
articles.summary: BIDUR, Nepal — Nepal was burying on Monday some of the hundreds of bodies retrieved after a deadly, tsunami-like flood crashed through the Himalayan region, sweeping away villages and leaving…

blocks.text: BIDUR, Nepal — Nepal was burying on Monday some of the hundreds of bodies retrieved after a deadly, tsunami-like flood crashed through the Himalayan region, sweeping away villages and leaving thousands still missing.
Distraught families have packed rescue stations and hospitals in search of their missing relatives, while others have faced the grim task of identifying bodies at overflowing morgues.

The huge wave of ice, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday claimed at least 797 lives in both Nepal and Tibet — across the border in China — with reports of some bodies possibly swept downstream as far as India.
At least 3,048 people remain missing, including many tourists and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash. There are also 933 workers at hydropower plants among those unaccounted for in Nepal.

Nepali army troops and engineers drilled through debris on Sunday towards workers believed trapped in a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site in the Himalayan river valley after they successfully inserted a pipe into the passage.
Workers who managed to get out described horrifying scenes when the disaster struck.
Surendra Dowluri, 33, from India’s Andhra Pradesh state, said raging water swamped the Upper Trishuli-1 site, where he was working.

“We heard a very loud sound… and saw that the turbine floor was submerged with slush, and six workers were stuck in that,” Dowluri told AFP in the Nepali capital Kathmandu after his rescue four days into the disaster.
“We managed to rescue five of them, but one person lost his life,” he said, describing how some workers reached higher ground or construction areas out of reach of the torrent.
Overnight rain and rising river waters also hampered rescue operations on Sunday, filling the excavation area with water before conditions eased, the Nepali army said.
DNA samples
The disaster was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
The torrent caused the formation of huge lakes, closely watched by emergency workers for risks to their operations.
Chinese rescuers near the Tibet border port that was hit by a deadly mudslide were “moved to a safe location” on Sunday after a new lake was formed by a landslide, state media reported.
China has so far put the death toll in Tibet at 16, with the number of missing at 546.
In Nepal, the disaster agency raised the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 2,502 on Sunday, saying there were also 781 confirmed deaths.
Overwhelmed by the number of bodies and without proper freezing facilities, Nepali authorities have had to begin burials before completing the identification process.
Officials said DNA samples were taken from the bodies so that families could later claim them and perform traditional funeral rites.
Grieving relatives gathered at identification centres to watch LED screens showing pictures of retrieved bodies, occasionally closing their eyes when the grim exercise overwhelmed them.
Walking out from one such building next to a makeshift morgue, Shobha Adhikary told a local coordinator she believed one image showed her childhood best friend.
“It looks like him, for sure,” she said, showing coordinators a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
“My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta,” she said. Geeta has also been missing since Wednesday.
‘Swept away’
Survivors were also faced with the daunting prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” resident Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal’s Nuwakot district.
“There is nothing left.”
The United States and Canada said they would provide $3.6 million each in humanitarian aid to Nepal.

The UK has offered $6.8 million, while the UN released $2.5 million in emergency funding, and aid pledges were made by the European Union, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, and others.

Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the reconstruction bill could run into “billions of dollars”.
He appealed for specialised assistance, including heavy-lift drones and technology to help locate people who are trapped.
Khanal also called for forensic testing kits to identify corpses and freezer units to store them, saying bodies that have been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
The minister has highlighted the inequity that Nepal should suffer the extreme impacts of climate change when it has one of the world’s lowest per-capita carbon emissions.
That is due to its location in the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, where glaciers are melting at rapid speed as the planet heats.
In Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, a total of 2,141 personnel have joined search and rescue operations.
In an illustration of the difficulties of access, Chinese rescuers seeking to establish a route to the Tibet epicenter of the disaster, Gyirong Port, only advanced 285 meters (935 feet) on Sunday.
They have another 1.25 kilometers to go before reaching the site, the state-run Xinhua news agency reported. /dl

articles.title: Lacson says P3.713-B in public funds wasted on illegal Taguig reclamation projects
articles.summary: Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said on Monday, August 31 that at least P3.713-billion in public funds may have been wasted on projects along areas of Laguna Lake in Taguig City that are subject to…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said on Monday, August 31 that at least P3.713-billion in public funds may have been wasted on projects along areas of Laguna Lake in Taguig City that are subject to government action over “illegal” reclamation.
Senator Alan Peter Cayetano (left), Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson (Senate PRIB)

Lacson said this latest finding will be among the pieces of evidence he and his team will send to the Office of the Ombudsman’s fact-finding team “for proper disposition" as his feud with Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano continues.

“WASTED PUBLIC FUNDS DUE TO MISUSE: Based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of Identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH Flood Control and Multi-Purpose Projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore Reclamation Areas in Taguig City has so far reached ₱3.713 billion,” Lacson said in a post on X.

“These do not include other anomalous Slope Protection and Flood Mitigation projects along Taguig River involving double appropriations and 'ghost' projects using recycled photographs in different 'completed' projects, for billing purposes,” he added.
Lacson, citing official records and his and his team's investigation, identified the top five contractors involved in projects covering P2.372-billion as:
1) Dahl Construction: ₱858.22-million covering five solo projects worth P571.5-million and four joint ventures totaling ₱286.7-million;
2) J.C. Uyecio: ₱483.1 million covering four joint ventures;
3) Toughbuilt: ₱434.2 million covering three solo projects;
4) Topnotch: ₱329.9 Million covering two joint ventures with Core Check and one with Beam Team; and
5) GR Fervidal: ₱266.6 Million covering five solo multi-purpose building projects
Moreover, Lacson said all of the multipurpose building projects of GR Fervidal were suspended due to a “revision of plans” involving soil re-investigation.

Earlier, Lacson said Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon assured him that the DPWH would immediately issue cease-and-desist orders on projects linked to the illegal reclamation once he receives the appropriate requests from the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA).
This is to prevent further waste of government funds on contractors carrying out unauthorized or illegal activities, he said.
On Sunday, Dizon had said the DPWH has already issued the cease-and-desist orders, following a directive from the Office of the President coursed through the PRA.

On Saturday, Lacson revealed that at least four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City had been initially identified as covered by “fraudulently” issued land titles while at least four other parcels have no plotted title lots in the Land Registration Authority (LRA)'s digital file.
Lacson was prompted to make the disclosure after Cayetano insinuated that his earlier findings on the illegal reclamation activities were “fake news.”

But on Sunday, August 30, Cayetano, whose political bailiwick is Taguig City, said that the government stands to gain if allegations of illegally titled properties along Laguna Lake in Taguig are proven true.

Speaking at the 44th anniversary of Mandaport Apostolic Pentecostals (MAP) Church, Cayetano said the roughly 18-hectare property could ultimately benefit the government if the allegation surrounding its title is established.

“May isang nasa dyaryo kahapon na (nagsabi na may) 181,000 square meters o 18 hectares daw na ‘illegally titled.’ Sa isang banda po, nagho-hope din kami na totoo iyon. Bakit? Kasi kung totoong illegal iyon, sa gobyerno iyon (mapupunta), eh di may 18 hectares tayo ngayon para sa gobyerno (There was a report in the newspaper yesterday stating that there are 181,000 square meters—or 18 hectares—that are supposedly ‘illegally titled.’ On one hand, we actually hope that is true. Why? Because if it really is illegal, the property would revert to the government; that means we would have 18 hectares now for the government),” he said.
The minority leader said he welcomes the scrutiny of land titles in the area, noting that City of Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano had also long wanted the properties examined.

“Katulad ngayon na gusto nilang tingnan lahat ng titulo, matagal na pong gusto ni Lani iyon ( Just like now, when they want to examine all the titles—Lani has wanted to do that for a long time),” he said.

articles.title: Scheffler captures another FedEx Cup, surpasses Tiger Woods in career earnings
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Scottie Scheffler's second FedEx Cup title, and his 22nd victory on the PGA Tour during this astonishing five-year run, was different from all the others, even if it looked all too…

blocks.text: ATLANTA (AP) — Scottie Scheffler's second FedEx Cup title, and his 22nd victory on the PGA Tour during this astonishing five-year run, was different from all the others, even if it looked all too familiar.
Scheffler celebrated with a beer.

He had just closed with a 4-under 66 in the Tour Championship on Sunday, Aug. 30 — no one else from the leading six players broke par — and Scheffler had to wait for the last two groups to finish to make it official.

“There was an open bar inside and I'm like, ‘All right, I’m grabbing a beer.' It tasted great,” Scheffler said. “I don't really drink often. My wife and manager were like, ‘Wow, I haven’t seen you have a beer in a long time.' Well, season's over now. I'm going to have a beer. Well-earned beer.”
There was no arguing that, and there's no longer a debate over who had the best season in golf.

Scheffler took care of that at East Lake when he made up a three-shot deficit in four holes and pulled away to win the Tour Championship, claim a second FedEx Cup title and move past Tiger Woods for most PGA Tour earnings.

Scheffler signaled his rally with a 5-iron to within 2 inches of the cup on the 211-yard second hole. He caught Viktor Hovland with a 25-foot birdie on the fourth hole, pulled ahead for the first time on the 13th and wound up with a three-shot victory.
It was his first time with the low 72-hole score at the Tour Championship.

When he won in 2024, he had a two-shot lead before the tournament began given to the No. 1 seed under the “starting strokes” format. He won by four shots, even though two other players had a lower actual score. That still bugs him.

“When you’re coming down the stretch of a tournament and you’re tied or one shot back, it’s different than when you’re adding it up at the end and there’s starting strokes and all that stuff,” Scheffler said. “I think having a real tournament to finish the year, where I am the winner and the lowest score at East Lake, feels like a bit more of an accomplishment.”

Scheffler won for the third time this year — twice in the last three weeks during the PGA Tour's postseason — to match Chris Gotterup, Matt Fitzpatrick and U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark for most titles in 2026.
Players vote on the Jack Nicklaus Award for PGA Tour player of the year. Scheffler has won the last four years — another would tie him with Woods for most consecutive awards.

Taking over the top spot in career earnings was inevitable. The $40 million purse at the Tour Championship now counts as official money. Scheffler won $10 million, pushing his career total to $130,390,661.
Woods, who never played for more than a $10 million purse during his peak years from 1997 through 2009, had been at the top of the career money list for nearly 26 years.
It was a small slice of redemption for Scheffler, who lost in a playoff to Hovland at the Travelers Championship, one of his five runner-up finishes this year.

Hovland made only one birdie and closed with a 72 to finish alone in second, worth $5 million. Most aggravating for the Norwegian was having three putts hit the lip in a four-hole stretch on the back nine, two of them for birdie and one for par.

“He’s just good, and he played good every day,” Hovland said. “I could have shot 66 easily as well today. Just didn't have it. ... It wasn’t like anybody else really played all that great in contention, and that’s what you see — a lot of guys just gagging and throwing up. And that’s where he just kind of stays in it and shoots a nice score. That gets the job done.”

Scheffler had two bogeys — one an aggressive miss with a wedge from the fairway on No. 7, the other from a gnarly lie in the rough on the 14th — and otherwise felt he didn't miss much over a tough day of wind and firm turf that made the landing spots feel smaller.
East Lake played to a cumulative average of 67.35 through three rounds. On Sunday, the average score was 70.07.
Ryan Gerard, one shot behind Hovland staring out, made double bogey on the opening hole, followed with 13 straight pars and shot 72 to finish alone in third.
“They made it as difficult as they could today, and that’s kind of what we were looking for,” Gerard said. “I just wasn’t on enough to execute shots to really tucked hole locations.”
Scheffler said winning the Tour Championship for the FedEx Cup doesn't change his outlook on the season. That's for others to judge. Even so, he had a point to prove.

He felt as though he had underachieved in the PGA Tour postseason — losing a six-shot lead to Rory McIlroy in 2022, not putting up much of a fight when Hovland won in 2023 when he started with a two-shot lead and finished 16 shots behind.

“To come in this year maybe not winning the tournaments that I could have won throughout the regular season, to come in and win two out of three playoff events, is definitely a nice way to finish off the season,” Scheffler said.
“That was my motto going into the playoffs. Maybe in years I’ve underperformed in the postseason, and maybe this is a year I’ll perform better than I have in the regular season.”
That he did, and the beer no doubt went down smoothly.

articles.title: Pegula, Medvedev, Kostyuk make winning US Open start
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Jessica Pegula was one of the first players to compete at the U.S. Open, and she learned last year that starting Sunday, Aug. 30, provided some nice relief. “It is a little bit weird,…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Jessica Pegula was one of the first players to compete at the U.S. Open, and she learned last year that starting Sunday, Aug. 30, provided some nice relief.

“It is a little bit weird, but I did kind of enjoy that I could breathe for the next couple of days and everyone else is still freaking out about whether they’re going to win their first round,” she said.
The head start is great — unless it's a head start back to the airport.

“We were just talking about it, and I said, it’s so nice to play on Sunday when you win. But if you lose it’s not nice, because you feel like the tournament didn’t even start and you’re out of it,” No. 11 seed Marta Kostyuk said.
Pegula and Kostyuk both won easily and now the get the benefit of any extra day of rest before returning for the second round.

Novak Djokovic lost the first set as he began his quest for a record-extending 25th Grand Slam title on Sunday night against Mariano Navone. The match was paused during the first set so that the roof above Arthur Ashe Stadium could be closed because of rain that suspended play on the outer courts. Djokovic, 39, most recently lost his opening match earlier this month at Cincinnati.
The No. 3-seeded Pegula beat Elena-Gabriela Ruse 6-3, 6-2. She said she was nervous early, which makes sense given what could be at stake for the 2024 U.S. Open runner-up.

Pegula leads the women’s tour with 46 wins this season. She has two titles and has reached three other finals. Pegula can become No. 1 in the rankings if she wins her first major title and No. 2 Elena Rybakina loses before the semifinals.

Pegula next faces the winner of the match between Venus Williams and fellow wild card Sofia Kenin. They were set to play in the nightcap at Ashe, and Williams and sister Serena are scheduled to play doubles together.
“I felt really nervous before I went out there, but I know my coaches were like, ‘You didn’t really look that nervous. We thought you played great,’” Pegula said.
The No. 11-seeded Kostyuk sure did, beating Storm Hunter 6-4, 6-1 for a strong start to the year's final major after reaching the semifinals at the French Open and Wimbledon.
A Sunday start but the champions don’t begin until Monday

It was the second year of a Sunday start, though some of the biggest headliners don’t begin until Monday. Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka plays her opening match against Camila Osorio, before Carlos Alcaraz, who won his second U.S. Open title last year, plays his first singles match since April after recovering from a right wrist injury.

Past U.S. Open champions Naomi Osaka, Iga Swiatek, Sloane Stephens and Stan Wawrinka are also on the Monday schedule, along with Wimbledon women’s champion Linda Noskova and men’s contenders such as Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils, Felix Auger-Aliassime and Frances Tiafoe.

Daniil Medvedev, the 2021 U.S. Open champion, shook off his miserable preparation for the tournament by beating Hugo Gaston 6-4, 6-2, 6-4. The No. 7 seed was just 1-3 in the North American hard-court swing, usually a time he thrives.
“Last couple of weeks was not easy,” Medvedev said. “But I’m happy that today I managed to produce high-level tennis.”
Rain causes havoc, even in a stadium with a roof

Other winners Sunday included No. 9 Elina Svitolina, No. 19 Jasmine Paolini and No. 31 Leylah Fernandez, the 2021 U.S. Open runner-up. No. 27 seed Barbora Krejcikova, a two-time Grand Slam singles champion, lost 7-6 (4), 6-2 to Kamilla Rakhimova.

American Tommy Paul, the No. 20 seed, bounced back from losing a first-set tiebreak to Coleman Wong to win 6-7 (3), 6-1, 6-3, 6-3. Wong a year ago became the first man from Hong Kong to win an Open-era Grand Slam men’s singles match on the way to reaching the round of 32.

Seven matches couldn't be completed because of rain — and one was delayed even though it was being played in the other stadium with a retractable roof. There was a mechanical issue with one of the sensors at Louis Armstrong Stadium, and even after the roof finally closed, the court had to be dried before No. 15 seed Alexander Bublik and J.J. Wolf could play.
Maric Cilic, the 2014 U.S. Open champion, and 2022 runner-up Casper Ruud both withdrew with injuries.
The U.S. Open is in the process of getting a new look

Though the main draws didn't begin until Sunday, action at the U.S. Open has already been going on for nearly a week. Large crowds gathered for the mixed doubles tournament, an exhibition headlined by Roger Federer's return to Flushing Meadows and the singles qualifying tournaments, with admission to the grounds free.

Fans who came for the first time Sunday may have noticed a tournament in transition. The U.S. Open is in the second year of a three-year renovation of Arthur Ashe Stadium, the main venue at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. The improvements in the $800 million project include the addition of some lower-level seating, upgrades and additions of entertainment areas and the construction of a player performance center.
“Please pardon our appearance while we are reimagining spectacular,” reads a sign above the entrance to Ashe.
The project is scheduled to be completed in time for the 2027 U.S. Open.

articles.title: No shots fired in Baclaran Church incident, says rector
articles.summary: Two suffered minor injuries during the disturbance but church maintains no shooting occurred.

blocks.text: Composite: The National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Parañaque, known as Baclaran Church, as seen in September 2020 and interiors of the church as photographed in May 2023
Ranieljosecastaneda and LMP 2001 via Wikimedia; Philstar.com composite
MANILA, Philippines — An intoxicated man carrying a firearm caused a commotion at Baclaran Church on Sunday afternoon, but no shot was fired, the shrine's rector said.

Fr. Rico John Bilangel corrected reports of a shooting and said the scare occurred between around 4:45 p.m. and 5 p.m. on Sunday, August 30 at the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Parañaque City.
"It's important to clarify that there was no shooting at the church," Bilangel said in Filipino in a statement late Sunday.
Security personnel and authorities responded to the disturbance and the man was taken into police custody, according to the church.
Two people sustained minor injuries during the incident and were given first aid.
The church did not identify the injured individuals or provide details on how they were hurt.
Police account. A Parañaque police report cited by local media said a security guard approached the man after noticing his suspicious behavior while he was allegedly under the influence of alcohol.
The man allegedly punched the guard while being escorted out, causing a ruckus. Some churchgoers then helped restrain him until police arrived, according to the report.
Police arrested the troublemaker at around 5:15 p.m.
Authorities reportedly recovered from him a homemade .38-caliber revolver loaded with one round.

The police report, cited by Remate, noted complaints for alarm and scandal, disobedience to an agent of a person in authority and violation of the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act were being prepared against the suspect.
Bilangel urged the public not to circulate unverified information about the incident, saying such reports could cause unnecessary confusion and fear.
Baclaran Church is one of Metro Manila's major Catholic shrines and holds several Masses throughout Sundays as well as its well-known Wednesday novena services.

articles.title: Sweet sweep of fourth window makes Cone ‘the happiest guy’
articles.summary: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone just couldn’t hide his elation after the Nationals pulled off what they initially believed an improbable task of sweeping the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA World…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone just couldn’t hide his elation after the Nationals pulled off what they initially believed an improbable task of sweeping the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against Iran and Jordan.

Gilas hacked out a pulsating 82-81 escape against Jordan and then clamped down on world No. 26 Iran, 68-56, to improve the Nationals' record to 4-4, just a game behind their victims who are now on the third and fourth spots.
“I’m almost lost for words. That’s really unusual for me. I’m not usually lost for words. But I’m extremely happy,” said Cone during the post-game press conference.

“Kai just walked in (and asked), ‘Are you the happiest guy in the world?’ Because I said earlier, if we can win these two games, I’ll be the happiest guy in the world. So right now, I’m the happiest guy in the world,” he added.

Playing without a naturalized player and with their World Cup fates hanging in the balance, Gilas showed steely nerves and unwavering resolve to complete the two-game home stand before a roaring crowd which braved through the rainy weekend to watch the team.
The team also had to overcome two slow starts in the contests before digging deep and doing the game-winning plays when it mattered the most.

“These are two really, really high-level international teams, Iran, especially. I read something in FIBA yesterday that this is only the third win we’ve had against them in the last 13 games,” said Cone
“And we were able to do it all-Filipino pa. So it makes it really sweet to come out and win this game. And to do it at home,” he added.
Gilas’ win over Iran is the team’s first win over the Middle East powerhouse in a FIBA-sanctioned tournament since 2015.

Gilas also got several highlight performances from some of its players with CJ Perez and Kevin Quiambao spearheading the overtime win over Jordan, and Dwight Ramos and Juan Gomez de Liaño sparking the fourth-quarter pullaway against Iran.
Kai Sotto was in his usual dominant form in the two games while AJ Edu remains the defensive lynchpin the Nationals can rely on.

"It was one of those slow starts that we had but the guys just kept fighting and fighting and getting back into the game, and we came into halftime, we felt pretty good about ourselves. I think we felt we could pull this out,” said Cone.

“Just a great character performance by these guys in both games. To have that overtime game. It’s easy to kind of let down coming into this one [against Iran]. But they all knew the importance of it. They all knew the importance it was for them, and for the country,” he added.
"They came out and played and it was fun to be part of it. Really a lot of fun to be a part of it,” Cone furthered.

articles.title: One less thing to carry: US Navy, PH Army bring help to Tacloban school
articles.summary: Pacific Partnership 2026 focuses on humanitarian aid and disaster preparedness, with activities planned in various countries to strengthen community resilience against natural disasters

items: US Navy and Philippine Army are improving infrastructure at Lorenzo Daa Memorial School in Tacloban City, addressing long-standing issues like a broken water system and deteriorating classrooms.
The project aims to enhance the school's environment for teaching and learning, potentially allowing for a school canteen and a larger library for students.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
TACLOBAN, Philippines – Before the main activities of Pacific Partnership 2026 begin in Eastern Visayas in September, work is already underway at a public school in Tacloban City.

At Lorenzo Daa Memorial School in Barangay 103-A Paglaum, US Navy construction personnel and the Philippine Army are working on improvements that include repairs to the school’s water system, concreting portions of the school grounds and rehabilitation of two classrooms.
For the 143 pupils who attend the school, the project is more than an engineering activity.
For years, the school has struggled with a broken water system, muddy grounds during heavy rains, limited storage space and classrooms that need repair.
One of the most immediate problems has been water.
Because the school’s well and pump stopped working, pupils have had to bring about a liter of water from home, mainly for use in the school toilets.
“Teachers and learners, they ask their parents to bring one liter per learner,” principal Eric John Estoque said. “They have to bring one liter of water para CR.”
Now, the school hopes it will no longer have to rely on that arrangement.

Lorenzo Daa Memorial School is one of two public schools in Tacloban City selected to receive an infrastructure project through the US Navy’s Naval Mobile Construction Battalion 5 and the Philippine Army as part of Pacific Partnership 2026.
The work is expected to address some of the school’s long-standing problems.
The water system will be repaired, portions of the grounds will be concreted and two deteriorated classrooms will be rehabilitated.
For Estoque, the changes could also give the school room to do more.
He is considering using one of the repaired spaces for a school canteen so pupils can have a proper place to eat.
He also hopes to improve the school’s library, which currently shares a small space with his office.
A larger library would give pupils more room to sit, read and study.
“We are very much grateful for the help that they extend to us,” Estoque said.
He said the improvements would also help the school provide a better environment for teaching and learning.

Pacific Partnership is an annual US Navy-led multinational mission focused on humanitarian assistance and disaster preparedness in the Indo-Pacific. It brings together military personnel, medical teams, engineers, government agencies and community partners for activities including medical services, engineering projects, disaster-preparedness training and professional exchanges.

Pacific Partnership 2026 includes activities in Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Timor-Leste, with enduring projects in Fiji and Palau. Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Singapore and Britain are also listed among participating countries, although their involvement does not necessarily mean they will send personnel to Eastern Visayas.
In the Philippines, a coordination hub was established in Subic Bay in June to prepare medical, disaster-management, engineering and outreach activities.
For the Philippine Army, Pacific Partnership provides an opportunity to work with international partners and civilian agencies before an emergency.

Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Sabas, public affairs chief of the Philippine Army’s 8th Infantry Division, said the Army is coordinating with the US military, partner nations, national government agencies and local governments.
“The primary objective is to strengthen humanitarian assistance and disaster-response capabilities while enhancing interoperability among the participating forces and civilian agencies,” Sabas said.

The training allows responders to become familiar with each other’s procedures before they have to work together during an actual disaster, when time may be limited to arrange transportation, move supplies, maintain communications or reach isolated communities.
The focus on disaster preparedness is particularly relevant in Eastern Visayas, which regularly experiences tropical cyclones, heavy rain, flooding, landslides and storm surges.
The region was among the areas hardest hit by Super Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in 2013, and coastal and vulnerable communities remain exposed to flooding, landslides and storm surges.
The Philippine Army’s role includes logistics, transportation, coordination, security and community engagement during humanitarian activities.
Specific locations for Pacific Partnership 2026 in Eastern Visayas are still being coordinated.
Sabas said communities are being considered based on their needs, disaster vulnerability, accessibility, existing preparedness programs and the feasibility of conducting activities.
Local governments will help identify community needs and coordinate activities with residents to ensure they complement local disaster-risk-reduction and development priorities.
Some communities in Eastern Visayas are far from urban centers and can be difficult to reach, particularly during bad weather.

Paglaum is one example. It has no regular jeepney route directly serving the area, and residents and visitors often rely on private vehicles, motorcycles and other available transportation. Heavy rain or flooding can make access more difficult.
Sabas said preparations include planning transportation routes, staging areas, communications, medical support and backup arrangements.
The Army is working with local governments and other agencies through early planning, coordination and contingency measures.
For Sabas, the value of Pacific Partnership should extend beyond the departure of participating teams.
Training and exchanges can help responders identify gaps in communication, coordination, logistics and resource management, with lessons applied to future disaster exercises and contingency planning.

“More importantly, the activity is expected to contribute to a more resilient Eastern Visayas by helping communities and local responders improve their preparedness and ability to respond to natural disasters,” Sabas said.
At Lorenzo Daa Memorial School, the impact is more tangible: a repaired water system, rehabilitated classrooms and school grounds that will be easier to use during rain.
The improvements could also give pupils a better place to eat and a larger space to read.
For years, pupils have had to bring water from home because the school could not provide enough. If the repairs are completed as planned, that extra liter may finally stay at home.
For the children of Barangay 103-A Paglaum, that means one less thing to carry to school and one less problem to worry about. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

blocks.text: The Palawan Group of Companies proudly joined the celebration of the Baragatan sa Palawan Festival 2026, highlighting its deep connection to the province where its story began over 40 years ago. As one of Palawan's most anticipated annual events, Baragatan celebrates the province's culture, heritage, and unity, making it a meaningful occasion for the company to honor the community that has supported its growth from a single branch in Puerto Princesa into one of the country's leading financial service providers.
Pikoy, the official mascot of the Palawan Group of Companies, inspired by the endemic blue-naped parrot of Palawan, brought color and energy to the Baragatan Festival's float parade

Among the highlights of the company's participation in this year's Baragatan Festival were its participation in the Parada ng mga Palaweño and the Float Parade, where it joined communities from across the province to honor Palawan's history, culture, and traditions. Through its presence in these festivities, the company celebrated the spirit of togetherness that defines the province while supporting initiatives that preserve local heritage and encourage greater appreciation for the unique identity of the Palaweño people.

Throughout the festival, the Palawan Group engaged with residents and visitors through its interactive booth, offering games, prizes, giveaways, and information about its products and services, including Palawan Pawnshop, Palawan Express Pera Padala, Palawan Gold, and PalawanPay. The activities provided an opportunity for the company to connect directly with customers while highlighting its commitment to delivering accessible, reliable, and affordable financial services.

articles.title: Vaccine misinformation hampers measles-rubella drive in Central Visayas
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Health authorities in Central Visayas are battling more than measles and rubella (MR) as vaccine misinformation and hesitancy hamper efforts to immunize hundreds of thousands…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Health authorities in Central Visayas are battling more than measles and rubella (MR) as vaccine misinformation and hesitancy hamper efforts to immunize hundreds of thousands of young children.
The Department of Health in Central Visayas (DOH-7) has vaccinated only 21.7 percent of its 630,214-target for the region’s Measles-Rubella Supplemental Immunization Activity (MR-SIA).
The turnout improved from the 15 percent recorded last year, but remained far below the 95 percent coverage goal needed for strong population protection against measles.
As of Aug. 29, only 137,042 children aged 6 to 59 months in Cebu and Bohol had received the shot, leaving 493,172 still unvaccinated and vulnerable to the contagious diseases.
Officials have identified vaccine hesitancy and misinformation as major obstacles.
In Mandaue City, health officials pointed to social media misinformation as a key reason some parents refuse vaccination.
During the campaign’s first week, the Mandaue City Health Office reported about 577 parents refusing vaccination daily, with another 448 children deferred to a later date.
Health workers also reported encountering resistance, including hostility, during house-to-house vaccination.
The Mandaue City Council condemned social media posts discouraging vaccination and called for an investigation into the content.
Cebu Provincial Board member and physician Stanley Caminero warned that misleading posts from vloggers and social media personalities were swaying parents’ decisions.
“In the age of Facebook, TikTok and YouTube, the wrong message spreads faster than the virus,” he said.
DOH-7 has responded by stepping up barangay-level information campaigns and urging parents to consult health professionals, instead of relying on unverified online claims.
Infant death fuels concerns
The misinformation battle has been complicated by the death of a 7-month-old infant in Dumanjug, Cebu, whose family raised concerns about a possible link to the child’s MR vaccination.
The child was vaccinated on Aug. 10 and died on Aug. 24.
The Dumanjug Municipal Health Office, DOH-7 and the Cebu Provincial Health Office are investigating the case as an adverse event following immunization (AEFI).
But authorities stressed the probe has not established a link between the vaccine and the death. /apl

articles.title: [Newspoint] Sitting for what purpose?
articles.summary: As of this writing, four of the 24 senators are not actually 'sitting for the purpose' intended by the Constitution, as judges in an impeachment trial

blocks.text: As of this writing, four of the 24 senators are not actually 'sitting for the purpose' intended by the Constitution, as judges in an impeachment trial

items: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has sparked extensive debate among lawyers and pundits regarding the constitutional requirement for a two-thirds vote to convict an impeached official.

Mel Sta. Maria argues that the two-thirds requirement should be based on the actual number of senators present and able to vote, rather than the total number of senators, which is affected by absences due to various reasons.

With four senators not participating in the trial, Sta. Maria concludes that the effective threshold for conviction is 14 votes, emphasizing that the Constitution must be interpreted in a way that reflects reality.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

I’ve never seen the law, and anything that could be connected to it, however tenuously, quarreled over so interminably as in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. I guess one ought not to have been surprised. It was something bound to happen on any occasion that collects lawyers, politicians, and pundits.

Being no lawyer or politician myself but just a journalist, although, again, one not exactly invulnerable to the temptations of punditry, I’m careful not to overreach, careful not to weigh in, not without independent expert support, at least. Otherwise, I always proceed from a simple precept in my appreciation of the law — no law has any place in the books that cannot stand on moral grounds and to reason — but still, I try to keep what I think to myself.

That’s why I feel not just affirmed but validated with authority by Mel Sta. Maria in guessing where the impeachment trial might be going. Sta. Maria happens to be a former dean of law and also happens to speak my own language, thus able to make himself clear to me. He has sent me his discussion of the question that matters ultimately: What constitutes the two-thirds vote required to find an impeached official guilty?

Sta. Maria prefaces his communication to me with the applicable constitutional passage: “The Senate shall have the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment. When SITTING FOR THAT PURPOSE, the Senators shall be on oath or affirmation…. No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of ALL MEMBERS OF THE SENATE.” The two capitalized phrases make for the point around which the contention centers — the capitalization is all Sta. Maria’s, as well as all the typographical renderings of the other utterances I ascribe to him in quotation marks.

The position taken opposite Sta. Maria’s — and mine too, as it happens — is that the applicable rule is cast in stone: The guilt of the impeached is decided by 16 votes — 16 being presumed as the absolute, unalterable number that represents “two thirds” of “all members of the Senate” sitting in judgment, in turn presumed to be represented by the absolute, unalterable base number 24.

These representations are plainly contradicted by reality. As of this writing, four of the 24 senators are not actually “sitting for the purpose” intended by the Constitution, as judges in an impeachment trial. Indeed, they are unable to fulfil that duty: one is in hiding as a fugitive from the law, two are in detention on the non-bailable charge of plunder, thus likely sitting in jail while on trial, and one is in France on an indefinite medical leave officially but, being potentially liable for graft, is suspected seeking asylum there.

Argues Sta. Maria: “[The Constitution] DOES NOT state ‘2/3 of all the members of the Senate regardless of his or her inability to be present or to vote.’ While there is a rule that ‘when the law does not distinguish, we should not distinguish,’ this rule must not be used in its absurdity. The Constitution DOES NOT OPERATE BY LEGAL FICTION. It cannot count a physical vote of persons not physically present. Remember: an abstention or non-voting in an impeachment proceeding is the same as a vote for acquittal. To count or even consider what is not there or what was not given is an illusion. The Constitution must be interpreted contextually and legally in light with reality. The base therefore of the 2/3 vote must conform to what is achievable, not desirable.”

He goes on to portray a scenario only too practical and realistic in the not abnormally corrupt Philippine setting: “If 16 is fixed, an official facing impeachment does not need to convince the Senate of their innocence. They only need to convince 9 senators to hide, flee the country, or simply refuse to show up. By rendering themselves absent, those 9 senators effectively cast a vote for acquittal without ever having to sit through the trial, look at the evidence, or face the public. This could not have been the contemplation of the Constitution. The Constitution cannot be interpreted to mean providing the mechanism for its own destruction.
“The use of ‘two-thirds’ instead of ‘16’ is the Constitution’s built-in safety valve. It acknowledges that while the hurdle to convict must always be high, it must never be impossible.”

Finally, Sta. Maria credits Leo Camacho, a professor of constitutional law at the Ateneo, for reminding his fellows of noscitur a sociis. It is a legal maxim, in Latin, whose felicity strikes at the very heart of the matter: “A word is known by the company it keeps.” Pursuing Camacho, Sta. Maria continues: “…words and phrases in the Constitution should not be interpreted in isolation but must be construed in the light of the words and phrases surrounding them. The words, ‘SENATE,’ ‘SITTING FOR THAT PURPOSE,’ ‘ALL MEMBERS OF THE SENATE” must be harmonized.”
At any rate, by his reckoning, with four senators sitting elsewhere than in the impeachment court, the threshold vote for conviction comes down to 14.
Sta. Maria’s full discussion is on Facebook. – Rappler.com

articles.title: AUDIOJUNKIE: No new music this week!
articles.summary: No new music this week! So says my brain as I write this article. True enough there’s absolutely nothing new to be written about at this outing. I actually tried researching. I even bought a copy of…

blocks.text: Dolly Parton (Facebook)
No new music this week!
So says my brain as I write this article.

True enough there’s absolutely nothing new to be written about at this outing. I actually tried researching. I even bought a copy of Mojo magazine because of the cover, which depicted Depeche Mode at a youngish age. Then I realized there’s no new music coming from these UK synth heroes of mine in the past month or anytime soon. Well, there’s “Memento Mori: Mexico City” released in December of last year, so there’s that but no new music.
How about Rush? The Canadian hard rock pioneers are back touring again where guitarist Alex Lifeson and bassist Geddy Lee got together with new drummer Anika Nilles.

Rush’s Fifty Something Tour began in Los Angeles, California and is said to be knee deep in “thrills, deep cuts and tributes to fallen drummer Neil Peart.” Concert goers are enthralled so to speak with the shows at The Forum and is fast becoming the hot ticket tour of 2026.

A customer of mine couldn’t stop talking about Nilles who took every Peart drum fill and wowed everyone who saw Rush at the concerts. Nilles , a German, paired well with Lee and Lifeson, who both seem happy up and about and playing live again. But seeing this as a greatest hits/tribute tour, no new music ever came out of it. But yeah, amazing tour!

How about the news that beloved Dolly Parton passed away? The “Jolene” singer died last Tuesday at the age of 80 after a brief tussle with the big C, leaving her family and a seven-decade career as a global icon and humanitarian.

Parton had many hits, among them “9 to 5”, “Islands in the Stream”, “I Will Always Love You” and even old ones like the Porter Wagoner duets like “Good As Gold”, “One By One,” and “Daddy Was An Old Time Preacher Man.”

While many people knew her through her career as a musician and a movie star, Parton had a literacy program since the 90’s called the Imagination Library, where she donated millions of books to children.

Parton had many memorable albums, but in 2023 she had released The Rockstar Playlist, wherein she had done duets with the likes of Ann Wilson (Heart), Rob Halford (Judas Priest), Sting, Steven Tyler, Peter Frampton, Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr. Parton was a multi-hyphenate in the truest sense of the word and all these artists would attest to that.
Most of these artists will have a memory about Parton, but I guess Miley Cyrus really said something nice about her "fairy godmother" in a rather long quote.

“The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour and between our hearts. What I know is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.”
Definitely no new music comes after that. But just in case, Emmylou Harris, Linda Ronstadt and Parton singing a cover of Neil Young's "After The Goldrush" would fill in the hole.
Next week will be better.

articles.title: DSWD's Gatchalian: Family food packs cost P797, not P1,503
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday clarified that its prepacked family food packs (FFPs) cost P797.80 each, contrary to claims circulating online that each pack costs…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 10:44am

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday clarified that its prepacked family food packs (FFPs) cost P797.80 each, contrary to claims circulating online that each pack costs more than P1,500.

DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said the P1,503.84 figure being cited online refers to the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC), or the ceiling set for the procurement—not the actual amount paid by the government.
“Actually, fake news,” Gatchalian said in an interview on Unang Balita, referring to the claim that each FFP costs P1,503.
He said the P1,503.84 ABC is the maximum amount that may be allocated for the procurement, while the actual award price for the food pack is P797.87.

The Secretary explained that DSWD procurements undergo competitive bidding, with the contract awarded to a supplier that submits the lowest responsive bid (the lowest bid that meets all the requirements) and complies with the agency’s technical specifications.
Thus, Gatchalian said the ABC should not be mistaken for the actual price paid by DSWD for the food packs.
The clarification came after a social media post claimed that a family food pack costs more than P1,500.
The food pack contains:

items: six kilos of rice (vacuum packed),
four canned corned beef,
four canned tuna,
two canned sardines,
five sachets of 3-in-1 instant coffee,
five sachets of powdered choco malt drink

blocks.text: Gatchalian also rejected claims that the contents of the food packs were not fit for consumption.
He said he personally checks the food items included in the packs.
“Walang papasok sa kahon na ’yan na hindi ko personal na natikman o kinain,” Gatchalian said. (Nothing goes into that box that I have not personally tasted or eaten.)
He added that the food items undergo evaluation by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI) of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST).
According to Gatchalian, this ensures that the contents meet the prescribed food safety and nutritional standards and are suitable for inclusion in the food packs distributed to beneficiaries.

The DSWD earlier emphasized that its FFP procurement process includes requirements on the quality and specifications of the food items, with the contents assessed against applicable food safety and nutritional standards. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: On National Heroes Day, senators urge Filipinos to remember their legacy, build a better nation
articles.summary: Senators on Monday, August 31 called on Filipinos to remember the legacy left behind by the country’s heroes and use this as an inspiration to build a better Philippines. Senate President Sherwin…

blocks.text: Senators on Monday, August 31 called on Filipinos to remember the legacy left behind by the country’s heroes and use this as an inspiration to build a better Philippines.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian led the Senate in pushing for this call as the country observes this year’s National Heroes Day.
“As we honor the men and women whose sacrifices secured our freedom, sovereignty, and democracy, let us remember that their legacy calls on us to continue building a better nation,” Gatchalian said.

“Magiging mas makabuluhan ang sakripisyo ng ating mga bayani kung bawat isa sa atin ay maglilingkod sa pamilya, komunidad, at bayan nang may integridad, katapatan, at malasakit (The sacrifice of our heroes will become more meaningful if each of us serves our family, community, and country with integrity, honesty, and compassion),” he further said.

Gatchalian also said the recent problems facing the country should spur Filipinos to do their part in protecting public funds and ensure that every program of the government is sincerely for the benefit of the country.

“Sa gitna ng mga problemang kinakaharap ng bansa — tulad ng pagbaha, korapsyon sa gobyerno, mga hamon sa kalidad ng edukasyon, at mataas na presyo ng pagkain at kuryente — sama-sama nating pangalagaan ang kaban ng bayan at tiyaking bawat programa ng pamahalaan ay maayos, tapat, at tunay na nagsisilbi sa bawat pamilyang Pilipino (Amidst the problems facing the country—such as flooding, government corruption, challenges regarding the quality of education, and the high cost of food and electricity—let us work together to safeguard public funds and ensure that every government program is well-managed, honest, and genuinely serves every Filipino family),” he said.
Real heroes do not ‘ghost’
Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, on the other hand, said this year’s celebration of National Heroes Day should serve as a reminder that real heroes do not ghost.

“Madalas natatapat ang Araw ng mga Bayani sa ghost month — paalala na ang tunay na bayani, hindi nanggo-ghost (National Heroes' Day often falls during the “Ghost Month”—a reminder that a true hero doesn't “ghost”),” Pangilinan said.
The senator further pointed out that the commemoration of National Heroes Day is rooted in acknowledging the collective struggle for freedom that began with the Revolution of 1896.
The annual exercise is a means to pay tribute not only to the renowned heroes found in history books but, above all, to the unsung Filipinos who bravely love their country.
He pointed out that many of these heroes come to the aid of those on the brink of peril, even at the cost of their own health, safety and livelihood.

“Sabi nga nila, not all heroes wear capes. Nandyan lang silang: Mga magulang, marami sa kanila mga overseas Filipino workers (OFWs), na araw-araw nagsasakripisyo upang maitaguyod at mabigyan ng mas magandang kinabukasan ang kanilang pamilya; mga environment defender na nangangalaga sa ating lupa, kagubatan, karagatan, at mga komunidad (As the saying goes, not all heroes wear capes. They are right there among us: Parents—many of whom are OFWs—making daily sacrifices to provide for their families and secure a better future for them; environmental defenders who safeguard our lands, forests, oceans, and communities),” Pangilinan explained.

“Mga magsasaka at mangingisda, na nagpapakain sa bayan, kahit ginigipit ng price manipulators at smugglers; at mga truth-tellers, kasama ang mga saksi sa mga krimen, na naninindigan para sa tama at pananagutan kahit binabantaan o sinusuhulan (Farmers and fisherfolk who feed the nation, even while being exploited by price manipulators and smugglers; and truth-tellers—including witnesses to crimes—who stand up for what is right and for accountability, despite facing threats or offers of bribes),” he stressed.
Pangilinan further hailed as heroes the country’s riders, social workers, health professionals, disaster and emergency response volunteers who braved the recent floods to serve fellow Filipinos.
“Hinarap nila ang panganib para maghatid ng pagkain, gamot, tulong, at kaligtasan. They faced danger to deliver food, medicine, aid, and safety,” he noted.
“‘Yan ang bayaning Pilipino: Hindi nagpapasiil sa hamon ng buhay (That is the Filipino hero: one who does not yield to life's challenges),” he reiterated.

articles.title: Manila police check Mendiola security setup for Heroes’ Day protests
articles.summary: The Manila Police District (MPD) inspected its security preparations at Mendiola, Manila, on Monday, Aug. 31, as various groups hold protests and activities for National Heroes Day. MPD Chief Brig.…

blocks.text: MPD Chief Brig. Gen. Atty. Arnold C. Santiago inspects the security barriers and setup at Mendiola, Manila, during a simulation exercise ahead of National Heroes Day protests on Monday, Aug. 31. (Photo courtesy of the Manila Police District)
The Manila Police District (MPD) inspected its security preparations at Mendiola, Manila, on Monday, Aug. 31, as various groups hold protests and activities for National Heroes Day.
MPD Chief Brig. Gen. Atty. Arnold C. Santiago personally led a simulation exercise and evaluation of the police deployment, barriers, and other security equipment in the area.

The activity was conducted pursuant to the directive of NCRPO Chief Brig. Gen.Christopher N. Abrahano to simulate the installation of metal and concrete barriers and container vans at seven strategic gates or entry points around Malacañang.
Police also monitored the area for possible developments involving protest groups.
Santiago inspected the barriers and strategic security points in Mendiola to assess the positioning of police personnel and equipment and ensure a prompt response to possible incidents.

The MPD said its security preparations would be carried out under the principle of maximum tolerance, with police tasked to maintain peace and order while respecting the public’s right to peaceful assembly and expression.

Police said the simulation and evaluation were intended to ensure the safety of protesters, police personnel, and other members of the public while preventing situations that could lead to confrontation or disorder.
The MPD said it would remain on alert and continue monitoring developments in the area throughout the National Heroes Day activities.
