articles.title: 15 people may be missing after Grand Canyon flash flood, dozens evacuated
articles.summary: A major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S.…

image.caption: This National Park Service photo shows remnants of a destroyed footbridge along Bright Angel Creek in the Grand Canyon following a flash flood on Saturday. (James Thompson/National Park Service/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S. National Park Service said. Saturday's flooding has left the park service seeking information about 15 people who may be missing or unaccounted for.
Popular tourist spots including Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch remained closed on Sunday

A major flash flood at Arizona's Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S. National Park Service said.
The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened Saturday afternoon and has left the park service seeking information about 15 people who may be missing or unaccounted for.
Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and creating what appeared to be a new river rapid.

As the park service tries to account for everyone in the area, it is asking asked anyone with details about people hiking or camping there to get in touch. It said it was working with the Arizona Department of Public Safety to continue evacuations Sunday.
"This is a reminder of what a dynamic and active landscape Grand Canyon is," said Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University.

Popular tourist spots including the Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab trail remained closed on Sunday while park officials surveyed the damage, the park said. Rafting trips on the Colorado River also have been halted for now.

More than 60 people were evacuated from Phantom Ranch, which has a historic canteen and dorms, and is a common spot for rafters to get off and on the river. More evacuations were planned Sunday, the park said. No injuries have been reported.

Erica Viola said she was at Bright Angel campground when the rain started Saturday afternoon, and she and about 50 other hikers watched the creek rise and then debris start to flow by, including what looked like a bunkhouse. The group was taken by helicopter to safety, ending her adventure two days early, she said.
About 1.2 to 2.5 centimetres of rain fell within about 30 minutes in the rocky area where there's a steep drop in elevation, said National Weather Service meteorologist Justin Johndrow in Flagstaff.
"Most of it ran off instantly," Johndrow said.
He said the flooding happened on the north side of the Grand Canyon, where Bright Angel Creek comes from the North Rim down to the Colorado River, dropping around 1,830 metres.
More rain and thunderstorms were possible for the area into Monday.

articles.title: Marcos calls on Filipinos to work toward nation-building, do more than remember heroes
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, August 31, National Heroes' Day, urged Filipinos to do more than remember heroes and to work toward nation-building.

blocks.text: NATIONAL HEROES' DAY
Published August 31, 2026 6:34am
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, August 31, National Heroes' Day, urged Filipinos to do more than remember heroes and to work toward nation-building.
"I am in solidarity with the entire Filipino people in the commemoration of our National Heroes' Day," Marcos said in his message.

"Today, I call on every Filipino to do more than remember our brave national heroes. Let us also renew our solemn duty to carry forward the nation for which they fought and sacrificed. Our forebears won our freedom, defended our dignity, and laid the foundations of the Republic we cherish. We honor them best by embodying their courage, keeping the flame of patriotism alive, and becoming the citizens our country needs," he added.
Marcos said the spirit of national heroes lives on in our countrymen who serve selflessly.

"Their spirit endures in every Filipino who chooses to serve, care, and contribute to a cause greater than oneself. We see it in our soldiers and first responders who risk their lives to keep us safe. We recognize it in our teachers, health workers, farmers, fisherfolk, and overseas Filipinos who sustain our families and communities. We find it in every citizen who helps a neighbor, protects the vulnerable, and works honestly for the common good," the president said.

Marcos then encouraged Filipinos to "continually prove ourselves worthy of the liberty entrusted to us and build a country that generations yet to come will proudly inherit. Let the Bagong Pilipinas we are shaping continue to revere the heroes of the past, present, and future."
"Mabuhay ang ating mga Bayani! Mabuhay ang dakilang lahi ng Pilipino!" he added.
Malacañang earlier declared the last Monday of August — August 31 — as a regular holiday to commemorate National Heroes' Day. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Dizon sacks DPWH exec over delayed flood response
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has relieved a maintenance chief following reports of delayed response to calamities, as heavy rains continued to trigger flooding across…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has relieved a maintenance chief following reports of delayed response to calamities, as heavy rains continued to trigger flooding across Metro Manila and several parts of Luzon.
In an Aug. 29 memorandum, Dizon ordered engineer Loreto Balena Jr. relieved as maintenance chief of the Las Piñas-Muntinlupa District Engineering Office.
Dizon cited Balena’s “unsatisfactory performance, lack of urgency, and delayed response to calamities” as grounds for his removal.
Balena was directed to complete an inventory of his office’s properties, finish and sign pending documents and deliverables, and turn over official records and other papers.

Sen. JV Ejercito, meanwhile, urged the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to complete unfinished flood control projects before starting new ones, saying incomplete infrastructure could worsen the country’s vulnerability to flooding.
“For practical reasons, we need to close the gaps so that mitigating or solving flood control would be effective,” Ejercito, chair of the Senate finance committee, told dzBB on Sunday.

“Close the gaps, complete the unfinished flood control projects. No new projects. Finish what needs to be finished,” he added.Ejercito’s call came amid renewed scrutiny of the government’s multibillion-peso flood control program and concerns over unfinished or poorly implemented projects.

He also pushed for the proposed Masterplan for Infrastructure National Development, which he said would provide a long-term framework for infrastructure planning that would survive changes in administrations.

The proposed measure would integrate flood control with transportation, housing, water, energy, utilities and other major infrastructure, rather than allowing projects to be planned and implemented separately.
Ejercito said the government should prioritize the country’s 10 most flood-prone areas and use a 30- to 50-year framework to guide major infrastructure investments.

He said long-term planning could also strengthen accountability by giving projects clear objectives, timelines and costs and help prevent corruption by ensuring that projects form part of a coherent national plan.
Rain volume
The warnings came as Metro Manila was placed under a red rainfall warning by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) at 12:10 p.m. on Sunday.

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) said the metropolis had 186 millimeters of rain in 23 hours from 9 a.m. on Saturday to 8 a.m. on Sunday, based on data from the Pagasa Science Garden Station in Quezon City. A millimeter of rain amounts to a liter of water on a flat area.
Serious flooding remained possible in low-lying and flood-prone areas.
The MMDA said it was deploying mobile pumps, clearing clogged drains and waterways, dredging and removing debris and garbage from drainage inlets as part of its flood mitigation efforts.
Classrooms damaged
The prolonged rains have also taken a toll on schools.
The Department of Education said 9,869 classrooms had been damaged by the combined effects of the “habagat” (southwest monsoon) and tropical cyclones “Luis,” “Maymay,” “Neneng” and “Obet.”
Of the total, 5,731 classrooms sustained minor damage, 2,055 suffered major damage and 2,083 were totally damaged, according to the latest DepEd situation report as of 8 a.m. Sunday.
Central Luzon had the highest number of affected classrooms and schools, with 3,732, followed by Region I with 2,746 and the Cordillera Administrative Region with 1,266.
DepEd estimated that P280 million would be needed for minor repairs, P1 billion for major repairs and P5.2 billion for reconstruction.
At least 59 schools also experienced flooding, including 47 in Central Luzon. —WITH REPORTS FROM SHERIDAN DELFINO, TINA G. SANTOS, AND ANDREA GREGORIO

articles.title: DPWH stops Taguig reclamation projects
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders on allegedly illegal reclamation projects in Taguig City, Secretary Vince Dizon said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders on allegedly illegal reclamation projects in Taguig City, Secretary Vince Dizon said on Sunday.
Dizon said the orders were served on Aug. 20 following a directive from the Office of the President through the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA), which is under the said office.
“Let’s just discuss and if there is any problem there, then let’s determine the way forward,” Dizon told reporters in an interview after his inspection of the Tumana pumping station in Marikina City.
He added that the orders were “effective immediately,” but he also said his agency did not yet have a list of the projects involved.
Titles questioned
“I think a meeting will be called among different stakeholders, including the City of Taguig plus [Laguna Lake Development Authority] and PRA,” Dizon said.
Earlier this month, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said an investigation by his office has found reclamation activities on Taguig City’s side of Laguna Lake covering at least 85 hectares of land.
He warned that these activities may threaten the Laguna Lake’s ecosystem as garbage meant for the Rizal provincial sanitary landfill may end up there instead.

In a series of posts on X on Saturday, Lacson disclosed that four allegedly “fraudulently” titled parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City have been identified and will be turned over to the Office of the Ombudsman for investigation.
According to Lacson, the lands cover areas ranging from 5,000 to 193,027 square meters. All four were processed through various patent and land registration procedures.
The senator said further there were four other parcels with no plotted titled lots in the Land Registration Authority’s digital records.
‘Cauldron of worms’
Lacson’s probe into Taguig’s infrastructure projects started last month, triggered by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano’s allegations on Facebook live that his net worth had increased twofold.
Lacson fired back, saying he had no budget insertions since he was elected senator, and in turn accused Cayetano of making P6.79-billion insertions in the 2025 General Appropriations Act.
Cayetano has denied all these allegations and said Taguig had no “ghost” projects.
Earlier this month, Lacson said his probe into the Taguig projects uncovered a “cauldron of worms” to include illegal reclamation activities in Laguna Lake.

He claimed these activities, which he linked to the Cayetano political family, had been carried out for years under the guise of flood control and mitigation projects. He also alleged that Cayetano threatened the PRA to stop it from investigating the reclamation works.
He had sought the forfeiture of the reclaimed lakeshore areas in favor of the national government.

The Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya) has expressed support for the investigation into the reclamation activities, saying these were threatening Laguna Lake’s ecosystem and affecting fisherfolk and urban poor communities in Muntinlupa and Taguig cities.
Pamalakaya, a national federation of small-scale fisherfolk organizations in the Philippines, also rejected Cayetano’s claim that the projects were intended to control flooding and protect the lake.
Lacson’s office has identified 32 allegedly anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City since he started his probe. —WITH REPORTS FROM INQUIRER RESEARCH, AND PHILIPPINE NEWS AGENCY

articles.title: Globe Telecom boosts 5G spending to ₱26.3 billion as data demand surges
articles.summary: Globe Telecom Inc. increased capital expenditure by 39 percent in the first half of the year to ₱26.3 billion as the local wireless carrier accelerated network expansion and data infrastructure…

blocks.text: Globe Telecom Inc. increased capital expenditure by 39 percent in the first half of the year to ₱26.3 billion as the local wireless carrier accelerated network expansion and data infrastructure investments to meet growing digital demand.
In a statement, Globe said the spending boost reflects an ongoing strategy anchored on expanding infrastructure capacity while maintaining capital discipline.
Globe reaffirmed its guidance to keep full-year capital outlay below $1 billion, signaling a balanced approach between network execution and balance sheet flexibility.

About 91 percent of the total first-half outlay went into data-related assets, including core digital infrastructure and capacity additions. Capital expenditure represented 31 percent of service revenues during the six-month period.
The carrier broadened its 5G network footprint, expanding outdoor population coverage to more than 98 percent across Metro Manila and key cities in the Visayas and Mindanao regions.
The high-speed wireless service now reaches at least 80 percent of the population in secondary cities nationwide, extending next-generation mobile connectivity beyond traditional urban centers.

“Globe’s continued investments in network infrastructure are about more than expanding capacity; they are about delivering a better everyday experience for our customers,” Globe Chief Executive Officer Carl Cruz said.
He added that the network buildout is intended to bridge the digital divide and support wider economic participation.
The infrastructure push translated into consistent performance metrics, according to network testing firm Ookla.

Data from the second half of 2024 through the first half of 2026 showed Globe winning back-to-back recognitions, including four consecutive titles as the most consistent mobile provider, alongside repeated awards for widest 5G coverage and most consistent home internet service.
Globe expects the focused capital allocation to support long-term revenue growth and operational performance as consumer reliance on mobile data and home broadband accelerates across the archipelago.
The company emphasized that its capital allocation framework will remain focused on critical infrastructure while preserving financial maneuverability in a competitive telecommunications market.

articles.title: Hikers feared missing after flash flooding hits Grand Canyon
articles.summary: More than 20 people are thought to be unaccounted for after flash flooding on Saturday.

blocks.text: More than 20 people are thought to be missing or unaccounted for after flash flooding swept through parts of the Grand Canyon.
It hit at around 14:30 local time (22:30 BST) on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).
Sixty-two people have so far been airlifted out of the area, with more expected to follow. No injuries have been reported.
The NPS said flooding had caused significant damage in some areas and that trails in the area have been closed.

It warned that more thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were forecast for Sunday and Monday, which could lead to "additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions".
The NPS asked anyone who knew of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday to get in touch.
The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular national parks in the US, with about five million people visiting each year. The Bright Angel trail is its most popular hike.
The Phantom Ranch area can only be reached by foot, mule or by rafting the Colorado River, according to Grand Canyon National Park Lodges.

articles.title: CHR: Press freedom remains under threat
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — As the Philippines marked National Press Freedom Day on Sunday, the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) and the Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFoMS) called for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — As the Philippines marked National Press Freedom Day on Sunday, the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) and the Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFoMS) called for stronger safeguards for journalists, citing the country’s 114th ranking in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index of Reporters Without Borders.
In a statement, the CHR warned that press freedom in the Philippines continues to “face serious challenges.”
“The lack of accountability for crimes against media workers perpetuates a dangerous cycle of impunity,” it said as it urged the government to ensure swift justice for victims and their families.
The CHR added that Red-tagging, vilification and other forms of intimidation likewise pose threats to journalists and the public’s right to information.
It cited its National Inquiry on Red-tagging, which found that journalists are frequently targeted for critical reporting on government policies and programs.
The CHR also reiterated its recommendation for legislation that would specifically penalize Red-tagging, saying that it continues to strengthen mechanisms aimed at protecting media workers.

In April, Reporters Without Borders (RSF), an international nongovernment organization that advocates for press freedom, said the Philippines improved from 116th place in 2025 to 114th place this year, although it remains in the lower half of the press freedom index.
The index measures the degree of freedom enjoyed by journalists, news organizations and netizens in 180 countries and the efforts made by authorities to respect this freedom.

The RSF, however, noted that despite its extremely dynamic media landscape, the Philippines remains one of the most dangerous countries in the world for journalists. It cited the Maguindanao massacre in 2009, which left 32 journalists and media workers dead.
The PTFoMS, on the other hand, said that “continuous vigilance and action” is needed in defending press freedom amid threats.

While noting that its efforts have contributed to improved international press freedom rankings and stronger mechanisms for responding to threats against media, it also acknowledged that journalists continue to face challenges, including violence.
The task force called on the public to recognize the vital role of journalists in democracy.
“Let us recommit to fostering an environment where truth prevails over disinformation and where laws protect rather than restrict press freedom,” the PTFoMS said.
Decriminalizing libel
The CHR, meanwhile, reiterated its call to decriminalize libel and cyberlibel, saying journalists should work free from criminal prosecution and undue restrictions.
“Beyond protection mechanisms, laws and policies must foster an environment where journalism can flourish without fear of criminalization or undue restriction,” it said.
The CHR also warned of artificial intelligence and digital technologies being used to surveil journalists, expose sources, suppress dissent and spread disinformation.
At the same time, it urged the government to address impunity and create a safe civic environment free from censorship, intimidation and other threats.
“When journalists are silenced, people lose information necessary to make informed decisions, participate meaningfully in public life, and hold institutions accountable,” the CHR said. /cb

articles.title: Lawmaker: Algorithms put kids at risk online
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A lawmaker warned on Sunday that “increasingly sophisticated” social media algorithms are deliberately hooking users and exposing minors to age‑inappropriate content amid…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A lawmaker warned on Sunday that “increasingly sophisticated” social media algorithms are deliberately hooking users and exposing minors to age‑inappropriate content amid growing concern about online child safety following rising cases of school violence.

“The evolution of social media platforms’ powerful algorithms makes it more and more difficult for adolescents to avoid illicit content—even if that’s not what they were originally searching for,” Las Piñas Rep. Mark Anthony Santos said in a statement.
Social media platforms have been facing mounting global backlash over harmful content and the lack of safety features for users, particularly children.
In the United States, Facebook’s parent company Meta has agreed to pay around $17 billion to over a dozen states to settle a suit accusing it of creating addictive products that harmed young users.

In the Philippines, a series of violent incidents in schools, most recently two shootings separately carried out by students that left five other students dead and scores more wounded, has prompted authorities to look into the possible influence of violent online games and “groomers” on the perpetrators.

“If we know that these platforms can influence what our children see, think and eventually do, then government has a responsibility to make sure that influence does not become a gateway to exploitation, addiction or illegal drugs,” Santos said.
He added that drug syndicates are also exploiting online platforms to reach potential victims.
“They can exploit digital platforms, fake identities, private messaging and algorithm-driven content to reach potential victims, including young people,” Santos said.
Last week, a Philippine delegation met in Singapore with Meta officials who pledged to work with the government to improve coordination and act on harmful content. /cb

articles.title: Furor in PLM campus over honorary degree to Marcos
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Students of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) have questioned the university’s decision to confer an honorary Doctor of Laws degree on President Marcos and warned that…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Students of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) have questioned the university’s decision to confer an honorary Doctor of Laws degree on President Marcos and warned that it could be seen as an endorsement of an administration facing good governance issues.

In a joint statement on Saturday evening, PLM’s Supreme Student Council, along with 33 other local student councils and organizations, criticized the resolution of the board of regents (BOR), the highest policymaking body of the university, to award the degree to Marcos.

“To bestow such an honor upon a sitting President whose administration remains subject to serious questions concerning transparency, accountability, human rights, and public service risks turning an academic distinction into an endorsement of a record that remains deeply contested,” the student groups said.
“For an institution that prides itself on Karunungan, Kaunlaran, at Kadakilaan, such recognition must be held to a standard higher than political position or institutional convenience,” they added.
They said they were not consulted on the matter.
Marcos received the honorary degree on Aug. 27 during graduation rites at the city government-run university.

The university cited the President’s support, particularly for the construction of the PLM Allied Health Sciences Building, through the conversion and retrofitting of the old Ospital ng Maynila facility. Marcos himself attended the groundbreaking ceremony of the building in February.
Memory of activist

In questioning the decision, the groups invoked the memory of Liliosa Hilao, a PLM student journalist who was the first reported case of a student activist who died in detention during martial law under the Marcos Sr. dictatorship.
Hilao, 23, was allegedly tortured after she was abducted by Philippine Constabulary troopers in 1973.

“Her story, together with the lives of countless others who suffered, were silenced, and were taken during that dark chapter of our history, must never be forgotten or erased,” the PLM students said. “More so, we must never forget to honor our own blood—a fellow Haribon who, like many others, became a victim of the same regime.”

In a separate statement on Sunday, the PLM College of Law Student Council called for clarification on the conferment of the degree to Marcos “in the interest of preserving the trust and credibility of PLM and the distinctions it confers.”

It asked if the PLM board of regents, as well as the Legal Education Board (LEB), determined whether Marcos’ academic credentials had satisfied the educational qualification under LEB Memorandum Order No. 033, series of 2025.
Section 4(d) of that order states that a prospective honoree need not be a lawyer or a law graduate but must have at least a baccalaureate degree or its equivalent from a reputable institution.
Credentials

While Marcos had claimed that he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Philosophy, Politics and Economics from the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, the university maintained that, based on its records, he did not complete his degree but was awarded a Special Diploma in Social Studies in 1978.

He admitted that he was not able to complete his Masters in Business Administration course at Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania after enrolling in 1979 because he was elected Ilocos Norte vice governor in 1980.
In 2023, Marcos also revealed that he did not finish his special diploma course in economics at the University of Asia and the Pacific in Pasig City.
‘Grateful recognition’
PLM’s BOR chair Edward Serapio has acknowledged the criticisms.

“I stand by the principle that the honor was conferred in grateful recognition of the President’s support for education and for the construction of the PLM Medicine and Allied Sciences Building,” Serapio said in a statement on Saturday.
“The intention was to acknowledge this tangible contribution that advances learning and strengthens opportunities for our students,” he added.
Serapio was among the founding partners of the now-defunct MOST Law Office alongside first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos. /cb

articles.title: Remembering Magsaysay: Greatness of spirit in service of Asian peoples
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Today, Aug. 31, the new set of recipients of the Ramon Magsaysay (RM) Award, Asia’s most prestigious prize, will be announced. The winners will be recognized for greatness of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Today, Aug. 31, the new set of recipients of the Ramon Magsaysay (RM) Award, Asia’s most prestigious prize, will be announced.
The winners will be recognized for greatness of spirit they have demonstrated through the outstanding service they have been and are doing for Asian countries and peoples.

The event marks the 119th birth anniversary of the seventh President of the Philippines after whom the award is named. It is meant to honor and perpetuate the memory of the man who devoted his life to serving his country and people, especially the underprivileged and underserved.
Magsaysay’s devotion to the Philippines and Filipinos began even before he entered politics. He was a soldier and, later, guerrilla leader during World War II (WWII).
After the war, he pursued his commitment to help ordinary Filipinos achieve a better life through public service.
Soldier, peacemaker
Magsaysay was among those who turned “swords into plowshares (the sharp steel blade at the bottom of the plow),” as the biblical phrase from prophets Isaiah and Micah in the Old Testament goes.
The popular saying literally means turning weapons into tools for growing food.

He was a warrior, a leader of guerrillas fighting the Japanese in his home province of Zambales during the war, who became a peacemaker as defense secretary in the administration of President Elpidio Quirino. He had the task of taking back into the fold disenchanted Filipinos who felt left out after the war and rebelled against the government.
Magsaysay, the youngest to be elected to the highest office in the country, pursued a two-pronged strategy in pursuing a peaceful resolution to the insurgency.

People who were using violence were met with force but Magsaysay also pursued programs to persuade those opposing the government to drop their weapons and resume their peaceful existence. He leveraged his experience as a regular working man before the war and procurer of supplies for his guerrilla unit (his code name was the self-explanatory “Chow”) during the war to connect with ordinary citizens.
Public life
His stint as secretary of defense earned him credibility and respect to get elected president of the Philippines, which was rebuilding after the devastation of WWII.
As president, he would continue his campaign to help the masses so they would be less inclined to take up arms against the government.

Magsaysay was one of many WWII combatants who were thrust into politics after the end of the war. His sterling performance as a guerrilla leader launched the political career of the president who would be known as The Guy and Man of the Masses.

While some claimed credit for getting RM into politics, the President, according to “The Magsaysay Story” by Carlos P. Romulo and Marvin M. Gray, declared “without any hesitation” that Col. Gyles Merrill, an American military officer who stayed behind after Gen. Douglas MacArthur left, was “instrumental in urging him into public life.”

In 1945, upon MacArthur’s return, the general, dubbed by writer William Manchester as the American Caesar, asked Merrill to submit nominees for the post of military governor of Zambales. “The chosen man must be acquainted with the terrain, capable, honest, careful of details and, above all, liked and trusted by both civilians and soldiers.”
Merrill submitted only one name—Ramon Magsaysay.
Courage and selflessness

When Gen. Charles Hall informed Magsaysay of his appointment, he told the future president, “Colonel Merrill has recommended you as honest, courageous and patriotic. My own investigations bear this out.”
RM was inducted as military governor of Zambales on Feb. 4, 1945.

The friendship between Magsaysay and Merrill remained strong even after the American returned to the United States. In 1948, then Zambales’ representative in Congress, Magsaysay visited his wartime buddy in Texas.
Merrill, according to Romulo and Gaye, told the would-be president: “It’s well enough to be a congressman, but take my advice, it’s better to be in the Cabinet.”
RM would visit his old friend again four years later. By this time, Magsaysay was secretary of national defense.
Today, a new group of outstanding individuals who have demonstrated courage and selflessness in the service of the country and people will be recognized. /cb

articles.title: PSA: Luzon still dominates Top 10 local economies in 2025
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The country’s 10 largest local economies in 2025 were still dominated by cities and provinces in Luzon, with the exception of last placer, Davao City, according to the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The country’s 10 largest local economies in 2025 were still dominated by cities and provinces in Luzon, with the exception of last placer, Davao City, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).

Four highly urbanized cities in the top 10 were located in the National Capital Region (NCR), while three provinces came from the Calabarzon region and two from Central Luzon, according to the 2025 Full-Year Official Poverty Statistics released by the PSA on Aug. 26.

Quezon City retained its position as the Philippines’ biggest local economy in 2025, accounting for 6 percent (P1.4 trillion) of the gross domestic product (GDP), up from P1.3 trillion a year earlier.
Makati followed with a 5.5-percent share of the national economy, rising to P1.27 trillion from P1.204 trillion in 2024.
Laguna province ranked third with a 4.9-percent share, as its economy expanded to P1.14 trillion from P1.08 trillion a year earlier.
Manila, the country’s capital, placed fourth, accounting for 4.6 percent of national GDP, with its economy growing to P1.06 trillion from P1.039 trillion in 2024.
These four localities maintained their rankings from the previous year and remained the only local economies to generate more than P1 trillion worth of goods and services.
Cavite province ranked fifth, with its economy at P875.67 billion in 2025.
Taguig, the fourth city from NCR, climbed to eighth place from ninth place in 2024 with P686.68 billion or 2.96 percent of the country’s GDP.

Ranking sixth, seventh, and ninth were the Calabarzon province of Batangas (with P713.22 billion or 3.1 percent of GDP) and the Central Luzon provinces of Bulacan (P694.81 billion or 2.99 percent of GDP) and Pampanga (P627.89 billion or 2.7 percent of GDP).
Davao City, replacing last placer Baguio in the 2024 list, stood at P601.68 billion, accounting for 2.6 percent of GDP.
Fast-growing economies
PSA data also showed 76 of the country’s 82 provinces and all 33 highly urbanized cities posting year-on-year growth in 2025.

Occidental Mindoro emerged last year as the country’s fastest-growing local economy, after recording the only double-digit growth among all these areas at 11.2 percent—accelerating sharply from its 2.1-percent growth in 2024.
Capiz followed Occidental Mindoro as the second-fastest growing local economy with an 8.7-percent growth rate.

Maguindanao del Sur in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao came next at 8.63 percent, followed by Antique in Western Visayas at 8.55 percent and Davao del Norte in the Davao Region at 8.3 percent.
Poverty incidence
In terms of poverty incidence, Northern Samar—among the provinces that had been lagging in the national economy—dropped to a new record-low of 12.5 percent in 2025.
Its family poverty incidence dropped anew, this time by 9.3 percentage points from 21.8 percent in 2023 and by 6.8 percentage points from 19.3 percent in 2021.
The PSA said this decline since 2023 is statistically significant as it lifts the province out of areas with poverty rates of at least 20 percent.
Northern Samar ranked the fourth lowest among the six provinces in Eastern Visayas in terms of family poverty incidence.
Southern Leyte posted the lowest rate at 3.4 percent, followed by Biliran at 7.8 percent and Leyte at 12.4 percent.
Northern Samar’s 12.5 percent was slightly below the regional rate of 12.8 percent.
Samar recorded 15.7 percent, while Eastern Samar had the highest at 20 percent.
Threshold

The latest figures also moved Northern Samar from Group 4 to Group 5 in the PSA’s provincial poverty classification. Group 5 covers provinces with family poverty incidence of at least 10 percent but below 20 percent.
In 2023, Northern Samar was classified under Group 4, covering provinces with poverty incidence of at least 20 percent but below 30 percent.
This improvement came even as Northern Samar’s annual per-capita poverty threshold increased to P36,451—up from P33,472 in 2023.
The threshold indicates the amount considered necessary to meet basic food and non-food needs increased.
For a family of five, the latest figure is equivalent to an annual threshold of about P182,255, or P15,188 per month.

The provincial government said the latest figures showed a “strong foundation” for sustaining and expanding its poverty-reduction programs—including livelihood and employment, community-based enterprises, improved access to basic services, and targeted interventions for communities where poverty remains concentrated.

Northern Samar Rep. Edwin Ongchuan also welcomed the PSA report, saying the province’s performance was due to the combined efforts of farmers, fisherfolk, the local governments, national government agencies, and development partners. /cb

articles.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
articles.summary: Iran says the attack killed some civilians and is the first known US strike on Iran since late July.

blocks.text: Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global shipping.
Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (£1.5m) to cross.

Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields".
Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said.

Trump ​said last week that all mines‌ placed in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran as part of its efforts to blockade the route had been detonated or removed. He said Iran had been warned that any ship ​or boat deploying new mines would be ​destroyed.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described Trump's claim as a "propaganda" deception.
Iran is facing renewed economic pressure after Washington announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies.

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Iran war has now crossed its six-month mark.
Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel through before the war began.

articles.title: USDA reportedly shelves cyclospora research amid relocations and fund cuts
articles.summary:
Trump officials shuttering three projects on foodborne parasite, two defunded by Congress, Politico reports

The Trump…

blocks.text: The Trump administration is shuttering ⁠two of the three US Department of Agriculture research projects studying cyclospora after the foodborne parasite has ⁠sickened tens of thousands of Americans during the summer, Politico reported on Sunday.

The two projects were defunded by Congress earlier in the year, while the third is ⁠due to be moved in coming months from Maryland to Iowa as part of a broader USDA reorganization, according to the ⁠report.

Although the third project remains funded, all scientists working on the ​parasite have declined to relocate ‌to Iowa, Politico reported, citing ‌people familiar with the plans and internal documents.
Reuters could not immediately ‌verify the report.
“None of the research has been disrupted, and research will continue without disruption,” a USDA spokesperson said, while pointing to Congress over the funding cuts.

Congress did not appropriate funding for the two research projects that were being undertaken at the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center ‌outside Washington DC for the 2026 fiscal year in the Agriculture Appropriations Act, the spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The spokesperson ​added that the Agricultural Research Service is working with research leaders to ensure an orderly transition of the programs.
Scientists researching foodborne parasites, including cyclospora, are retiring or leaving the USDA’s ARS rather than relocating or being reassigned to ⁠other projects, the report said.

The Centers for Disease ​Control and Prevention has ​recorded more than 17,000 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases across 48 states ​plus Washington DC, from 1 May to 24 August, making ​it one ​of the largest foodborne illness outbreaks in recent US history.
At least 11,844 additional cases may require further investigation and analysis, the CDC said.

More than 3,000 people are believed missing after flash floods triggered by a massive glacier collapse in the Himalayas on Wednesday engulfed Gyirong port on the Nepal-China border.

double quotation markThere has been about eight power stations that have been affected as well, so it’s very difficult to get into the area.

articles.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak island amid strait of Hormuz tensions
articles.summary:
US says attack was response to ⁠Revolutionary Guards preparing rockets to launch sea mines into strait

US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran’s Larak island on Sunday, a US…

blocks.text: US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran’s Larak island on Sunday, a US official said, marking the ⁠first known American strikes since late July.

“I can confirm that earlier today US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak island. Islamic ⁠Revolutionary Guards Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait of Hormuz,” the official said.
Iran’s ⁠Revolutionary Guards said the attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens and ​would be met with a “response ‌and punishment” from ‌Tehran, Iranian state media reported.
A spokesperson said the US would pay for the attack on both economic and military fronts, according to the semi-official news agency Fars.
Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency reported the US had carried out ‌a drone strike on the island.

US president Donald Trump said last week that all mines had been detonated or removed from the international waters of the strait of Hormuz and Iran had been told that any ship or boat placing new mines will be destroyed.
The last known ‌US strikes on Iran were in late July and the war has reached a stalemate in recent weeks, with Washington threatening ​to impose costly sanctions on countries that support Iran.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February and Iran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. The Iran war has now ⁠crossed its six-month mark.
US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on ​Lebanon have killed thousands ​and displaced millions. Eighteen US service ​members have been killed in the conflict.
The war has ​led to the ‌blockade of the ​strait of ​Hormuz, which before the conflict accounted for the transit of about a fifth of the world’s oil barrels consumed.

articles.title: Water shortage hits 1,500 Agusan homes
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Over the past 30 years, the once-degraded 1,658-hectare Mt. Magdiwata has gradually been covered with lush forest vegetation. But the green cover has not…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Over the past 30 years, the once-degraded 1,658-hectare Mt. Magdiwata has gradually been covered with lush forest vegetation. But the green cover has not been enough to ensure a steady water supply as the ongoing El Niño reduces rainfall in the area.

At least 1,500 households have experienced limited or no tap water since the end of July, with elevated portions of three poblacion barangays and neighboring Barangay Alegria among the hardest hit, according to the San Francisco Water District (SFWD).
The rehabilitated forests of Mt. Magdiwata help slow runoff, allowing rainwater to seep into the ground and replenish the watershed.

But weeks of below-normal rainfall have severely reduced the watershed’s stored water volume. Elmer Luzon, SFWD general manager, said rainfall at Mt. Magdiwata dropped sharply during the first three weeks of July, reducing the watershed’s yield.
Villager Regnar Gador Edrabel criticized the lack of a permanent solution to the city’s recurring water problems.

“We are always staying awake waiting for the water,” he wrote on social media. Engineer Leonilo Tandog Jr., chief of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, said the local government plans to acquire a water filtration truck.

Tandog said the municipal government has been conducting water rationing in coordination with the SFWD. Mauro Bravo Jr., a retired public works district engineer, has proposed building a large water-impounding facility in the upper portion of Mt. Magdiwata to capture rainwater. —CHRIS V. PANGANIBAN

articles.title: Cordillera body pushed to oversee all rice terraces
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines —Cordillera technocrats are pushing to revive a regional governing body for the preservation of the country’s rice terraces, as calls grow for a comprehensive master plan to…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines —Cordillera technocrats are pushing to revive a regional governing body for the preservation of the country’s rice terraces, as calls grow for a comprehensive master plan to protect the World Heritage-listed landscape from abandonment, climate change and deteriorating infrastructure.

The Cordillera Regional Development Council is studying a draft resolution urging President Marcos to establish a Cordillera Rice Terraces Commission, which would oversee the conservation of rice terraces across the region.

The proposed commission would replace the Ifugao Rice Terraces Commission, which was created in 1994 to oversee the preservation and restoration of the terraces but was abolished in 1999. Its responsibilities were later transferred to the Banaue Rice Terraces Task Force, which was dissolved in 2002, leaving the provincial government of Ifugao to take the lead in conservation efforts.
The proposed body would also cover rice terraces outside Ifugao, including those in Mountain Province.

The Batad, Bangaan, Mayoyao, Hungduan and Nagacadan rice terraces in Ifugao were collectively inscribed on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization World Heritage List in 1995.

The terraces remain notable for their indigenous engineering, in which water collected from forested areas at the upper portions of the mountains is channeled through traditional irrigation systems to successive rice paddies, locally called “payao.”

“The establishment of the Cordillera Rice Terraces Commission is crucial for stopping the deterioration of the terraces,” the draft resolution says. It adds that the body could help revitalize indigenous knowledge and sustainable farming practices while enabling younger generations to continue traditional agriculture.
Master plan

The proposal comes as urban planner and architect Felino Palafox recently pitched to Malacañang a comprehensive master plan for Banaue and other municipalities where the Ifugao rice terraces are located.

During a meeting with Marcos last week, Palafox offered to prepare a Comprehensive Urban, Environmental, Infrastructure, and Economic Development Master Plan for Banaue and the Rice Terraces Municipalities of Ifugao.
His proposal goes beyond repairing damaged terrace walls and irrigation systems, focusing also on the terraces’ role in the local economy and the engineering interventions needed to preserve them.
It argues that the terraces are deteriorating partly because the communities maintaining them can no longer earn enough from farming to sustain their livelihoods.

Palafox estimated that 25 percent to 35 percent of the terraces have been abandoned or irreversibly damaged, citing population decline and environmental pressures, including extreme weather that has damaged the ancient stone and earthen terrace walls.

The proposal, cosigned by the Ifugao provincial government and Polish entrepreneur Maciej Podhajski, also cited low farm incomes as a reason residents leave the province, threatening the workforce needed to maintain the terraces.
Palafox placed the typical farmer’s annual income at about P50,000, which he described as insufficient to sustain a livelihood.
Ifugao officials have been reviewing the proposal and have yet to make their comments public.
Protecting culture
Former Ifugao Rep. Teodoro Baguilat Jr. said any master plan must address the needs of the communities that continue to maintain the terraces and grow heirloom rice.
“We must protect and nurture the watershed,” Baguilat said.
He said the government should subsidize farmers and provide livelihood support, rehabilitate irrigation systems and strengthen programs that preserve indigenous knowledge.
Ifugao communities follow a traditional rice culture that governs planting schedules and the maintenance of the terraces.
Baguilat also called for mechanisms that would allow farmers and local communities to benefit from tourism revenues generated by the terraces.

Often described as 2,000 years old, the Ifugao terraces have been the subject of archaeological research suggesting that some of the structures may have been built or significantly expanded only several hundred years ago, possibly in response to pressures brought by Spanish expansion into the Cordillera.
The terraces remain a living agricultural landscape, sustained not only by stone and earth structures but also by indigenous knowledge and communal practices passed down through generations.

Ifugao had a population of 208,668, according to the latest available census data. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that in 2024, the province was the second-fastest growing economy in the Cordillera, accounting for 7.5 percent of the region’s gross domestic product, estimated at P28.24 billion.

The proposed commission and master plan are aimed at addressing the intertwined challenges of conservation, livelihood, tourism and climate resilience—while keeping the terraces a living part of Ifugao culture rather than simply preserving them as a heritage site. /cb

articles.title: ‘Habagat’ leaves 16 dead in Central Luzon
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, ZAMBALES, Philippines — At least five more people died, and four remained missing in separate incidents across Central Luzon amid days of relentless southwest monsoon or “habagat” rains…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, ZAMBALES, Philippines — At least five more people died, and four remained missing in separate incidents across Central Luzon amid days of relentless southwest monsoon or “habagat” rains that triggered floods, landslides and strong currents, bringing the region’s death toll to 16 in less than a week.

In Zambales, the body of pregnant Aeta woman Arryn Paanan Liwanag, 26, was recovered from Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino on Sunday, four days after a boat carrying 13 Aetas capsized. Her recovery brought the lake tragedy’s death toll to nine, with four survivors.

Two other passengers, children Chandnea Serrano Dela Cruz, 3, and Anqelito Serrano Liwanag, 8, were recovered on Saturday. The group had traveled to Barangay Buhawen for a vaccination program and a 4Ps meeting when their boat encountered strong winds and rough waters.
Two men also drowned in separate incidents in Zambales earlier in the week, while two workers died after being buried in a landslide at the Tipo High-Tech Park in Subic Bay Freeport on Saturday.
In Olongapo City, the body of a 3-year-old boy who was swept away by floodwaters was recovered at the Subic Bay Boardwalk on Sunday, a day after he went missing in Old Cabalan.
Evacuation
More than 16,000 residents in Zambales and Olongapo had evacuated their flooded homes as of Sunday.
In Pampanga, 25-year-old Reiner Novero died after falling into a flooded open drainage canal in Angeles City. His body was recovered about 2 kilometers downstream.
A 70-year-old Aeta man also died in a landslide in Porac town on Friday.
Flooding affected 317 of Pampanga’s 505 barangays, with water reaching up to 2.74 meters (9 feet) in low-lying areas.

In Tarlac City, four people remained missing after an SUV plunged into a river when the Agana Bridge collapsed on Saturday night. Nathaniel Dion, 20, was rescued, while authorities continued searching for the four others.

The Agana Bridge had served as an alternative route after the Aquino Bridge collapsed on Friday night amid heavy rains. —REPORTS FROM JOANNA ROSE AGLIBOT, JUN MALIG, MADELLE CALAYAG, AND TONETTE T. OREJAS

articles.title: 39 kg of bread dumped in park roadside in Japan
articles.summary: JAPAN — A total of 39 kilograms of bread was recently dumped along a roadside in a national park in western Japan, prompting police to investigate who discarded it and why. The loaves were left near…

blocks.text: JAPAN — A total of 39 kilograms of bread was recently dumped along a roadside in a national park in western Japan, prompting police to investigate who discarded it and why.

The loaves were left near guardrails in Daisen-Oki National Park in Tottori Prefecture between Aug. 14 and 20. The incident has prompted the spread of fake images and videos attempting to link the dumping to a sharp increase in bear encounters in Japan over the past year.
“When I first heard of the reports, my head was full of question marks,” said Koji Iwaihara, director of the Natural Parks Foundation’s Tottori branch.
The bread was initially believed to have been used as bait for cameras livestreaming images of animals, but no such equipment was found.
The foundation later came to believe the bread had been left to feed animals after 1.3 kilograms of chicken was found in the same area.
Bear bait?
Bread was also found scattered around the prefecture’s Hakuto coast, but the brand appears to be different from that found in the national park.
Neither the bread nor the chicken was poisoned.
The prefecture has since installed security cameras in Daisen-Oki National Park, but no further dumping has been reported.

“I don’t understand why it was left on the side of the road” as opposed to inside the mountain, said Tottori Gov. Shinji Hirai, questioning the theory that the food may have been placed there as bear bait.
If that really is the aim, “it may become a dangerous precedent as bears become accustomed to the taste of bread,” he added.
Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated videos and images showing a bear looking at or eating the bread have spread on social media.
The prefectural government plans to ask social media platforms to remove them over concerns the false content could cause reputational damage.
Prefectural police said the perpetrator may have violated a law against illegal dumping or regulations governing national parks. /cb

  • 35-year-old aiming to win second Super Bowl in…

blocks.text: Aaron Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, is coming out of retirement to rejoin his only professional team, the Los Angeles Rams.

During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32.

The 35-year-old returns to a stacked Rams roster who were already betting favorites to win the Super Bowl this season. The team includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback and the reigning defensive player of the year, Myles Garrett, who Los Angeles acquired in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June.
ESPN reports that Donald will earn $20m in his one-year deal, which could rise to $30m with bonuses.

Rumors had circulated that Donald would return after the trade for Garrett. If Donald can replicate anything close to the form he showed during his peak – when he was arguably the greatest defensive tackle of all time – he will form part of a formidable line with Garrett, who set the NFL single-season sack record in 2025.

Donald, who was listed at 6ft 1in and 280 lbs when he retired, is small for a defensive tackle but during his first spell with the Rams he made up for his lack of size with his extraordinary athleticism and work rate. He ended his career with a franchise record 111 sacks.

If the Rams do reach the Super Bowl this season, they will play on home turf at SoFi Stadium, the venue for their championship victory in February 2022. The Rams start their season on 10 September against their NFC West rivals, the San Francisco 49ers.
