articles.title: Tarriela proud as Occidental Mindoro sheds 'brown out capital' tag, records economic boom
articles.summary: Formerly saddled with the unenviable tag of "brown out capital of the Philippines", Occidental Mindoro has now emerged as the country’s top performing local economy. Occidental Mindoro lone district…

blocks.text: Formerly saddled with the unenviable tag of "brown out capital of the Philippines", Occidental Mindoro has now emerged as the country’s top performing local economy.
Occidental Mindoro lone district Rep. Leody “Odie” Tarriela highlighted this after the province posted a double-digit economic growth of 11.2 percent.
The figure was reflected in the 2025 Economic Performance Report released by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) last Aug. 28.

“Mula sa pagiging 'brown out capital' tungo sa pinakamalaking pag asenso ang ekonomiya. Totoong sa pagtutulungan at pagsusumikap, maaring makakamit ang kaunlaran na inaaasam,” said the second-term solon.
(From being the “brownout capital” to having the biggest economic growth. It is true that through cooperation and hard work, the development we aspire to can be achieved.)
While detailed sectoral drivers for this growth are yet to be released, one of the perceived key driver is the resolution of the province's power crisis.

Oriental Mindoro gained the distinction brown out capital no thanks to its chronic, prolonged, and at times unscheduled power interruptions. These outages sometimes affected the entire mainland, including towns like Sablayan, Mamburao, Paluan, and Santa Cruz.

Tarriela had endeavored to resolve Occidental Mindoro’s persistent power issues since becoming congressman. He consistently coordinated with various agencies such as Department of Energy (DOE), Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), National Electrification Administration (NEA) and the National Power Corporation (Napocor).
He was also steadfast in cracking the whip with the local power distributor, the Occidental Mindoro Electric Cooperative (OMECO), and its power suppliers.

“Ang naging game changer sa ating pagresolba ng issue ng kuryente sa Oksi ay ang pamamagitan ng ating Kagalang galang na Pangulong Ferdinand “Bong-Bong” Marcos, Jr. Dahil sa kanyang personal na pagtutok, natuldukan ang perennial na issue ng brown out sa probinsya,” noted Tarriela.

(The game changer in resolving the power issue in Occidental Mindoro was the intervention of our Honorable President Ferdinand “Bong-Bong” Marcos, Jr. Because of his personal attention to the matter, the province’s perennial brownout problem was finally put to an end.)

With the establishment of new power infrastructures came the large infusion of capital into the local economy during the past years, he said. These were primarily through investments of both the government and private firms to key sectors such as agriculture, power, transport and infrastructure.
For the year 2025 alone, Occidental Mindoro surpassed other agencies and overtook the country’s 4.4 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth.

“Sa tulong na ating pambansang pamahalaan, nakapagpagawa tayo ng mga proyektong inprastraktura sa Oksi, gaya ng mga kalsada, tulay, ospital, eskuwelahan, pier at iba pa,” added Tarriela, the chairperson of the House Committee on MSME Development.
(With the assistance of our national government, we were able to undertake infrastructure projects in Occidental Mindoro, such as roads, bridges, hospitals, schools, piers, and others.)
Solar power plant

The improvement in the power situation continues with the establishment of a 7.4-megawatt (MW) solar power plant in San Jose town. The public infrastructure investments was matched by privately constructed cold storage facilities, batch mix plants, diagnostic centers/hospitals, schools and shipyards.
These fueled the economic activity of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It created job opportunities for local workers. It increased the purchasing power of consumers.
Even tourism contributed to the economic growth. With stable electricity and increased road and transport networks, accessibility to tourist sites and destinations became easier.

"The province’s strong 2025 economic performance shows that resolution of the longstanding power crisis, paired with national government investments, can drive private sector participation," Tarriela said.
"When matched with strong local MSME involvement and support from local governments, local economies can transform and improve for the benefit of the general population," he further said.

articles.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides — but it could backfire
articles.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used…

image.caption: Using drones to spray pesticides is common in other parts of the world — for example on this rice field in ChinaImage: CFOTO/IMAGO

blocks.text: In theory, the idea doesn't sound bad: Instead of using tractors to spray large quantities of pesticides over fields, drones could precisely spray herbicides, fungicides and insecticides only where they are actually needed.

The plan would be to scan a field, identify affected areas and treat them selectively — significantly reducing pesticide use, according to the European Union's Omnibus X legislative package, which aims to simplify EU food and feed safety rules. After all, the bloc aims to halve the use of chemicals for plant protection by 2030.

Until now, however, the EU had a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air over agricultural land. Exceptions applied only to difficult-to-work terrain, such as steep vineyard slopes. Omnibus X is now set to change that. In May, the European Council gave the legislative package the green light.
Drone use doesn't automatically mean less pesticides

"I think it makes sense in principle to distinguish spray drones from conventional aerial application from a regulatory perspective," said Thomas Daum, an agricultural economist and human ecologist at the School of Global Studies at the University of Gothenburg. Daum studies new technologies and their impact on agriculture. Compared with an airplane or helicopter, he said drones can generally spray more precisely.
How toxic is the industry behind pesticides?

However, Daum also cautioned that "the drone itself does not save any pesticide." He sees potential for using drones to respond more selectively to pest infestations — and thus reduce overall pesticide use. Another advantage for farmers could be the ability to respond quickly to an infestation "even when soils are wet or in difficult-to-access terrain."

"At the same time, this flexibility lowers the barriers to treatment and could therefore also lead to spraying being carried out more frequently overall," Daum said. This could result in a technological lock-in — meaning that more efficient application could reinforce dependence on chemical crop protection.
Omnibus X aims to save administrative costs, cash
Chemical pesticides have been cause for concern for many researchers. Omnibus X is intended not only to make it easier to use spray drones, but also to change the way pesticides are approved.

When the European Council approved Omnibus X in May, a group of researchers from 27 European research institutions voiced strong criticism. Among them was Carsten Brühl, a biologist at the Institute for Environmental Sciences at the Rheinland-Pfalz Technical University of Kaiserslautern-Landau. Brühl, who studies the effects of pesticides on the environment, called Omnibus X a "deregulation package" and is deeply alarmed by it.

To date, pesticide active substances have generally been approved at the EU level for a period of 10 years. Once that period expires, manufacturers can apply for renewed approval and must once again submit data on the safety of the active substance. Since this review process was introduced in 2011, it has resulted in 59 active substances not being reapproved, as they were deemed harmful to human health and the environment.

The main aim of the Omnibus X package is to cut administrative costs, reduce bureaucracy and "ensure fair treatment for companies while safeguarding fair competition within the internal market [...]," according to an EU press release.
Researchers warn Omnibus X could harm people, environment

European scientists have been critical of the EU proposal to cut red tape and deregulate the industry, because it could lead to many active substances being approved indefinitely, eliminating regular reassessments. They also say the transition periods after an approval expires would be extended from 18 months to three years.

Brühl called the idea "reckless." It would mean that even active substances suspected of being harmful to human health could remain on the market — like weedkiller glyphosate, for example, which has been linked to cancer in humans.
Bayer wins in US court, but at what cost to public health?

But the precautionary principle should apply, Brühl argued. This political principle holds that potential harm to people and nature should be prevented proactively, even when there is not yet conclusive scientific evidence.

The scientific evidence on pesticides is already incomplete. The risks posed by an active substance are inferred from the results of laboratory studies, Brühl said. But how that substance actually behaves over the long term under different environmental conditions and in combination with other pesticides is unclear at the time of approval. That is why regular reassessments are so important.

Brühl now fears Omnibus X could undermine scientific interest in studying these active substances. It would be unappealing for researchers "to engage with a system that can no longer be influenced anyway," he said.
Agriculture can work without pesticides

Brühl is certain the new EU legislation will not lead to lower pesticide use — not even with the help of drones and more targeted spraying. This approach, for example, does not work at all with fungicides, he pointed out. Fungicides combat fungal infections and have to be applied preventively because once a plant has become infected, it can no longer be saved.

But Brühl stressed there is another way: doing without pesticides entirely, through what is known as "integrated pest management." And this isn't some hippie eco-fantasy, but rather a concept for the sustainable management of harmful organisms enshrined in German law in 2012.
Pesticides banned in Europe linked to bees deaths in Kenya

Shortly after the European Council gave the green light to Omnibus X and its new rules on drones and pesticides in May, the Scientific Advisory Board of Germany's National Action Plan for the Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products reminded the German government of its own law in a statement. Brühl was the lead author.

Researchers wrote that integrated pest management calls for the use of synthetic chemical pesticides only as a last resort. The goal is to secure yields and quality while also minimizing negative consequences for people and nature and preventing resistance to plant protection products. This can work if certain crop rotations are taken into account and mixed cropping is favored. Pests can be controlled by attracting natural predators through flower strips or hedges, while weeds can be removed mechanically.
The problem: Spraying pesticides is often the less time-consuming and therefore cheaper option. There is also a persistent narrative that pesticides are necessary to ensure food security.

What this narrative leaves out is that monocultures and ecosystems disrupted by pesticides make agriculture more vulnerable to changing environmental conditions. That threatens food security, said Brühl, "because you have a system in place that can't cope with climate change."
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Venezuela’s Delcy Rodríguez says oil deal with Trump has ‘endless’ benefits
articles.summary:
Deal that will reportedly see US take control of 65bn barrels of Venezuelan oil has provoked outrage in her country

Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has defended her…

blocks.text: Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has defended her government’s highly controversial energy deal with Donald Trump, insisting the South American country will maintain ownership and sovereignty over its massive oil reserves.

Rodríguez, who assumed power in January after Trump ordered the abduction of the president, Nicolás Maduro, took to the airwaves on Saturday to push back against criticism of what the US president has called “the biggest oil deal in world history”.
“The benefits are endless,” claimed Rodríguez, a former vice-president who Trump backed after ordering Maduro’s capture during a special forces raid on the capital, Caracas.

During a six-minute television broadcast, Venezuela’s acting leader claimed the deal would help her resource-rich country develop its economy, earn revenues of more than $209bn (£154bn), and become “an energy powerhouse”.

Rodríguez said: “As everyone knows, our country has the biggest oil reserves in the world. But having resources underground isn’t enough. We need investment, technology, infrastructure [and] production capacity to convert this wealth into wellbeing for our people.”
She added: “It’s no use having our oil reserves underground, only to appear in statistics or bookkeeping … and for us not to be able to convert and translate them into development for Venezuela.”

Trump announced the “groundbreaking” deal on Friday, calling it a “historic transaction [that] more than doubles American oil reserves … while helping to continue to set Venezuela on a course toward Tremendous Success and Great Prosperity”.

On Sunday, Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform: “One of the things I am going to do with the Venezuelan Oil is fill up the Strategic National Reserves which, because of Sleepy Joe Biden, has been virtually emptied.”
Trump added: “The ‘topping out’ process will begin very shortly, and is a Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States.”

Hours after seizing Maduro on 3 January, Trump warned Rodríguez she would face an even worse fate if she failed to toe the US line. “If she doesn’t do what’s right, she is going to pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro,” Trump said.
Details of the agreement – struck during months of secret talks – remain sparse but it will reportedly see Washington take control of 65bn barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves.

The South American country has the world’s largest proven crude oil reserves, with an estimated 303bn barrels, compared with Saudi Arabia’s 268bn and Iran’s 208bn. Rodríguez said the deal involved 17 “strategic oilfields” where it was hoped more than 1.5m barrels could be produced each day.
But the deal has provoked outrage, both among members of Venezuela’s opposition and within the Chavismo political movement of which Rodríguez is part.
Speaking on Friday, one prominent opposition figure, who asked not to be named, called the agreement “a massive land grab” by a “a rapacious, mafioso United States”.

Writing on X, Rafael Ramírez, the former head of Venezuela’s state-owned oil company PDVSA, accused Rodríguez’s administration of “driving a dagger straight into the heart of the homeland” with the “neo-colonial” transaction. “They are handing over 65bn barrels of our reserves to the United States. That has never happened in Venezuela, and I think nowhere else in the world,” Ramírez added in an interview with the newspaper El Nacional.
On Saturday, dozens of leftwing protesters marched through Caracas with banners reading: “We are neither a colony, nor a backyard” and “Yankees go home!”
Critics of the agreement shared an ironic meme on social media suggesting the state oil company’s name should be changed from PDVSA to “PDUSA”.

In her broadcast, Rodríguez, the daughter of a Marxist guerrilla who spent years denouncing “imperialist” attempts to snatch her country’s oil reserves, countered claims she was surrendering Venezuela’s natural resources to a foreign power. She thanked Trump and the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, for striking the deal but added: “There is something that must be made absolutely clear: Venezuela retains the ownership and sovereignty over its resources.”
“We are thinking of Venezuela’s future,” claimed the politician, whose country was plunged into authoritarian rule and one of the world’s worst peacetime economic crises during Maduro’s 13-year rule.
The deal represents an astonishing U-turn from Rodríguez and the socialist, anti-imperialist political movement she and Maduro inherited from Hugo Chávez after his 2013 death.

In one 2024 speech, footage of which circulated on social media after Friday’s announcement, Rodríguez lambasted the Venezuelan opposition, accusing it of seeking to surrender the country’s oil, natural gas and gold reserves to their “masters” in Washington.
Last September, as the US tightened the screws on Maduro, Rodríguez told the New York Times: “The Pentagon always had a strategic objective of obtaining Venezuelan reserves.”

The deal will reportedly involve the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital, which channels funds into projects seen as important for national security. It will also involve a private company owned by Alejandro Betancourt, a controversial UK-based tycoon who has emerged as a key intermediary between the Trump administration and Rodríguez and owns mansions in Oxfordshire and London.

Opposition politicians fear the deal will scupper attempts to recover Venezuela’s democracy and hold fresh presidential elections. Maduro is widely believed to have stolen the last vote, in 2024, and Rodríguez has deflected questions about a future election, saying vaguely that it will happen “some day”. Trump has also said Venezuela is “not really ready” for elections.

Writing on X, the opposition leader Juan Pablo Guanipa, said: “The only way to truly reactivate the Venezuelan economy in the long term and make this agreement benefit both parties is through a free election that leads to a representative government, clear rules of the game, rule of law, and institutions that allow our resources to be managed transparently and for the benefit of the nation.”
Without that, the energy deal was like “a skyscraper [built] on pillars of clay”, Guanipa added.

articles.title: Gilas Pilipinas dedicates win over Iran to retiring June Mar Fajardo
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—Ensuring a memorable national team exit for June Mar Fajardo served as extra motivation for Gilas Pilipinas in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers. Kai Sotto…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas center June Mar Fajardo during a game against Iran in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers at Mall of Asia Arena.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines—Ensuring a memorable national team exit for June Mar Fajardo served as extra motivation for Gilas Pilipinas in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers.
Kai Sotto and Juan Gomez de Liaño said that was their mindset heading into the Philippines’ crucial clash against Iran on Sunday night in Fajardo’s final game in a national team jersey.

“That’s June Mar Fajardo,” said a proud Sotto after the Filipinos’ 68-56 win over the Iranians before a packed crowd at Mall of Asia Arena. “I thank my idol and everyone else’s idol in Kuya June. He had such a great career in the national team. This win is dedicated to him.”

FOR KUYA JUNE 🫡 Kai Sotto dedicates Gilas’ latest win to June Mar Fajardo, who officially retired from national team duties. @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/OfFlIqaeEo — Rommel Fuertes Jr. (@MeloFuertesINQ) August 30, 2026

The 7-foot-3 Sotto honored his veteran teammate by recording 13 points and 16 rebounds, while Gomez de Liaño also played a key role with 16 points, seven of which came in a critical stretch in the third when Gilas was having a hard time scoring.
“We all came here with the same goal, which is to be on the same page for June Mar,” Gomez de Liaño said. “We also wanted to win these two crucial games for us to advance to the next round.”
Fajardo’s swansong concluded a successful window for the Philippines, which improved to 4-4 in Group E.

‘LAST GAME NA. LAST GAME NA TALAGA’ 👏 After 13 years of representing the Philippines with Gilas, June Mar Fajardo officially calls it a career. @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/tCPss9VjKy — Rommel Fuertes Jr. (@MeloFuertesINQ) August 30, 2026

The 36-year-old center saw limited action but still made an impact as one of the team’s sparks off the bench in the second quarter after Gilas fell behind by as many as 13 early. Fajardo finished with 6 points and two rebounds and even received MVP chants while shooting free throws.

Fajardo had a decorated national team career that began 13 years ago as part of the Gilas Pilipinas squad that secured a historic silver medal at the 2013 Fiba Asia Championship in Manila and qualified for the World Cup in Spain.
“It’s nice and really heartwarming,” said Fajardo. “I’m so blessed. I got to play with the past, present and future of Gilas.”

articles.title: Cash settlements on home insurance claims leaving vulnerable Australians short-changed, Asic says
articles.summary:
Corporate regulator finds insurers settling most claims with cash rather than by managing repairs or rebuilding, warning of ‘unfair outcomes’ for homeowners

  • Get our

blocks.text: Home insurers are overwhelmingly paying cash to settle claims, leaving Australians to foot blowouts in repair costs for their cyclone-damaged homes.
The corporate regulator is calling for “realistic” bigger payouts, warning the practice could cause “unfair outcomes” for people already in vulnerable positions.
In a report released on Monday, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (Asic) found many homeowners were being paid based on a single quote from insurers’ favoured builders.

Asic commissioner Alan Kirkland said homeowners were then left to find tradespeople, oversee repairs and pay for unexpected costs and damage, all issues that would otherwise have been handled by insurers.
“The easy option for insurers can be the expensive one for homeowners,” Kirkland said.
“If the amount falls short, consumers can be left shouldering the cost of repairs and paying the difference out of their own pocket.”
Asic reviewed a sample of home building insurance claims from Cyclone Jasper, which hit far north Queensland in December 2023.
It looked at the companies that it said accounted for most of the home insurance industry: Insurance Australia Group (IAG), AAI, QBE Insurance, Allianz Australia and Sure Insurance.

Asic said insurers professed to prefer to settle claims by managing repairs or rebuilding, not by paying cash. The review found none of the five were systematically recording why claims were being settled with cash.
Cash settlements were used in more than 63% of final claims. IAG and Allianz each used full or partial cash settlements in more than 80% of cases.
Most cash settlement offers were based on just one quote and most of those were from insurers’ preferred suppliers, the review found.
Asic said it was concerned the quotes may not be high enough to cover customers’ repair costs, as customers may not be able to get the discounts given to insurers.

In one case, an insurer’s preferred builder provided a quote at a 40% discount and the insurer paid out that cheaper quote in cash. When the customer asked the builder to repair their home for that cash amount, the builder refused.
Some insurers applied extra pay to account for their suppliers giving the insurer a discounted quote but none had consistent systems in place to do so, the review found.

Insurers rarely provided consumers enough information to determine if cash was their best option. Three insurers did not tell consumers their policies permitted them to change their mind after accepting cash settlements, though two later told Asic they had begun clearly informing consumers of their rights.
Four of the five insurers had flawed approaches for identifying and assisting vulnerable customers, the report found.
after newsletter promotion

While the report did not identify any breaches of legal obligations, it said insurers would clearly comply with the rules if they ensured cash settlement offers were based on market prices, not discount rates.
The costs of construction and repairs have soared in recent years, with a resulting surge in home insurance costs.
Finity, an analytics company, has found home insurance premiums rose 51% in the five years to October 2025.
Insurance prices generally rose 4.2% in the year to July, faster than inflation of 3.5%, the Australian bureau of statistics reported on Wednesday.
Asic earlier this month advised car owners to challenge their insurers and shop around for better deals after finding insurers were failing to clearly justify their steep increases to premiums.
Complaints about home building insurance have returned to highs not seen since 2022-23 due to insurers’ delays in handling claims.
The Insurance Council of Australia has found the climate crisis and increasing incidence of extreme weather has nearly tripled total costs for insurers.
In a 2025 report, it estimated extreme weather had generated $4.5bn worth of claims each year on average in the 2020s.

articles.title: Canada erects giant ‘Lake Ontario’ sign as spat with Trump over name escalates
articles.summary:
Meanwhile, Trump posts video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America sign

Donald Trump…

blocks.text: Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the country erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA.

Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa.

Trump’s order for the US government to refer to Lake Ontario as Lake America by Sunday had at least one prominent impact. Google Maps had changed Lake Ontario’s name to Lake America for US users to reflect the president’s executive renaming order.

Canada’s prime minister Mark Carney has flat-out rejected the renaming, explaining that Lake Ontario derives from an Indigenous Wendat word meaning “the lake is beautiful, the lake is great” that dates back more than 400 years.
With talks to resolve the trade dispute stalled, Trump issued an executive order on Thursday directing US agencies that the lake was now Lake America.
It revived memories of a dispute earlier in his second presidency with Mexico, which saw Trump direct US agencies to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America.

“We’re going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America,” Trump told reporters before he signed an executive order renaming the body of water among US federal agencies.

In a statement explaining why it was acquiescing to Trump’s desired name for Lake Ontario, Google said its practice is to “reflect name changes in official government sources”. Trump’s order affects the US’s federal Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), “which sets the standard for official US maps”, the tech company said.

blocks.caption: Lake Ontario renamed as Lake America on US-facing Google Maps. Photograph: Google Maps

blocks.text: The Lake of Ontario’s name change “does not have any impact on Canadian naming conventions or ​how the rest of the ‌world refers to the ‌lake,” Google said in a statement. And it said “those in Canada will continue to see ‘Lake Ontario’” on Google Maps, “and those outside … the US and Canada will see both names.”

Google had done similarly in Trump’s executive order for the US government to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. US Google Map users for now see that body of water named as the “Gulf of America”.
Meanwhile, on Saturday, the US president raised the volume again by resorting to the kind of AI-generated imagery for which he has shown a penchant.

He posted one such video of an army of Canada geese with Trump-like blond hair firing rifles in protection of Lake America. He published another of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America while he danced in his distinctive to a soundtrack of the Village People hit YMCA, which he has implemented into his public appearances for years.

Across the US’s northern border, Ontario premier Doug Ford replied with a two-stories high billboard declaring “Lake Ontario. Now and Always,” near Grimsby, Ontario. Ford said Trump was trying to rename the lake because Ontario and Canada were “standing up for ourselves”, and he argued the name would outlast the president.
“Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario,” Ford said in a video posted on social media.
In an interview with the Associated Press earlier, Ford said the late Ronald Reagan would be “throwing up” over Trump’s tariff policies.
Meanwhile, Manitoba’s premier, Wab Kinew, said Trump’s Lake America provocation was akin to an aging rock band trying to revive an old hit.

“You know when, like, a rock band is really over the hill and you see them like in a casino playing some song from like 50 years ago, I think that’s the part of Donald Trump’s presidency we’re at now,” Kinew said. “Like he thought he had a real hit, a real golden oldie, with the Gulf of Mexico.
“He’s trying to bring back that, and he’s trying to play the hits for his base. But I think everybody here thinks it’s a little sad, and it’s not his best work.”

Wendat Nation grand chief Pierre Picard called Trump’s move an attempt to erase Indigenous history. “I want to tell him that it is unacceptable for us, as a nation, to have a president who can eradicate our history, our culture and our identity,” Picard said.
Lake Ontario is one of North America’s five Great Lakes, alongside Superior, Michigan, Huron and Erie. At 7,340 sq miles, Lake Ontario is the smallest of those in terms of surface area.

articles.title: Parts of NLEX, MacArthur Highway, Bulacan roads impassable due to floods
articles.summary: CITY OF MALOLOS, Bulacan — Heavy rains caused flooding that rendered parts of major roads in Bulacan, including the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) and MacArthur Highway, impassable to some vehicles,…

blocks.text: CITY OF MALOLOS, Bulacan — Heavy rains caused flooding that rendered parts of major roads in Bulacan, including the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) and MacArthur Highway, impassable to some vehicles, the Bulacan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) said Sunday.
Manuel Lukban Jr., head of the Bulacan PDRRMO, said the road conditions were based on an 11 a.m. Sunday assessment.

In Meycauayan City, all northbound and southbound lanes of NLEX in Barangay Libtong became impassable around 11 a.m. Saturday, Aug. 29, due to knee-deep floodwaters. The water began rising at 10:20 a.m. and subsided at 3:05 a.m. Sunday.
Several roads in Meycauayan were also inaccessible, including portions of MacArthur Highway in Barangay Calvario and roads in Barangays Saluysoy, Pandayan, Banga, Hulo, Bangcal, and Bayugo.
In Hagonoy, portions of barangay roads in San Juan, San Isidro, and Palapat were impassable to light vehicles.
In Calumpit, roads in Barangays Gugo and Meysulao were completely submerged by floodwaters caused by heavy rains and high tide, leaving boats as the only means of transportation.

Barangays Bulusan and Sta. Lucia were also impassable to all vehicles, while roads in San Jose, Frances, Calizon, and portions of the Calumpit-Hagonoy road could only be used by heavy vehicles and elongated tricycles known as “tikling.”
In Balagtas, Bantayan Street in Barangay Panginay and MacArthur Highway in Barangay Wawa-Poblacion were impassable to light vehicles.
The Macaiban Bridge in Barangay Tumana, Sta. Maria, was closed to all vehicles.
Several roads in Bocaue and Marilao were likewise impassable to all types of vehicles, while a barangay road in Dampol 1st, Pulilan, was closed to light vehicles.
Meanwhile, water releases from Bustos Dam increased to 912 cubic meters per second (cms) after its water elevation reached 16.98 meters at about 8 p.m. Saturday. Its spilling elevation is 17 meters.
Ipo Dam reached 100.79 meters at around 7 p.m. Saturday, just 0.21 meter below its 101-meter spilling elevation.
Angat Dam also continued to rise, reaching 199.01 meters above sea level as of 4 p.m. Sunday, or about 11 meters below its 210-meter normal high-water elevation. /mcm

articles.title: Gilas Pilipinas beats Iran in key duel to sweep Fiba fourth window
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–Gilas Pilipinas rallied past Iran, 68-56, to complete a crucial sweep in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers on Sunday night before a packed crowd at Mall of…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas center Kai Sotto towers over Iran players during their game in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers at Mall of Asia Arena.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net

MANILA, Philippines–Gilas Pilipinas rallied past Iran, 68-56, to complete a crucial sweep in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers on Sunday night before a packed crowd at Mall of Asia Arena.
Gilas improved to 4-4 and more importantly, put itself back into serious contention for a top-three finish in Group E and an automatic qualification for next year’s World Cup in Qatar.
Kai Sotto came up big anew on both ends with 13 points and 16 rebounds, while Dwight Ramos and Juan Gomez de Liano led the Philippines in scoring with 16 apiece.
The Philippines trailed by as many as 13 early before turning things around in the second quarter behind Gomez de Liano, Ramos and veteran center June Mar Fajardo.
In his national team swansong, Fajardo was one of the sparks off the bench, scoring all of his six points in a key second quarter for Gilas.

articles.title: Northern Cyprus ferry disaster: at least seven dead as vessel capsizes – latest updates
articles.summary:
An estimated 237 people have been rescued after accident off the coast of northern Cyprus

  • Fatali…

blocks.text: At least seven people reportedly die after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
At least seven people have died after a ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off the coast of Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus, local media reported.

An estimated 237 people have been rescued, Northern Cyprus’ prime minister, Ünal Üstel, told the TRT news channel, adding that the ferry had faced adverse weather conditions and began taking in water just 15 minutes after departure.

Local media report that an intensive search and rescue effort was launched after the boat capsized off the coastal town of Kyrenia earlier today. The ferry had been travelling to the Turkish port of Tasucu.
Key events

items: 14m agoPriority following 'tragic shipwreck' is reaching 23 missing passengers, region’s prime minister says
28m agoAt least seven people reportedly die after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
28m agoMayor describes Cyprus ferry incident as 'very serious'

blocks.text: Here are some of the latest images being sent to us over the newswires following the incident:

blocks.caption: Survivors arrive on shore after being rescued from the sea after the boat capsized off Kyrenia in northern Cyprus. Photograph: Reuters
Some of the survivors arrive at the port of Kyrenia in the Turkish occupied northern part of Cyprus. Photograph: AP
A helicopter brings survivors ashore after they were rescued from the sea after a passenger boat carrying more than 260 people capsized off northern Cyprus. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: Priority following 'tragic shipwreck' is reaching 23 missing passengers, region’s prime minister says

The prime minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Ünal Üstel, has posted an update on X about the “tragic shipwreck”. He said 237 out of the 267 people on board the ship have been rescued – but seven people have died.
Üstel said search and rescue operations are under way to locate the 23 missing people, which he describes as the “utmost priority”.
“I offer my condolences from Allah for those who have passed away, and wish patience and strength to their families and loved ones. I pray for a swift recovery for the injured,” he added in the post.
“All institutions of our state are on the ground. We are continuing the search and rescue efforts with the utmost care and closely following developments.”
Mayor describes Cyprus ferry incident as 'very serious'

In a post to Facebook, the mayor of the coastal town of Kyrenia, Murat Senkul, described the situation as “very serious” and confirmed that 270 passengers and crew were aboard when the ship sank off the coast of Diana beach. He said the ferry belonged to the Filo Denizcilik company.
“The Coast Guard, the *Akgünler Express* vessel, and numerous small boats are participating in rescue operations,” he wrote in the social media post.
“Please refrain from sharing information that could cause confusion or spread misinformation.”

articles.summary: Widespread flooding due to the heavy rainfall from the Habagat and recent storms has affected at least 2.4 million families across 10 regions in Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, the OCD said.

blocks.text: Widespread flooding due to the heavy rainfall from the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) and recent storms has affected at least 2.4 million families across 10 regions in Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, the Office of Civil Defense said.

In a statement, the OCD said that as of 6 p.m. Sunday the confirmed death toll from the calamities remains at 32, its tally since Saturday. The number of injured and missing remain at 19 and three respectively.
The population affected by the flooding consists of 2.4 million families or 8.4 million individuals in the following regions across the country:

I (Ilocos Region)
II (Cagayan valley)
III (Central Luzon)
IV-A (CALABARZON)
IV-B (MIMAROPA)
V (Bicol)
VI (Western Visayas)
IX (Zamboanga Peninsula)
NCR (Metro Manila)

blocks.text: In those regions, 35,500 families made up of 122,500 individuals are staying at 1,115 evacuation centers, it added.
PAGASA on Sunday also issued orange and yellow rainfall warnings over several areas in Luzon, a downgrade from earlier red rainfall warnings:

Orange Rainfall Warning (Flooding is still threatening)• Zambales• Bataan (Abucay, Bagac, Balanga, Dinalupihan, Hermosa, Morong, Orani, Orion, Pilar, Samal)• Tarlac (Mayantoc, San Jose, Capas, Bamban, San Clemente, Camiling, Santa Ignacia)• Pampanga (Porac, Floridablanca, Lubao, Sasmuan, Apalit, Bacolor, San Fernando, Macabebe, Masantol, Mexico, Minalin, San Luis, San Simon, Santa Ana, Santo Tomas, Angeles, Mabalacat, Guagua, Santa Rita)• Bulacan (Hagonoy, Calumpit, Paombong, Malolos)

Yellow Rainfall Warning (Flooding in flood-prone areas)• Nueva Ecija• Metro Manila• Tarlac (Concepcion, Anao, Tarlac City, Gerona, La Paz, Paniqui, Pura, Ramos, San Manuel, Victoria, Moncada)• Pampanga (Arayat, Candaba, Magalang)• Bulacan (Angat, Balagtas, Baliuag, Bocaue, Bulakan, Bustos, Meycauayan, San Jose del Monte, Dona Remedios Trinidad, Guiguinto, Marilao, Norzagaray, Obando, Pandi, Plaridel, Pulilan, San Ildefonso, San Miguel, San Rafael, Santa Maria)• Rizal (Antipolo, Rodriguez, San Mateo, Cainta, Taytay)• Cavite (General Trias, General Emilio Aguinaldo, Magallanes, Maragondon, Ternate, Trece Martires, Bacoor, Cavite City, Imus, Kawit, Naic, Noveleta, Rosario, Tanza)• Batangas (Nasugbu)• Bataan (Limay, Mariveles)

Tarlac has declared a state of calamity, amid the collapse of two bridges in recent days, bringing the tally of provincial and local governments that have declared a state of calamity to a total of 118.

PAGASA also said in its 11 a.m. video briefing on Sunday that while Tropical Depression Pilandok will have no direct effect on the Philippines, it continues to intensify the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat even as Pilandok remains far from the Philippine landmass.

As of 4 p.m., Pilandok was located at 1,180 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility and is moving northwestward slowly over the sea, PAGASA said in its 5 p.m. bulletin. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
articles.summary: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.

image.caption: A drone view of the aftermath of flash flooding along the Trishuli River amid a new water surge warning in the Trishuli Bazaar area of Nepal on Sunday. (Rajesh Kumar Singh/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.
Residents remain on high-alert in some of worst-hit areas

Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday's catastrophic floods, which killed at least 800 people and left more than 3,000 missing in Nepal and Tibet.
In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some residents began returning to ruined homes to see what can be salvaged.

Residents sat in homes with walls washed away by the floods, shovelling sludge-like mud and rubble off balconies. Others scanned the ground for items they could pick out of the mud and rinse off. One man had returned for his chickens, which he found alive. He tied them up and put them in the cabin of his truck.

items: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood

blocks.text: "Everything is finished. Nothing is left. Not even our home," Sharmila Tamang, a Dhading resident who was trying to salvage items from her home, told The Associated Press.

At a key power plant that was severely damaged by the floods, workers started inspecting the facilities Sunday to survey the destruction. The plant serves more than 20,000 people across four districts.

In the town of Galchhi, a group of residents sought higher ground on a nearby bridge and watched as the river roared by. Some pointed to enormous rocks washed downriver during the earlier floods, while others standing on a suspension bridge were warned off with whistles.

Along the river, homes, vehicles and farm tractors could be seen jutting from the thick grey-brown sediment that enveloped entire villages in some areas. Parts of rice terraces along the riverside had dropped into the river after landslides hit them.
Nepal-Tibet flash flood death toll climbs as fears of 2nd flood grow
Nepal's disaster agency said Sunday the death toll had climbed to 788 with 2,502 missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing on the Chinese side of the border.

The missing include hundreds of people from over a dozen countries who were in the region to work, visit the mountains or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak. On Sunday, Chinese state media said 261 foreigners were missing in Tibet, including over 100 Nepalis and others from around the world.
Residents are receiving constant flood warnings
Homes and businesses left intact after the flooding were still without electricity on Sunday, as twisted power line poles and wires lay tangled in the mud.

Prithivi Highway is a crucial supply route for food, fuel and other goods entering Kathmandu from other parts of the country. While most of the highway is operational, other parts still face repair challenges.

items: Families search for loved ones among the dead in Nepal

blocks.text: The latest warnings came after Chinese authorities informed their Nepalese counterparts of increased water flow upstream, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
But residents of the flood-hit villages said they were struggling to make sense of near-constant alarms they've received since the initial floods.

"Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain," said Govind Shreshta, a resident. "It's really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mom. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It's going on like this for those who are still alive."
Large concrete and smaller suspension bridges were destroyed, leaving communities on the other side of the river with less easy access.

"Those who are there are now stuck there. Those who are here are stuck here. It's going to be very difficult," said Sattan Singh Tamang, 47, who was working near a bridge when Wednesday's floods came.
Nepalis have become victims of climate change: minister

Wednesday's flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as magnitude 5.2.
The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.
Nepal's foreign minister called for a global response to climate change, saying Nepal was bearing a disproportionate share of its impact.
"Despite having only 0.1 per cent contribution to the global emissions, people of Nepal have become major victims of climate change," Shisir Khanal said Saturday.

Scientists have said it is too early to draw a direct connection between global warming and Wednesday's catastrophe. However, they said that as Earth's temperature rises because of human activities such as burning oil, gas and coal, the chances of such disasters increase, especially in the Himalayan mountains, which are warming considerably faster than many other parts of the world.

The catamaran-style ferry had been travelling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, in the breakaway north of divided Cyprus, to the port of Taşucu in Mersin province, Turkey.

articles.title: Masses suspended at Pampanga cathedral due to flooding
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — The Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando in Pampanga’s capital city suspended all Masses on Sunday, Aug. 30, due to flooding. In a Facebook post late Saturday, the…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — The Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando in Pampanga’s capital city suspended all Masses on Sunday, Aug. 30, due to flooding.
In a Facebook post late Saturday, the cathedral said floodwaters and silt had seeped into the church, while its patio and surrounding streets remained submerged.
“For the safety of all, we regret to announce that all Sunday morning and afternoon Masses tomorrow (August 30) are cancelled,” it said.
Four Masses were scheduled from 5 a.m. to 10:30 a.m., while three others were set between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.
Masses on Friday and Saturday had also been canceled due to flooding in downtown San Fernando.
Meanwhile, SM City Pampanga, which straddles San Fernando and Mexico, and SM City San Fernando Downtown also remained closed on Sunday due to flooding.
“For the safety of our customers and employees, SM City San Fernando Downtown and SM City Pampanga will be closed today, August 30, 2026,” the malls said in separate Facebook posts. /mcm

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet death toll rises amid new flood fears and race to free group trapped in tunnel
articles.summary: Combined toll of more than 750 dead and 3,000 people missing in Nepal and Tibet after devastating flood

blocks.text: Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet have battled through leg-sucking mud amid the threat of fresh flooding to search for thousands of people still missing after a deadly wall of water swept through the Himalayan border zone, engulfing entire villages.

The latest updates on Sunday put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There were 768 confirmed deaths, and reports of some bodies swept downstream possibly as far as India.

Nepal said it had begun the grim task of burying some of the hundreds of bodies after first taking DNA samples so that families could later reclaim them and perform traditional funeral rites after identification.
The disaster, which struck the border on Wednesday morning, was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
Nepal’s foreign minister called for a global response to the climate crisis, saying the small, poor Himalayan nation was bearing a disproportionate share of its impact.
“Despite having only 0.1% contribution to the global emissions, people of Nepal have become major victims of climate change,” Shisir Khanal said on Saturday.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far. Chinese authorities on Sunday reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, of whom 261 were foreign nationals, including 104 from Nepal, 49 from India, 33 from Latvia, 18 from the US and 15 British citizens.
In a breakthrough at the weekend, Nepal’s army was able to insert a pipe into a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site where more than 100 workers are believed to be trapped.
The home minister, Sudan Gurung, said: “We have already started sending air through the small opening, and we will now begin excavation work and send the rescue team inside.”

It is a race against time to reach the workers, who may still be alive inside the tunnels, with rescue efforts focused on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites. They are among 933 hydropower workers who are among the missing, according to Nepal’s disaster authority.

blocks.caption: Soldiers search for bodies as rescue operations shift into search and retrieval in Nepal.  Photograph: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images

blocks.text: Nepal warned on Sunday of rising flood waters and urged rescue teams to exercise caution. “We have received information that the flood flow in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa has increased further,” the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
Flood warnings were sent to people’s phones early on Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas hit by the devastating floods.

In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some people began returning to ruined homes to see what could be salvaged. Residents of the flood-hit villages said they were struggling to make sense of near-constant alarms they had received since the initial floods.

One resident, Govind Shreshta, told the Associated Press: “Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain. It’s really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mum. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It’s going on like this for those who are still alive.”
The government estimated Nepal’s reconstruction bill could run into the billions of dollars.
Officials in Nepal called for forensic testing kits to identify bodies and freezer units to store them in, saying bodies that had been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
Survivors face an agonising wait to learn the fate of missing relatives and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” Buddhi Ram Dangol told Agence France-Presse in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. “There is nothing left.”

blocks.caption: Firefighters conduct search and rescue operations along a river in Gyirong county in Tibet. Photograph: cnsphoto/Reuters

blocks.text: In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, rescue operations were temporarily paused at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of more flooding from a newly formed lake.
A total of 2,141 rescuers were near the Gyirong site, the Xinhua state news agency reported, including more than 500 in the worst-hit area.
In Kathmandu, Nepal’s capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning desperately searching for news of missing loved ones.
Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital noticeboard, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients’ lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had travelled from Ramechhap, about 80 miles (130km) away.
“I came here with the hope that I might find him,” she told the Associated Press. “There is no information about him.”
Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa. “I feel hopeless. It has already been four days,” she said.
With Associated Press, Agence France-Presse and Reuters

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY — Tarlac province has been placed under a state of calamity due to widespread damage caused by the southwest monsoon, Gov. Christian Yap said Sunday.

Yap said the declaration was approved through Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 416-2026, following the recommendation of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC) amid the severe impact of the monsoon rains.
Several towns have been affected by flooding, while two major bridges connecting Tarlac City to several municipalities have become impassable.
The Aquino Bridge and Agana Bridge, which serve as vital links to Sta. Ignacia, Mayantoc, Camiling, San Clemente and San Jose, were damaged by the persistent rains.
Another portion of the Aquino Bridge collapsed on Sunday, further worsening the damage.
Heavy equipment has been deployed to the Agana Bridge area as authorities work to construct a temporary Bailey bridge to restore access. /mcm

Rescue crews are on scene after a ferry carrying more than 260 passengers capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday.
Rescue crews are on scene
A ferry carrying more than 260 passengers capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, Turkish media reported.
The catamaran-style ferry was travelling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, in the breakaway north of ethnically divided Cyprus, to the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province.
There are no reports of casualties so far.
The ferry started taking in water a few kilometres off the coast, the Turkish state-run TRT news channel reported.
Northern Cyprus Transportation Minister Erhan Arikli told TRT that the ship had overturned and that rescue crews were already on the scene.
Several companies run ferries on the busy route between Kyrenia and Tasucu. It is not yet known which company was operating the ferry that capsized.
Video footage from the scene shows people with life-vests floating in the waters around the capsized vessel.

articles.title: Peace adviser optimistic on ‘peaceful’ BARMM polls
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY — Presidential Peace Adviser Sec. Mel Senen Sarmiento expressed optimism Sunday that the first regional parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY — Presidential Peace Adviser Sec. Mel Senen Sarmiento expressed optimism Sunday that the first regional parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) next month would be “peaceful and successful.”
“The success of the election will not only be a milestone for the Bangsamoro peace process. It will be a victory for peace, democracy, and the Filipino people,” he said in a statement.

Sarmiento said the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU), which he heads, recognizes the historic Bangsamoro Parliamentary Elections (BPE) as a significant milestone in the political track of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro and the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
Commission on Elections (Comelec) chairperson George Erwin Garcia earlier expressed hopes that the historic Sept. 14 BARMM election would also be peaceful.
The Comelec has been meeting regularly with the military, police and other stakeholders in the region to ensure next month’s balloting would be the “most peaceful electoral activity in BARMM.”
“We appreciate the continuing efforts of the Commission on Elections and the security cluster to ensure that the electoral process is conducted properly and peacefully,” Sarmiento said.
“We likewise acknowledge the maturity and sense of responsibility being demonstrated by the political parties and their leaders as we approach this historic exercise,” he added.

Sarmiento said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s clear guidance “is that the Bangsamoro elections must uphold the integrity of the democratic process and protect the people’s right to freely choose their leaders.”

On Sept. 14, about 2.4 million registered voters in 5,212 clustered precincts at 1,186 voting centers across BARMM will elect 40 seats for regional parliamentary political parties, 32 single-district representatives, and six sectoral representatives, with two seats for settler communities and one seat each for women, youth, traditional leaders, and Ulama (Muslim religious leaders).
The non-Moro Indigenous Peoples (NIMIP) had already selected its two leaders through traditional and customary means of electing their representatives to the regional parliament.
Once the 80 elected parliament members are proclaimed, the Parliament will then elect the Chief Minister.
BARMM voters do not directly vote for the chief minister. /mcm

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Around 8.4 million individuals have been affected by the southwest monsoon and recent cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Around 8.4 million individuals have been affected by the southwest monsoon and recent cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) said on Sunday.

In its latest update as of 6 p.m., the NDRRMC said the weather systems affected 8.4 million individuals, or 2.4 million families, in the National Capital Region, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, Cordillera Administrative Region, Bicol Region, and Zamboanga Peninsula.
Approximately 122,500 individuals, or 35,500 families, are seeking temporary shelter in 1,115 evacuation centers.
The NDRRMC also reported 32 deaths linked to the weather disturbances, most of them in Benguet due to landslides. Nineteen individuals were injured, while three remained missing.

The agency estimated the total cost of damage to infrastructure and agriculture at P6.16 billion and P2.32 billion, respectively. It also said P1.7 billion worth of assistance had been provided to affected families.
A state of calamity has been declared in 117 areas in Pangasinan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.

Meanwhile, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Tropical Depression Pilandok is not forecast to make landfall over the country but will enhance the southwest monsoon, bringing more rain.

Pagasa said monsoon rains are forecast over Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, some parts of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon), and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan). /mcm

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau votes to reshape presidency
articles.summary: The West African nation's military government wants to amend the constitution to give more powers to the president. The junta, which seized power last year, says it will hold elections in December.

image.caption: More than 900,000 people are eligible to take part in the referendumImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: Guinea-Bissau voted on Sunday in a referendum on whether to give the president new powers as the country prepares to transition from military to democratic rule.
The tiny West African nation of around 2.2 million people has been under army rule since last November following a disputed election.
What will the referendum decide?
Guinea-Bissau's junta has unanimously approved a constitutional amendment to switch the country from what it frames as a parliamentary to a presidential system.
This means abandoning the old system where the prime minister came from the parliamentary majority.
The amendment would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and dissolve parliament.
If passed, the new constitution will cut the number of seats in parliament from 102 to 65.
The junta says the change seeks to stabilize institutions before new presidential and parliamentary elections, scheduled for December 6, which are meant to hand power back to civilians.
Opposition groups, however, have urged the public to boycott the vote, saying it will allow the junta leader to cement power and calling it a "source of political instability at all levels."

blocks.caption: Guinea-Bissau is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections in DecemberImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: When are the results due?
Polls close at 1700 GMT on Sunday, with the first provisional results due from Tuesday.
One of the world's poorest countries, Guinea-Bissau has experienced five coups and a series of attempted coups since 1974.
A military government seized power in November following a disputed election in which former President Umaro Sissoco Embalo and opposition candidate Fernando Dias both claimed victory.
After legislative elections in 2023, Embalo himself dissolved the opposition-dominated parliament in response to what he described as an attempted coup.

articles.title: DOT eyes bringing Mindanao into PH tourism circuit
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY — The Department of Tourism (DoT) is keen on bringing Mindanao into the country’s tourism circuit, citing the island’s stable security conditions, rich cultural heritage, unique…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY — The Department of Tourism (DoT) is keen on bringing Mindanao into the country’s tourism circuit, citing the island’s stable security conditions, rich cultural heritage, unique culinary offerings, and ecotourism destinations and adventures.

Tourism Assistant Secretary Ferdinand Jose Bagcal recently led a DoT team in conducting a comprehensive validation of tourism attractions in the Zamboanga Peninsula, the results of which will be included in the national travel and tourism circuit.
He noted that the initiative, which included site validations in Zamboanga del Sur, aims to uncover new destinations beyond the country’s famed beaches.

“We want to focus on Mindanao this time because it is rich in exceptional tourist assets. Our goal is to link these destinations into cohesive circuits (in the Philippines) that travelers can easily navigate,” Bagcal explained.
Bagcal expressed optimism about this city’s tourism potential, citing the newly opened Pagadian City Water Park along the boulevard as a promising development.
“Pagadian is something waiting to be discovered. It has immense potential to emerge as a major destination,” he said.

The team’s itinerary included visits to the Sto. Niño Cathedral, the Tourism Boat, the Regional Government Center, the Provincial Government Center, the sandbar called Puting Balas, and Bakilid Resort.
Bagcal stressed that culture and heritage form a core part of the validation, with the delegation engaging the Subanen indigenous community in the towns of Kumalarang and Lakewood.
In Kumalarang, the team observed traditional weaving and handicraft-making and met with local officials led by Mayor Ruel Molina.

The delegation also visited Lakewood, home to the province’s largest freshwater lake, spanning 800 hectares at the foot of Mt. Serongan and Mt. Imbing. The site is being positioned as a scenic ecotourism destination.
Sara Mae Lee Monroy, DoT’s lead project officer for cultural tourism, emphasized the richness of Zamboanga del Sur’s tourism assets.
“We saw traditions, performances, and crafts that offer immersive experiences. Even simple mat weaving is something travelers should witness firsthand,” she said.
Monroy stressed that showcasing Mindanao’s warmth and diversity is vital to counter negative perceptions.
“Mindanao is safe, relaxing, and full of unique food and adventure. There is more to the Philippines than Boracay, Davao, or Bohol—Zamboanga Peninsula deserves a place on the tourism map,” she said.
Bagcal commended the local government units for investing in tourism infrastructure and product development, also citing the willingness of the tri-people to develop tourism in the area. /mcm

articles.title: Fiba World Cup Asian qualifiers: Dominant Australia crushes Jordan
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—There’s still no stopping Australia in the 2027 Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers. The Boomers continued their dominance after burying Jordan, 126-93, to remain the only unblemished…

blocks.text: Australia’s Anthony Dell’Orso during a game against Jordan in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines—There’s still no stopping Australia in the 2027 Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers.
The Boomers continued their dominance after burying Jordan, 126-93, to remain the only unblemished team in the tournament on Sunday at Mall of Asia Arena.
“We saw how Jordan played the other night and saw how well they can run their offense when given a chance,” coach Jacob Chance said.
“To come out and be as disruptive as we were early was a pleasing sign.”
The Aussies, who whipped Syria, 123-64, on Friday night, improved to 8-0.
Jordan, which was coming off a tough 82-81 overtime loss to Gilas Pilipinas on Friday night, dropped to 0-2 in the second round and 5-3 overall.

Australia flaunted its depth with seven players tallying at least nine points. Anthony Dell’Orso led all Boomers in scoring with 19. Angus Glover added 16, Josh Bannan had 15, while Tom Wilson posted 13. Elijah Pepper, who registered 32 against Syria, struggled to find the target but still wound up with 14 on 5-of-16 shooting.
The Boomers shot 52 percent from the field, including 14-of-31 from the 3-point area.
The Falcons dropped to 5-3 in Group E but not without Amin Abu Hawwas had 21 for the Falcons, who also drew 19 each from their backcourt Abdullah Olajuwon and Jalen Harris.

articles.title: USC Warriors start Cesafi Season 26 with a stunner over UV Green Lancers
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The University of San Carlos (USC) Warriors opened their Cebu Schools Athletic Foundation, Inc. (Cesafi) Season 26 men’s basketball campaign with a bang, stunning…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The University of San Carlos (USC) Warriors opened their Cebu Schools Athletic Foundation, Inc. (Cesafi) Season 26 men’s basketball campaign with a bang, stunning four-time defending champion University of the Visayas (UV) Green Lancers, 81-68, on Sunday, August 30, at the Cebu Coliseum.
What was expected to be a routine win for UV turned into a statement victory for USC. The Warriors controlled most of the game and led by as many as 16 points, 66-50, in the fourth quarter.

Playing in his final Cesafi season with the Warriors, Jhoernel Tangkay delivered a stellar performance. He posted a game-high 18 points and 11 rebounds for a double-double. He also came up with nine steals and an assist, falling just one assist short of a triple-double.
MORE CESAFI NEWS: Cesafi Season 26: CEC, USJ-R open campaigns with dominant wins
A challenge for the UV Green Lancers
Real Aureo added 15 points, three assists and three rebounds. James Paolo Gica chipped in 13 points and Jose Marie Tumabang contributed 12 for the Warriors.
AJ Sacayan led the UV Green Lancers with 17 points, two rebounds and two assists.
Kent Ivo Salarda finished with 10 points.
The Green Lancers struggled to find their rhythm offensively, committing 20 turnovers, with USC forcing 19 steals and adding five blocks.
USC Warriors hold steady

USC established its dominance early, building a double-digit lead in the first half before extending it to 13 points, 53-40, midway through the third quarter. The Warriors’ aggressive defense and timely long-range shooting kept UV on the back foot as the defending champions struggled to generate a consistent offense.
The game was briefly halted midway through the fourth quarter when the lights went out due to a rotational brownout in Cebu. But the interruption did little to cool off the Warriors.

When play resumed, USC picked up where it left off and pushed its lead to a game-high 16 points at 66-50, before holding off the defending champions to complete one of the biggest upsets of the Cesafi Season 26 opening day.

articles.title: Opinion: ‘Halad sa Pagtuo’ in the time of AI, climate emergency
articles.summary: The generosity that a fiesta occasions is the true heart of devotion to the saints, although a procession is a rather indispensable reminder that “open hands” are not some vague principle floating in…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The idea of a Cebuano festival of festivals is basically a good one.

To hold an event as big as Halad sa Pagtuo (Offering of Faith) toward the end of August, as the Cebu Provincial Government did on August 29 adds life to the month. This somehow makes up for the caution and inclination to belt-tightening with which we have begun to view this time of year, given that it is Ghost Month in the eyes of our Chinese brothers and sisters, to whose cultural beliefs we open ourselves as much as we do to other cultures on our planet.
Halad sa Pagtuo is already different from other festivals and fiestas on different levels.

For instance, its predecessor when Gwendolyn Garcia was governor of Cebu was Pasigarbo sa Sugbo (Cebu’s Show of Pride) and focused on the dancing that developed in light of the fiestas of the various locales in Cebu province.
Sacred roots of secular celebrations

Halad sa Pagtuo under Gov. Pamela Baricuatro, in contrast, put on center stage the patron saints of these places. Their carrozas, moreover, were taken in procession before the cultural program in which contingents representing a variety of festivals danced in an exhibition of their respective traditions.

It may be said that Halad sa Pagtuo made the sacred roots of the secular celebrations across this archipelago that we call Cebu more pronounced. It underscores, in addition, that the festivals rooted in faith in which everyone is welcome take place both in and outside January and in fact pepper the calendar year from start to finish.

Given two developments in human history which contextualize Halad sa Pagtuo and other festivals and will continue doing so in the foreseeable future — the unbridled development of artificial intelligence and the climate emergency — organizers must seize the opportunity to make the fiesta of fiestas a model of authentic humanity in opposition to the anti-culture of artifice and of sustainability as a counterweight to the throwaway culture at the root of our ecological crises.
Examples of authentic humanity

Take these for examples of authentic humanity. A netizen who attended the festival thanked the organizers of Halad on social media for the distribution of free food to all spectators. The governor, meanwhile, thanked a water firm for donating its products to spectators.

This power of the fiesta, so to speak, to trigger the preparation of welcoming communal tables ultimately ought to compel Cebuanos to build a culture in which no one who lives on the island is hungry or without shelter or clothes. There must be a better solution than simply telling nongovernment organizations, as Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival did back in May, to put a halt to street giving.
Could each fiesta as well as Halad be new channels for addressing malnutrition in Cebu, a cause that is dear to the governor?

The generosity that a fiesta occasions is the true heart of devotion to the saints, although a procession is a rather indispensable reminder that “open hands” are not some vague principle floating in the ether but belong to flesh-and-blood men and women, representable in sculpture, who were fully immersed in history and responsive to human suffering.

The ceremonials of faith, including honoring its heroes with well-wrought floats, floral arrangements, meditative walks, choreography, music, and lights become genuine expressions only when they culminate in a consistent culture (at the risk of redundancy: culture because consistent) of helping the poor.
Care for the earth

Now it would be quite tragic if this culture of mercy and helping remains exclusively anthropocentric. We must also care for the earth from which we draw everything we need for ourselves and to help one another.
Danao City, for its carroza in honor of Saint Thomas of Villanueva, a patron of the poor, used recycled materials as decoration.

“Designer Dan Wilson Damicog said preparations took nearly two weeks, with the team choosing an eco-friendly design to save on costs while putting available materials to use,” CDN Digital’s Lyle Andales and Airam Limatog reported.
“The approach reflected the spirit of Laudato Si’, Pope Francis’ encyclical that calls for care for the environment and responsible stewardship of natural resources.”
The municipality of Tudela, for its carriage for Saint Isidore the Laborer, a farmer, used as decoration fresh produce such as watermelons, bananas, cassava, and coconuts.
More sustainable festivals
The two locales’ judicious choice of decoration represent good beginnings for Halad as a template for sustainable festivals. The next laudable steps would be checking the carbon footprint of Halad.
Sinulog has become infamous for the amount of waste it generates. How far might Halad stress the planet if it becomes bigger and better as organizers would want each year?

The cut-flower industry, which feeds into the decorations of carrozas, is a high-carbon footprint one, and more discerning traders have begun a movement for sustainable floristry. Halad must take inspiration.
Are fireworks necessary or can organizers shift to a light show? Would the budget for one be acceptable in the face of our other struggles?

For those who have pagtuo (faith), a “cloud of witnesses” (Hebrews 12:1) such as Saints Thomas of Villanueva and Isidore the Laborer remind festival goers and organizers that there is a Divine Master who deserves devotion in the needy and to whom all will have to answer for how they treat the earth, his garden.

articles.title: La Mesa Dam below overflow level, still above critical mark
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City has fallen below its overflow level but remains above the critical level, according to the state weather bureau on Sunday evening.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City has fallen below its overflow level but remains above the critical level, according to the state weather bureau on Sunday evening.

In its latest update issued at 6 p.m., the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said the dam’s water level stood at 80.11 meters as of 5 p.m., below the overflow elevation of 80.15 m but still above the critical level of 79.50 m.
The water level had slightly eased from 80.30 m recorded at 5 a.m. on Sunday.

Pagasa warned that excess floodwaters from the dam would flow directly into the Tullahan River, affecting low-lying areas in Quezon City (Fairview, Forest Hills Subdivision, Quirino Highway, Sta. Quiteria, and San Bartolome), Caloocan City, Valenzuela City (North Expressway and La Huerta Subdivision), Malabon City, and Navotas City.
It added that light to moderate rains were still expected over the watershed area for the next 12 hours.
“All residents living in the aforementioned areas, especially those residing near the riverbanks, are still advised to take appropriate actions,” the weather bureau noted.
In its separate 5 p.m. weather forecast, Pagasa said Tropical Depression Pilandok was not forecast to make landfall in the country but would enhance the southwest monsoon, or habagat.

It added that monsoon rains were forecast over Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, some parts of Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon), and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and Palawan). /mcm

articles.title: Ferry carrying over 260 people capsizes off Cyprus
articles.summary: Several people have died after a passenger ⁠boat carrying more than 260 people capsized off ‌northern Cyprus, Turkish media reported. ‌

image.caption: The ferry capsized shortly after departing from the Northern Cyprus port of KyreniaImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: A passenger ferry capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, shortly after leaving port, the local government said.
At least seven people have died, Turkish state media reported, citing Unal Ustel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC).
Ustel said that some 237 people had been rescued.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974, with the northern part under the administration of the TRNC, which is recognized internationally only by Turkey.

blocks.caption: Authorities said many of the passengers and crew members were rescuedImage: Reuters TV/REUTERS

blocks.text: Passenger boat heading from northern Cyprus to Turkey

Turkish media reported that a ferry carrying more than 260 passengers was traveling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, to the Turkish port of Tasucu in southern Mersin province, when it sank.
Erhan Arikli, the TRNC's Transport Minister, told Turkish and Cypriot media that there were 267 people on board — 259 passengers and 8 crew members.
"All necessary preparations are being made for a swift response from rescue and health services," the TRNC's Health Ministry said in a statement.
Search and rescue operations ongoing
In a post on X, Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said: "We are closely following the unfortunate incident that has occurred and providing all possible support to the search and rescue efforts."
Turkey's state-run TRT news channel reported that the ferry began taking on water 7.5 kilometers (4 nautical miles) from the coast.
